whole dark logo](https://hol.org/brand/Logo_Whole_Dark.png) | **Stop risky AI actions before they compromise your machine.** HOL Guard is a local-first security layer for AI agents, tools, plugins, skills, MCP servers, and package installs.

[Install HOL Guard](https://hol.org/guard/activate)
[Read the documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/blob/main/docs/guard/get-started.md)
[PyPI Package (`hol-guard`)](https://pypi.org/project/hol-guard/)
[Report an Issue](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/issues) | | :--- | :--- | HOL Guard reviews agent actions before they run: shell commands, file access, package installs, and MCP tool calls. It detects secret exposure, destructive operations, prompt injection, and supply-chain risks, then allows, blocks, or requests approval according to your policy. It sees only the events each agent exposes to it: the [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) lists, for each agent, the event surfaces Guard hooks and the actions it does not cover. Run it locally without an account. Use the CLI and local dashboard to manage protection, resolve approvals, and inspect decision history. Optional [Guard Cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) adds shared history, team policy, and fleet management. [Get started](#install-hol-guard) · [Supported agents](#supported-ai-agents) · [Plugin scanner](#plugin-scanner) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) · [Contribute an adapter](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md) · [Development](#development) ### Sponsors #### Gold sponsors

#### Bronze sponsors

   

Thank you to our sponsors for supporting HOL Guard. Some sponsor links are referral links.
Sponsorship does not change Guard's security decisions or coverage.

## Install HOL Guard Requires Python 3.10 or newer, [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/how-to/install-pipx.html), and a matching native runtime. Check the [platform support and Windows ARM64 setup notes](docs/guard/get-started.md#platform-support) before installing. ```bash pipx install hol-guard hol-guard init ``` The first-run wizard discovers supported agents and walks you through protection setup. It asks before each setup change, including opening the dashboard, installing agent integrations, and connecting optional cloud services. **Python recommendation:** Use Python 3.11 or newer for the `pipx` installation shown above, in line with [pipx's current installation guide](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/how-to/install-pipx.html). HOL Guard itself supports Python 3.10+, so this is a setup recommendation, not a change to the package's minimum supported Python version. Check your installation: ```bash hol-guard --version hol-guard status ``` To update an existing installation: ```bash hol-guard update ``` For manual setup, see the [installation guide](docs/guard/get-started.md). Annotated release notes with upgrade context live at [hol.org/guard/releases](https://hol.org/guard/releases); raw releases and prereleases are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/releases). ## What HOL Guard Protects | Surface | Protection | | :--- | :--- | | **Shell commands and file access** | Reviews destructive operations, sensitive file access, credential exposure, and suspicious outbound commands. | | **Package installs** | Evaluates supported package-manager operations against supply-chain intelligence before installation. | | **Plugins, skills, and agent configuration** | Inventories local artifacts and reviews new or changed tools before launch. | | **MCP servers and tools** | Inspects server configuration and reviews tool calls through supported hooks and managed proxies. | | **Prompts and tool results** | Screens supported events for prompt injection and sensitive content. | | **Approvals and evidence** | Routes decisions to native prompts or the approval center, and records local receipts for review. | Guard connects through native agent hooks, managed MCP proxies, and launch integrations. Coverage depends on the events each agent exposes; the [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) documents enforcement, approval delivery, and failure behavior per integration. ## Supported AI Agents Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Grok, Hermes, Kimi Code, Pi, oh-my-pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Antigravity, ZCode, and Devin. [Paseo](docs/guard/paseo.md) is supported through these native provider integrations, with per-provider coverage. For example, to set up Codex explicitly: ```bash hol-guard install codex hol-guard run codex --dry-run hol-guard run codex ``` The dry run records the current artifact state before launch. For Codex, Guard installs native pre-tool hooks and refuses a managed launch if those hooks are missing or disabled. [Agent support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) ## Everyday Use | Task | Command | | :--- | :--- | | Check protection status | `hol-guard status` | | Diagnose an agent integration | `hol-guard doctor codex` | | Inspect changes before launch | `hol-guard diff codex` | | Review pending approvals | `hol-guard approvals` | | Approve or deny a request | `hol-guard approvals approve ` / `hol-guard approvals deny ` | | Read decision history | `hol-guard receipts` | | List tracked artifacts | `hol-guard inventory` | | Export an AI bill of materials | `hol-guard abom --format json` | | Scan workspace dependencies | `hol-guard supply-chain scan` | | Connect optional cloud sync | `hol-guard connect` | ### Understand a paused command Inspect the command's classification and matching rules: ```bash hol-guard command test 'rm -rf ./build' hol-guard command explain 'git clean -ndx' hol-guard command extensions command.git --json ``` `command test` and `command explain` inspect the command without executing it or creating an approval. Use `hol-guard approvals` to resolve a pending request and `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. The [Extension directory](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) lists command coverage generated from the Rust-compiled catalog. External contributions require explicit opt-in; required core protections remain enabled. To add coverage, follow the [Extension contribution guide](docs/guard/extensions/contributing.md). ### Check a package ```bash hol-guard supply-chain sync hol-guard supply-chain scan hol-guard supply-chain explain minimist@1.2.5 --ecosystem npm ``` The package verdict includes the available advisory evidence and ecosystem coverage. See the [get-started guide](docs/guard/get-started.md) for package-manager interception and the [remediation guide](docs/guard/remediation.md) for handling false positives. ## Plugin Scanner This repository also ships `plugin-scanner`, a CLI for maintainers who want security and quality checks before publishing agent plugins, skills, and MCP integrations. ```bash pipx install plugin-scanner plugin-scanner scan . plugin-scanner lint . plugin-scanner verify . ``` | Command | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | `scan` | Security findings and a quality report across detected package surfaces. | | `lint` | Rule-level authoring feedback. | | `verify` | Install-surface and runtime readiness checks. | | `submit` | A submission artifact for one plugin package. | | `doctor` | Component diagnostics and troubleshooting bundles. | The scanner detects Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, and OpenCode package formats. Use `plugin-scanner --list-ecosystems` to list them or `--ecosystem` to select one. At a Codex marketplace root, it discovers local plugin entries automatically. Checks cover manifests, secrets, MCP transport and command configuration, approval defaults, skills, dependency lockfiles, and GitHub Actions permissions. Optional Cisco integrations add skill and MCP analysis. Reports support text, JSON, Markdown, and SARIF. ```bash plugin-scanner scan . --format sarif --output plugin-scanner.sarif plugin-scanner scan . --fail-on-severity high ``` Quality grades use the checks applicable to each package. Trust scoring has separate provenance and weights; see the [skill](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md), [MCP](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md), and [plugin](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) scoring references. ### Package a plugin for every runtime `hol-guard plugin` is the Plugin Kit. Point it at one plugin source, such as a Claude Code plugin, Codex plugin, Gemini CLI extension, MCP Registry `server.json` or a folder of skills, and it checks the source and writes a ready-to-load copy for each agent runtime that can use it. It runs locally, reads only the folder you name and makes no network calls. ```bash hol-guard plugin check # what marketplaces and runtime loaders would reject hol-guard plugin package # writes dist/hol-plugin// for each runtime hol-guard plugin convert --to agent-plugins # Agent Plugins 1.0 package, checked against the spec hol-guard plugin links # install commands per runtime, plus listing links hol-guard plugin card # draft .well-known plugin card as JSON hol-guard plugin init --name my-plugin # scaffold a new plugin in an empty folder ``` Runtimes: `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `cursor`, `vscode`, `opencode`, `mcp-registry`, `agent-skills` and `agent-plugins`. See [the Plugin Kit guide](docs/guard/plugin-kit.md). ### GitHub Actions Add the scanner to a plugin repository: ```yaml name: Plugin security on: [push, pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6 - uses: hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action@fdb49f9d85321a2ced2933301b395dd3c1ce9c8f # v1.2.631 with: plugin_dir: "." min_score: 80 fail_on_severity: high ``` See the [action documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action) for SARIF uploads, submission workflows, and machine-readable outputs. The action source is maintained in [`action/`](action/). ### Optional Cisco analysis The baseline packages work without Cisco dependencies. To add Cisco skill scanning, use Python 3.11 through 3.14 and install the extra in an isolated environment: ```bash pipx install 'plugin-scanner[cisco]' ``` For Cisco MCP analysis, use the repository's [Docker image](Dockerfile) or the `cisco-mcp` dependency group: ```bash uv sync --extra dev --extra cisco --group cisco-mcp --python 3.13 uv run plugin-scanner scan . --cisco-skill-scan on --cisco-mcp-scan on ``` The published `cisco` extra provides skill scanning; the separate `cisco-mcp` group supplies the MCP scanner. Dependency versions and Python constraints are maintained in [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml). ## Ecosystem Support | Ecosystem | Detection surfaces | | :--- | :--- | | Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | | Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | | DeepSeek Harness | `package.json` with `dsh.bundle`, declared patches, and Cordis `apply(ctx)` exports, or `dsh.bundle.mode` set to `"patch"` for patch-only bundles | | Gemini CLI | `gemini-extension.json`, `commands/**/*.toml` | | Kimi Code | `kimi.plugin.json`, `.kimi-plugin/plugin.json`, declared skills, agents, commands, prompts, and MCP servers | | OpenCode | `opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode/commands`, `.opencode/plugins` | Use `--ecosystem auto` to detect supported packages in a repository, or select an ecosystem explicitly: ```bash plugin-scanner scan ./plugins-repo --ecosystem claude plugin-scanner scan ./dsh-plugin --ecosystem deepseek-harness ``` ## What The Scanner Checks | Category | Coverage | | :--- | :--- | | Manifest validation | Required fields, versions, declared paths, interface metadata, links, and assets. | | Security | Hardcoded secrets, unsafe MCP commands and transports, and risky approval defaults. | | Operational security | GitHub Actions permissions and pinned dependencies, privileged checkout patterns, Dependabot, and lockfiles. | | Plugin packaging | README and license files, skill frontmatter, ignore rules, and accidentally committed environment files. | | Marketplace | Manifest validity, local package discovery, and safe source paths. | | Skill and MCP analysis | Analyzer availability, findings, and analyzability from optional Cisco integrations. | | Code quality | Dynamic code execution and shell-injection patterns. | ## How Trust Scoring Works Plugin Scanner reports a quality grade alongside trust provenance. Quality scores are normalized across applicable checks, so optional surfaces do not inflate a package's grade. Skill trust uses the HCS-28 baseline adapter IDs, weights, and denominator rules. MCP and Codex plugin trust use explicit adapters, weights, and contribution modes documented in the local specifications: - [Skill Trust Local Draft](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md) - [MCP Trust Draft](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md) - [Codex Plugin Trust Draft](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) ## CLI Usage ```bash # Structured security report plugin-scanner scan ./my-plugin --format json --profile public-marketplace # Inspect authoring rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --list-rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --explain README_MISSING # Apply supported mechanical fixes plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --fix --profile strict-security # Verify package readiness; --online permits live probes plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --format json plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --online --format text # Generate a submission artifact for one plugin plugin-scanner submit ./my-plugin --profile public-marketplace --attest dist/plugin-quality.json # Collect component diagnostics plugin-scanner doctor ./my-plugin --component mcp --bundle dist/doctor.zip ``` For a repository marketplace, `scan`, `lint`, `verify`, and `doctor` can target the root. `submit` targets one plugin package. ## Codex Spec Alignment The scanner recognizes Codex plugin manifests, interface metadata, declared assets, and marketplace packages: - Local manifest paths use `./` prefixes; `lint --fix` preserves or adds them. - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the preferred marketplace location, with root `marketplace.json` supported for compatibility. - Interface validation checks declared links and assets without requiring an undocumented `type` field. - `verify --online` checks HTTP remote reachability. Stdio server execution is skipped for manual review. See the [Codex plugin documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins) and [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) for upstream formats. ## Config + Baseline Example Configure the scanner in `.plugin-scanner.toml`: ```toml [scanner] profile = "public-marketplace" baseline_file = "baseline.txt" ignore_paths = ["tests/*", "fixtures/*"] [rules] disabled = ["README_MISSING"] severity_overrides = { CODEXIGNORE_MISSING = "low" } ``` The GitHub Action requires `trust_repository_policy: true` before repository-owned configuration and baselines can change its verdict. Enable that option only for policy you intend the workflow to trust. ## Report Formats | Format | Use | | :--- | :--- | | `text` | Terminal summaries with category totals and findings. | | `json` | Structured reports for scripts and integrations. | | `markdown` | Review-ready reports for pull requests and issues. | | `sarif` | GitHub code scanning and security automation. | ## GitHub Action The [AI Plugin Scanner Action](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action) supports security gates, SARIF uploads, submission intake, and registry payloads. Its source lives in [`action/`](action/), and the [publication workflow](.github/workflows/publish-action-repo.yml) distributes the action bundle. The legacy [HOL Codex Plugin Scanner Action](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-codex-plugin-scanner-action) remains available for existing workflows. ### Plugin Author Submission Flow Use `submission_enabled: true` to open or reuse a submission issue when a plugin meets the configured threshold. `submission_token` must have permission to create issues in the target submission repository. The action emits submission status and issue URLs as outputs. See the [action's input reference](action/action.yml) for `submission_score_threshold`, `submission_token`, and the target repository options. ### Registry Payload For Plugin Ecosystem Automation Set `registry_payload_output` to write a machine-readable payload for a registry or badge pipeline. The action also exposes `score`, `grade`, `grade_label`, `max_severity`, and `findings_total` outputs and can write a job summary. The [HOL Registry Broker plugin](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/registry-broker-codex-plugin) is an example of an agent plugin in the [HOL Plugin Registry](https://hol.org/registry/plugins). Its [registry listing](https://hol.org/registry/plugins/hol%2Fregistry-broker-codex-plugin) provides current trust information. ## Why HOL Guard AI agents can run commands, install dependencies, read files, and call external tools within one session. HOL Guard reviews those actions at supported execution points and keeps the policy decision, approval request, and receipt together. Use it for AI agent security on a developer machine, MCP security around connected tools, and supply-chain checks for packages and plugins. Teams can add Guard Cloud for shared approvals and policy management while retaining local protection. ## Frequently Asked Questions ### What is HOL Guard? HOL Guard is open-source antivirus and runtime protection for AI agents. It reviews supported tool calls, shell commands, file access, and package operations for risks such as secret exposure, prompt injection, destructive actions, and malicious dependencies. Unlike endpoint antivirus, it does not scan the whole machine: it sees only the actions a supported agent sends through its hooks, and some events fail open or are only observed. The [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) names those limits per agent. ### Does HOL Guard work without a cloud account? Yes. Local protection, CLI commands, approvals, and receipts work without signing in. Guard Cloud is optional and adds synchronized evidence, team controls, and fleet visibility. See [Local Guard vs. Guard Cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) for the feature boundary. ### Which AI agents does HOL Guard support? Guard includes adapters for Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Grok, Hermes, Kimi Code, Pi, oh-my-pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Antigravity, ZCode, and Devin. [Paseo](docs/guard/paseo.md) is supported through these native provider integrations, with per-provider coverage. The [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) explains which events and enforcement paths each adapter supports. ### What is the difference between HOL Guard and Plugin Scanner? Install `hol-guard` to protect agent activity on your machine. Install `plugin-scanner` to inspect plugin packages and enforce security and quality checks in CI. This repository builds and publishes both distributions. ### How does HOL Guard protect MCP servers? Guard inspects MCP server configuration and reviews supported MCP tool calls through agent hooks and managed proxies. Plugin Scanner checks MCP configuration and HTTP remote reachability; optional Cisco MCP analysis adds static security findings. ### Why did Guard pause my command? The action may need approval under your active policy, or its tools or artifacts may have changed. Start with `hol-guard approvals`, inspect the command with `hol-guard command explain ''`, and use `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. ## Documentation For enrollment or stale native authority errors, see [extension-control recovery](docs/guard/extension-control-recovery.md). | Guide | Contents | | :--- | :--- | | [Get started](docs/guard/get-started.md) | Installation, manual setup, package protection, and common commands. | | [Agent support](docs/guard/harness-support.md) | Integration coverage and approval behavior. | | [Architecture](docs/guard/architecture.md) | Runtime components and decision flow. | | [Policy specification](spec/guard-policy/v1alpha1/README.md) | GuardPolicy document format. | | [Policy recipes](docs/guard/policy-recipes.md) | Configuration examples for common workflows. | | [Extensions](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) | Built-in command rules and contribution guidance. | | [Native extension authoring](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md) | Canonical JSON sources, the Rust compiler, portable fixtures, and review kits. | | [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) | Generate, review, integrate, and test a new extension with the CLI. | | [Local vs. cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) | Local capabilities and optional cloud services. | | [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) | Diagnosis and recovery. | | [Security](SECURITY.md) | Vulnerability reporting and disclosure policy. | ## Contribute a New Extension To integrate a new AI coding agent or IDE, use the separate [harness adapter contribution guide](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md). Harness adapters provide discovery, managed setup, and event integration. The command extensions below add policy coverage for CLI tools and do not install agent hooks. Command extensions are authored as **declarative JSON compiled and evaluated by Rust**. Add metadata, permissions, matcher trees, and safe variants in `contributions/command-sources/command..json`, then verify behavior with portable JSON fixtures. Most extensions compose existing native operations; a new Rust operation is needed only when the existing matcher contracts cannot express the behavior. | Contribution | Authoring input | Verification | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Command coverage | `contributions/command-sources/command..json` | Portable fixtures evaluated by `guard-command-source test`. | | MCP server knowledge | `contributions/mcp-servers/.json` | MCP contribution tests and native catalog validation. | | New matcher semantics | Reviewed Rust changes in `rust/crates/guard-command/` | Native contract, admission, evaluation, and regression tests. | The Rust compiler generates command descriptors, the catalog, and the native matcher program. Python remains part of the CLI, build orchestration, and tests; new command coverage does not require a Python detector or registry registration. See the [authoring guide](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md) for direct source authoring and the [architecture](docs/guard/command-extension-architecture.md) for the runtime boundary. The **Extension Builder CLI** can create those command sources and portable fixtures from exported command metadata. It also supports MCP inventories. It works offline and reads the export without importing or running the target tool. Use the Builder's plan-and-apply flow to create the canonical source and fixture. Open a draft PR early for scope review. Before marking that PR ready for review, run `scripts/prepare_extension_contribution.py --source ... --fixture ...` to synchronize deterministic projections, then run `hol-guard extensions handoff --repo . --source ... --fixture ...`. The handoff check catches missing generated descriptors, catalog entries, and source bindings before final review. **1. Define the coverage in the PR.** Check the [Extension directory](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) and current [open pull requests](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/pulls) for existing or overlapping coverage. For a new capability, open a draft PR with the **Command extension** template and include the proposed `command.` ID, supported operations, destructive examples, safe counterparts, and upstream references. Scope review happens on the PR; a separate issue is not required. Extend an existing extension when it already owns the operation. Follow the [development setup](#development), then run the examples below from your HOL Guard checkout. `uv run --no-sync` uses that checkout's installed development version. **2. Generate a contribution kit.** This example uses the checked-in, synthetic `samplectl` inventory. For your own contribution, replace the input and metadata with your tool's export and public publisher details. ```bash uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions generate --from cli \ --input docs/guard/extension-builder/examples/cli-surface.json \ --slug samplectl --executable samplectl --name 'Sample CLI' \ --publisher community.example --publisher-name 'Example Maintainer' \ --homepage https://example.test/samplectl \ --upstream-version 1.0.0 --output samplectl-kit uv run --no-sync hol-guard extensions validate samplectl-kit ``` The output directory must be new, with an existing parent directory. A command kit includes `discovery.json`, `review.json`, `report.json`, the canonical JSON source, a portable native fixture, a generated descriptor, and a file manifest. MCP kits contain their contribution metadata and generated Python tests. Other inputs: `--from help` reads saved command help; `--from click` reads a Click `Context.to_info_dict()` export; `--from oclif` reads `oclif.manifest.json`; `--from mcp` reads a complete exported `tools/list` result; and `--from snapshot` replays `discovery.json`. The `cli` example above uses normalized `guard.cli-surface.v1` JSON. For MCP contributions, the generator uses `--launcher` and `--package` instead of `--executable`. See the [MCP kit example](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md#generate-an-mcp-kit) for a complete command and pagination requirements. **3. Review the operations and regenerate.** Read `report.json` and compare the discovered operations with the upstream implementation. Copy the review file before editing: ```bash cp samplectl-kit/review.json samplectl-review.json ``` Edit `samplectl-review.json`, keeping its discovery binding and operation IDs intact. CLI operations use `review` or `block`; the root operation stays `review`. Set `reviewed: true`

# Pushpin for DeepSeek Harness

**English** · [中文说明](#中文说明)

Pin the whole DeepSeek Harness window above other windows with a pushpin in the title bar. Version 0.1.0, MIT.

Windows works out of the box. Linux needs `wmctrl` and `xprop` on X11. macOS needs [yabai](https://github.com/koekeishiya/yabai). Where the platform cannot do it, the Host reports why and the button is not rendered.

## Features

- A pushpin button in the title bar, mounted through the `shell.overlay` slot. Host builds without that slot fall back to `conversation.session.header.utilities` (order `100`, after the shipped header buttons).
- One click keeps the DSH main window above other windows; a second click releases it. The button is highlighted in the theme's brand color while the window is pinned.
- The displayed state comes from the window manager, not from the button. After every click the plugin re-reads the real "always on top" state and reports that value back.
- The last state is remembered and re-applied when DSH starts (can be turned off with `restoreOnStart`).
- Backends are per platform: a warm PowerShell server on Windows, `wmctrl`/`xprop` on Linux, `yabai` on macOS. The Windows helper is started on demand and released after an idle timeout.
- Where the platform has no usable backend, the button is not rendered.

## How it works

DSH does not expose the Electron `BrowserWindow` to plugins, so no plugin-side `setAlwaysOnTop` exists. The plugin asks the operating system instead, through a small backend per platform. All of them read the state back after changing it, so the button can only show what the window manager accepted.

**Host half (`index.js`)** registers two exact routes on the DSH web server:

- `GET /dsh-pin/api/state` reads the current state without changing it.
- `POST /dsh-pin/api/toggle` flips it; an optional JSON body may name `"on"`, `"off"` or `"toggle"` as `action`.
- Requests whose `Origin` does not match the DSH web server's origin (when that origin is known) are rejected with `403`.

**Windows** — `scripts/pin-server.ps1` keeps one `powershell.exe` alive:

- Declares `SetWindowPos`, `GetWindowLong` and `GetForegroundWindow` from `user32.dll` once, prints `{"ready":true}`, then reads one action per line on stdin (`get`, `toggle`, `on`, `off`, `quit`) and answers with one compact JSON line on stdout.
- Prefers the DSH window currently in the foreground, falling back to the first process named `DeepSeek Harness` (or whose title contains it).
- Reads `GetWindowLong(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE) & WS_EX_TOPMOST`; to change it calls `SetWindowPos` with `HWND_TOPMOST` / `HWND_NOTOPMOST` and `SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE`, waits 25 ms and reads the flag again.

**Linux (X11)** — `scripts/pin-linux.sh` finds the window in `wmctrl -l`, reads `_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE` through `xprop`, and changes it with `wmctrl -b add,above` / `remove,above`. Missing tools report `missing-tool`.

**macOS** — `scripts/pin-macos.sh` finds the window through `yabai -m query --windows`, reads its layer, and sets it with `yabai -m window <id> --layer above` / `normal`. Without yabai there is no CLI to change window level, so it reports `missing-tool`.

**Lifecycle (Windows).** The helper starts on first use. One request is in flight at a time; a reply that takes longer than 6 seconds is treated as a timeout, the process is killed and replaced on the next request. After `idleTimeoutMs` without requests the process is released entirely. The Linux and macOS backends are short-lived commands and need no lifecycle.

**Restore.** When the plugin loads, it waits 2.5 seconds and then asks for the window to be pinned if the remembered state was pinned, retrying up to two more times if the window is not up yet. A failure is silent.

## Requirements

- A DSH build that declares `shell.overlay`; otherwise the session header's utilities slot is used.
- No npm runtime dependencies on any platform.
- **Windows:** `powershell.exe` on `PATH` (the default), permitted by system policy and security software.
- **Linux:** X11 with `wmctrl` and `xprop` installed. Wayland is not supported.
- **macOS:** [yabai](https://github.com/koekeishiya/yabai) installed and running.

## Installation

### From npm

The package is published as [`dsh-pushpin`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-pushpin). A DSH plugin is not installed globally: the bundle goes into the profile's dependency list, and `pnpm` fetches it from the registry.

### From the plugin manager

1. Open the DSH plugin manager (or the plugin marketplace, depending on your build).
2. Search for `dsh-pushpin`, install it and enable it.
3. Restart DSH if the pushpin does not appear.

### From a profile

Add the bundle to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`. Both lists must contain it; the snippet shows only the relevant fields, so keep your existing entries:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dsh-pushpin": "0.1.0"
  },
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": ["dsh-pushpin"]
    }
  }
}
```

Then run `pnpm install` from that directory and restart DSH. The version is resolved from the npm registry.

To develop against a local checkout, replace the version number with a `file:` specifier pointing at that directory.

## Usage

- Click the pushpin: the window stays above other windows and the button is highlighted. Click again to release it.
- Hover for the current action ("pin" / "unpin"). A failed click shows the reason in the tooltip and in a short bubble beside the pin that fades after two seconds.
- While a request is in flight the glyph dims. The state flips immediately and is reverted if Windows refuses.
- A pin survives a DSH restart only when the last change succeeded and `restoreOnStart` is on.
- The button is absent where the platform has no usable backend (Wayland, macOS without yabai, Linux without `wmctrl`). It is also absent if neither slot exists in the current build (a `[dsh-pin]` warning is logged to the console).

## Configuration

Optional file: `~/.dsh/dsh-pin-window.json`. It is not created automatically; the plugin only reads it.

```json
{
  "idleTimeoutMs": 120000,
  "restoreOnStart": true
}
```

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | number | `120000` | Milliseconds to keep the idle PowerShell process after the last request. `0` keeps it until DSH exits. |
| `restoreOnStart` | boolean | `true` | Re-apply the remembered pin state when DSH starts. |

Rules:

- Read once when the plugin loads. Restart DSH after editing.
- Invalid values fall back to the defaults above: a negative or non-numeric `idleTimeoutMs`, a non-boolean `restoreOnStart`, or an unreadable / malformed file.
- The remembered state lives next to the config in `dsh-pin-window.state.json` and is rewritten after every successful change. Delete it to make the next start ignore the previous state.
- Restore only re-applies a pinned state. If the last state was unpinned, nothing is forced on startup.

## Limitations

- **Exclusive fullscreen covers the window.** Some video players and games take exclusive control of the display and go above a topmost window. This is an OS rule the plugin cannot bypass. Borderless fullscreen (browser F11, most modern games) is unaffected.
- **One window only.** Exactly one window is pinned: the DSH window that is in the foreground at the moment of the press, falling back to the first DSH window when none is. Other DSH windows do not follow.
- **Platform backends are external.** Linux depends on `wmctrl` and `xprop`; macOS depends on yabai. Without them the Host reports `missing-tool` and the button is not rendered.
- **PowerShell must be allowed.** If system policy or security software blocks `powershell.exe`, the button turns red and the tooltip carries the failure reason.
- **First click after idle is slower.** The helper is started on demand, so that press pays for process start and the P/Invoke compile and takes noticeably longer than later clicks.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No button | No usable backend, or neither slot is available | Install `wmctrl`/`xprop` on Linux, yabai on macOS; check the console for `[dsh-pin]` |
| Button turns red | PowerShell blocked, window not found, or timeout | Hover the button for the message |
| Pin lost inside an app | That app uses exclusive fullscreen | System limitation; use borderless fullscreen |
| Config change ignored | Config is read at plugin load | Restart DSH |
| Pin not restored after restart | Last change failed, or `restoreOnStart` is off | Check the state file and config |

## Development

```bash
npm test        # exercises both routes against the real window, then unpins it
npm run check   # release gate: version in changelog, placeholder URL, declared files
```

The smoke test really does pin the window for a moment and puts it back at the end, so running it is safe but visible.

## License

MIT. The pushpin glyph is [Lucide](https://lucide.dev)'s `pin` icon, used under the ISC License.

# 中文说明

标题栏右上角多一颗钉子，点一下把整个 DeepSeek Harness 窗口钉在其他窗口上面，再点一下取消。Windows 开箱就能用，Linux 需要 `wmctrl` 和 `xprop`，macOS 需要 [yabai](https://github.com/koekeishiya/yabai)；平台做不了的时候按钮不显示。

## 功能

- 钉子挂在 `shell.overlay` 这一层，位置在标题栏右侧。没有这个槽位的 DSH 会退回到会话头部的 `conversation.session.header.utilities`（order `100`，排在自带按钮右侧）。
- 点一下让窗口浮到其他窗口上面，再点一下放回去。置顶时按钮亮起主题的品牌色。
- 显示的状态来自窗口管理器而不是按钮自己记的：每次点击后都重新读一遍真实状态并回报。
- 记住上次状态，DSH 启动时自动恢复（`restoreOnStart` 可以关掉）。
- 后端按平台分：Windows 用常驻 PowerShell，Linux 用 `wmctrl` / `xprop`，macOS 用 yabai。Windows 那个按需启动，闲置超时自动退出。
- 平台没有可用后端时，按钮不渲染。

## 原理

DSH 不把 Electron 的窗口对象开放给插件，插件里没有 `setAlwaysOnTop` 可用。这里的做法是直接问操作系统，每个平台一个小后端，改完都回读一遍，按钮只能显示窗口管理器认可的状态：

- Host 半边（`index.js`）在 DSH 的 web 服务上注册两条路由：`GET /dsh-pin/api/state` 只读状态，`POST /dsh-pin/api/toggle` 切换状态。来源与 DSH web 服务不一致的请求返回 403。
- **Windows**：`scripts/pin-server.ps1` 保持一个常驻 `powershell.exe`，启动时声明一次 `user32.dll` 的 `SetWindowPos`、`GetWindowLong` 和 `GetForegroundWindow`，之后按行接收 `get` / `toggle` / `on` / `off` / `quit`，每次回一行 JSON。优先钉当前在前台的那个 DSH 窗口，没有前台窗口就取第一个进程名或标题带 `DeepSeek Harness` 的。请求串行处理，单次超过 6 秒算超时，进程杀掉、下次重起；闲置超时后整个释放。
- **Linux**：`scripts/pin-linux.sh` 在 `wmctrl -l` 里找窗口，用 `xprop` 读 `_NET_WM_STATE_ABOVE`，用 `wmctrl -b add,above` / `remove,above` 改。工具缺了报 `missing-tool`。
- **macOS**：`scripts/pin-macos.sh` 通过 `yabai -m query --windows` 找窗口、读 layer，用 `yabai -m window <id> --layer above` / `normal` 改。没装 yabai 就报 `missing-tool`。
- 启动恢复：插件加载 2.5 秒后，如果上次是置顶状态就发一次 `on`，窗口还没起来时最多再重试两次，失败不提示。

## 安装

已经发到 npm：https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-pushpin 。

1. 插件管理器（或插件市场）里搜 `dsh-pushpin`，装上启用，钉子在重启 DSH 后出现。
2. 手动：编辑 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`，`dependencies` 和 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里同时加上 `dsh-pushpin`，在该目录跑 `pnpm install`，重启 DSH。版本号从 npm 官方源取。
3. 本地改了代码想直接生效，把版本号换成指向本地目录的 `file:` 写法。

## 使用

- 点钉子：窗口置顶，按钮亮起；再点取消。
- 悬停显示当前动作（窗口置顶 / 取消置顶）。失败时除了 tooltip，还会在钉子旁边冒一个两秒后消失的小气泡。
- 请求期间按钮变淡；按钮先按点击切换，Windows 拒绝时再弹回原状态。
- 重启后是否还置顶，取决于上次操作是否成功以及 `restoreOnStart` 是否打开。
- 平台没有可用后端时不显示按钮（Wayland、没装 yabai 的 macOS、缺 `wmctrl` 的 Linux）；当前 DSH 构建两个槽位都没有时也不显示，控制台会有一条 `[dsh-pin]` 警告。

## 配置

可选文件 `~/.dsh/dsh-pin-window.json`，插件不会自动创建它，只读取。

| 字段 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `idleTimeoutMs` | 数字 | `120000` | 常驻进程闲置多少毫秒后退出；`0` 表示不自动退出。 |
| `restoreOnStart` | 布尔 | `true` | DSH 启动后是否恢复上次的置顶状态。 |

- 配置在插件加载时读取一次，改完需要重启 DSH。
- 非法值回落到上面的默认值（负数或非数字的 `idleTimeoutMs`、非布尔的 `restoreOnStart`、文件读不出来或格式不对）。
- 上次状态存在同目录的 `dsh-pin-window.state.json`，每次操作成功后重写。删掉它，下次启动就不会恢复。
- 恢复只做「置顶」，上次是取消置顶状态时启动不会强行改窗口。

## 限制

- **独占全屏的程序会盖住置顶窗口**（部分播放器、游戏）。这是系统机制，插件绕不过去；浏览器 F11 那种无边框全屏不受影响。
- **只钉一个窗口**。钉的是点击那一刻在前台的那个 DSH 窗口，找不到前台窗口时退回到第一个。DSH 开多个窗口时，其他窗口不跟着置顶。
- **平台的置顶能力来自外部工具**。Linux 依赖 `wmctrl` 和 `xprop`，macOS 依赖 yabai；缺了就报 `missing-tool`，按钮不渲染。
- **Windows 上需要允许运行 PowerShell**。系统策略或安全软件拦住 `powershell.exe` 时，按钮变红，悬停能看到失败原因。
- **Windows 上闲置后第一次点击慢一些**，要先启动 PowerShell 并编译 P/Invoke，之后几次点击就快了。

## 开发

```bash
npm test        # 对着真窗口跑一遍两条路由，跑完会把窗口还原成不置顶
npm run check   # 发布前检查：版本号在不在 CHANGELOG、仓库地址是不是占位、清单里的文件齐不齐
```

冒烟测试会真的把窗口置顶一下再放回去，能看见，但不会留下改动。

## 许可证

MIT。图钉图形来自 [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) 的 `pin` 图标，ISC 许可。

# Panorama mode

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) · [Development](docs/development.md) · [Publishing](docs/publishing.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

**A live, cinematic view of AI execution inside DeepSeek Harness / Hypers Work.**

Panorama adds a button to the conversation header. Open it to follow reasoning, tool execution, task progress and replies through a particle orb, activity list and live preview. It is an independent Cordis bundle that integrates through public extension points without modifying the agent loop.

## Visual preview

![Panorama visual reference: particle orb, execution steps and progress panel](docs/images/panorama-html-reference.webp)

*Screenshot of the user-supplied HTML visual reference, not a capture of the installed plugin. Task names, file previews, percentages and ETA in this demo are illustrative; Panorama uses the actual conversation and the progress rules below. Current controls, branding and labels may differ.*

## Interactive results

Click the completed card or a recent result to replace the left orb with a flat glass reading panel. The execution panel stays visible. Replies render as Markdown headings, lists, code and tables; cards use clean text summaries. Recent results retain only the last settled reply per closed turn. Esc closes the result panel first.

Web links open only on click in a new window. Image/video references load only after selecting their resource card; video never autoplays. Local document/media references use the native Chat turn-tail's Session file-opening callback; if it is not mounted, an explicit message asks the user to return to Chat. No file URL is guessed. Results merge reply references with DSH turn-level `deliverables.presented` files. PPTX, Univer, PNG and other presented files appear with names and descriptions even when absent from the reply. Presented files are distinguished from prose references; neither implies cloud upload/publication. Embedded document previews remain future work.

## Features

- Live reasoning and response text from the current conversation.
- Tool execution rows with stable identities, completion/error states and elapsed time; nested calls are included.
- Current-turn todo progress when available; an indeterminate activity indicator otherwise.
- State-driven automatic colors: ice for idle, aurora for thinking, ember for execution/waiting/error, mint for completed turns.
- A continuous, one-direction orbit head, separate from actual task progress.
- Configurable brand name, callsign (default **AVA**), subtitle, unit, palette, motion and particle density.
- Recent replies and provider-reported token accounting.
- English/Chinese entry labels and a WebGL fallback.

## Install

The repository includes the built `client.js`; installing the bundle does not require a build script.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hypershub/dsh-panorama-mode.git
```

In your Harness conversation, ask the agent to install the cloned directory using the **Plugin Manager** tool:

```text
Install this bundle using plugin_manager:
action: install_bundle
target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-panorama-mode
```

Use the absolute clone path on your own machine. `plugin_manager` is a Harness tool, **not a shell command**. Installation applies to the current Profile. Do not manually edit Profile manifests or copy the plugin into the application installation.

The npm package identity is `@hypershub/dsh-panorama-mode`. Once version 0.1.0 is available, install with the Harness tool (not a bare npm dependency install):

```text
action: install_bundle
target: @hypershub/dsh-panorama-mode@0.1.0
```

Registry publication is separate from market listing. If the registry does not yet contain the version, use the local directory method above. The local checkout directory remains `dsh-panorama-mode`.

## Use

1. Open a conversation with content and click **Panorama** (Chinese: **全景模式**) in the top-right header utilities.
2. Use the gear button or **S** to open settings. Changes apply immediately and persist in local browser storage.
3. Use **Esc** or the close button to return to the conversation. When settings are open, Esc closes settings first; in a text field it first leaves editing.

Panorama covers the current app viewport. It does **not** request or exit browser/native fullscreen. Use the application's native window controls for fullscreen.

After changing an installed local bundle, rebuild it and reload the client window. A refreshed Host/plugin activation is not proof that an already-open client is using new JavaScript.

## Progress is not a timer simulation

The original reference demo advances predefined steps using predefined durations. Real AI execution does not know its future tool count or elapsed time, so Panorama does not fabricate a countdown.

| Situation | Display |
| --- | --- |
| A successful `todo_write` belongs to this turn | Completed items / total items, labelled **todo completion progress** |
| No current-turn plan | Observed tool count and indeterminate activity; no percentage or ETA |
| Todo list reaches 100% while AI continues | Plan is complete, but the turn stays active |
| Turn ends with `reason.kind === completed` | Completed-turn feedback |
| Approval/question is pending | Waiting state; active scan pauses |
| Abort/error/interruption | Stopped/error state, never a success delivery |

Counts reflect the **loaded Chat window**, not guaranteed full-session history. Tokens are settled provider accounting, not a live token estimate. Recent items are replies, not proof that files were uploaded or published.

## Compatibility and privacy

The API integration was inspected against the installed **DSH core 0.2.2-rc.1**. It uses public `conversation.session.header.utilities` / `shell.overlay` slots, `useChat`, `useSession`, `useProjection` and the optional Session status hook. Later core versions require rechecking their Chat and Slot APIs; universal version/platform compatibility is not claimed.

The Host owns a single authenticated, owner-only read endpoint: `GET /api/panorama-mode/config`. The plugin registers no agent tools, changes no prompts, writes no Session events and adds no external telemetry or CDN resources. Appearance settings are stored locally. Conversation snippets shown on the screen may contain private task text; take care when screen-sharing.

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
```

Node.js 22+ is used for package development; the Harness runtime must satisfy its own version requirements. React is a dev-only test dependency; the browser uses the Harness-provided React instance.

See [development and verification](docs/development.md) for source organization, replay fixtures, packaging and live acceptance checks.

## Known limitations

- The host hides header utilities for blank conversations; the button appears after content is present.
- The desktop layout is authored at 1920×1080 and scaled as a unit. Small/mobile layouts are not optimized.
- State/data testing and SSR do not validate WebGL pixels, browser transport or actual window interaction.
- Whole-Chat subscriptions and loaded-window folding are intentionally simple; very long loaded conversations may need a future incremental projection.
- Some secondary operational labels remain Chinese/code-oriented even with an English locale.
- Appearance storage is browser/origin-local, not account/cloud synchronization. The historical storage key is retained for upgrade compatibility.

## License and attribution

The plugin code is distributed under the [MIT license](LICENSE). See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for the Hypers mark, provided reference artwork/code and shader attribution limitations. Bundled brand artwork does not imply a trademark grant.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DS Headbot

Current package version: **0.4.27**. The manager shows current and latest versions for **DS Headbot**, **DS Bot**, **DeepSeek Harness**, **LiteLLM**, and **SparkDash**. Each card is deliberately quiet: one installed-version line plus buttons — an upgrade button appears only while a newer release exists (labelled **升级到 vX.Y.Z**), reads **升级中** while a detached worker runs, and disappears once the upgrade lands; check errors and gate reasons never render on the card, they stay in the audit and API data. DSH and DS Bot upgrades stay manual from the version cards; DS Bot has one button to update every instance in sequence. This manager does not upgrade DSH or DS Bot automatically. Any separate host-level update scheduler is configured independently.

Version checks call GitHub anonymously unless a token is configured (see `githubToken` under [Configuration](#configuration)); without one, the shared anonymous rate limit can make checks fail silently from the card's point of view.

DS Headbot is a **DeepSeek Harness (DSH) bundle plugin** and the **upper-level manager for ds-bot**. Install it once in a DSH `web` profile to create and manage multiple independent DSH + ds-bot runtime instances from one shared DSH installation.

The controller's DSH Web service is also shown as the protected **default instance** (normally port 3080). It uses the DSH profile and data that already exist; Headbot does not launch a second copy. The default instance can be renamed, restarted, updated, and configured for Feishu, but its port and autostart are fixed and it cannot be stopped or deleted. Restarting it briefly interrupts Headbot and its managed processes; the controller resumes management when DSH returns, and child instances with autostart enabled start again.

Each additional team receives its own DSH home, `web` profile state, ds-bot configuration, workspace, process, and loopback service port. DS Headbot provides one management page to create, start, stop, restart, delete, or update those instances while the default controller stays running. The DSH executable is shared, while team data and runtime state remain separate and outside project checkouts. Its bundled communication plugin lets bot teams exchange messages and files through a central audit module.

## Access model

All instances use plain HTTP on port 80 under one or more approved hostnames or IP addresses. The manager keeps the address used to open it when generating instance links:

| URL | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `http://<host>/` | Headbot manager |
| `http://<host>/dsh/` | Controller DSH Web UI |
| `http://<host>/dsh/manage/` | DS Headbot team manager |
| `http://<host>/teams/<team-id>/` | One team's DSH + ds-bot instance |

Headbot listens on loopback port 3180 and routes the controller and team paths. On the Agent Mac, PF forwards inbound TCP port 80 to this local ingress; DSH and team services remain on loopback. HTTP traffic is unencrypted.

## Install the DSH plugin

Install DS Headbot into the DSH Web profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:idaydayup2023/ds-headbot
```

The package declares its DSH bundle through `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json`; DSH applies this patch to register the manager plugin in the Web profile.

Set the canonical public host and any additional browser-facing host aliases in the `ds-headbot` bundle configuration. `publicHost` is used for DSH-advertised links; `publicHosts` adds accepted authorities. For example:

```yaml
publicHost: agent.lan
publicHosts:
  - agent.example.net
```

The parent DSH service environment must include `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, or set `dshCommand` to the absolute DSH executable path.

Start the controller DSH on loopback with its public path and trusted LAN authority:

```sh
dsh --profile web \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 3080 \
  --no-open \
  --public-url "http://$HEADBOT_PUBLIC_HOST/dsh/" \
  --trusted-host "$HEADBOT_PUBLIC_HOST" \
  --trusted-host agent.example.net
```

Repeat `--trusted-host` for every `publicHosts` alias. DSH treats `--public-url` as one advertised URL; each alias is admitted separately by the repeatable `--trusted-host` option. Headbot passes all configured authorities to each managed DSH process and rewrites absolute redirects to retain the browser's current authority.

The controller's printed token URL is the initial sign-in link. Open it once in a browser; after that, use `http://<host>/` or `/dsh/manage/`. The manager API uses DSH's Connection admission check, so unauthenticated or cross-origin state-changing requests are rejected. The static manager page itself contains no team data.

## Add and manage instances

Open `http://<host>/dsh/manage/`, then create a team with a lowercase identifier, display name, and unique port. The team list lets you edit its display name and port; changing a running team's port stops and restarts it on the new port while preserving its previous running state. On its first start, Headbot:

1. creates `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/teams/<id>/home` as the team's isolated DSH data home;
2. copies the controller's `settings.yaml` and stored credentials when present, removing the controller's browser-session signing grant (model settings are not copied — they are inherited live, see [Team model settings inheritance](#team-model-settings-inheritance));
3. installs `ds-bot` and any configured `teamPlugins` into that team's DSH `web` profile; and
4. launches a separate DSH process on `127.0.0.1:<team-port>` with the team's public URL and trusted host.

The **模型目录** card imports the controller's current default model (including an existing local endpoint such as `http://192.168.1.9:8888/v1`) and lets an administrator add OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as OpenRouter. The catalog is the single source every team reads. Each catalog entry preserves its declared `input` modalities (for example `input: [text, image]` for vision models) — through the stored catalog, through the load-side validator, and into the generated provider entries, so a model the gateway can actually see is not refused by a missing declaration. Each model entry has a unique DSH provider ID, endpoint URL, model ID, display name, and optional API key. OpenRouter uses `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`; see the [OpenRouter developer guide](https://openrouter.ai/developers) for its OpenAI-compatible API details.

Use **编辑** on an instance to assign a model to every Bot in that instance. Saving the choice updates the instance's DSH default and each existing Bot's model reference, then restarts that DSH process so ds-bot applies the selection to each Bot's persisted Session. A running child team restarts by itself; a stopped team uses the new model the next time it starts. Changing the protected default instance's model briefly disconnects the manager and restarts auto-start teams. On macOS, Headbot stops the controller LaunchAgent, waits for DS Bot to release its state lock, updates the Bot model references, and bootstraps the LaunchAgent again; this prevents the running DS Bot process from overwriting the change. The default instance must use the LaunchAgent named by `launchdLabel` (default `com.deepseek.dsh`); set `launchdPlist` if its plist is outside `~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist`. New teams inherit the default instance's model choice.

Model API keys are stored separately in `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/model-secrets.json` with owner-only permissions and are never returned by the management API. A child process receives only the selected model's key. For the default instance, Headbot keeps the selected key in a marked block in `<DSH_HOME>/.env`; its DSH launcher must source this file before starting DSH. Headbot preserves other `.env` lines and redacts model keys from captured DSH errors and logs. Teams still run under the same macOS account, so this is credential separation between instances rather than an operating-system security boundary.

Sessions, ds-bot configuration, installed profile packages, logs, and later edits stay in each team's directory. Data remains after stopping or removing this bundle. Nothing is written into a project checkout.

### Protected default instance

The first card is the controller already running in the DSH Web profile, usually on port 3080. Its display name and model assignment are stored in `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/controller.json`; it is not a child entry in `teams.json`. Headbot fixes its port to the controller's actual DSH Web port and forces autostart on. The page hides stop, port-edit, and delete controls, and the management API rejects those operations as well. The card still offers name and model editing, restart, and Feishu settings. DS Bot updates are managed from the shared DS Bot version card.

Restarting the default instance restarts the DSH LaunchAgent (`com.deepseek.dsh` by default), so the management page and its child processes disconnect briefly. When DSH starts again, Headbot resumes and starts child teams whose own autostart option is enabled. Custom service managers should set `restartCommand` and `restartArgs` as described below.

Use `teamPlugins` for required environment plugins, such as a locally maintained network fetch fix: `teamPlugins: ["/absolute/path/network-fix.tgz"]`. These packages are installed when provisioning a new instance. Controller plugins and bot state are not copied wholesale. Later changes to this list do not automatically alter already provisioned teams; install the needed package into their Web profiles during a maintenance window.

### Per-team Feishu bot

Select **编辑** on a team to configure a Feishu App ID, App Secret, and the DS Bot that should receive its messages. Choose exactly one of **启用飞书** and **关闭飞书**; deleting a saved App Secret is a separate action. Each enabled team must use its own Feishu App ID. Headbot installs the bundled `ds-headbot-feishu` plugin into that team's isolated DSH Web profile and connects through Feishu WebSocket. The bridge reuses the selected Bot's native DSH session, so the Bot keeps its identity, model, memory, tools, and team configuration. The Chat transcript shows a readable `飞书消息 · 发送人` label and the original message text; routing metadata (chat, message, sender IDs, and reply route) is delivered as hidden DSH context for the model. Messages targeting the same Bot session are processed serially across chats, and the Bot's normal response is sent as a reply to the exact Feishu message that prompted it. The team card shows the Feishu connection and Bot session states without exposing the App ID or Bot ID. Feishu does not need an inbound public callback URL or a new service port. The Agent Mac needs outbound access to Feishu.

Create and publish a Feishu self-built app with the bot capability, subscribe to `im.message.receive_v1`, and grant message receive and bot-send permissions. Enter its `cli_...` App ID and App Secret in the team editor, then choose a Bot from that team's saved DS Bot list. When the team is running, saving a changed Feishu configuration stops and restarts that team to load the new binding. The bridge sends Feishu messages to the selected Bot's current DSH session and replies to the originating Feishu chat. If DS Bot moves to a new session after a long conversation, Headbot detects the change and restarts that team to refresh the binding.

App Secrets are stored in `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/feishu-secrets.json` with owner-only permissions. The management API only returns whether a secret is stored; it never returns the value. Generated DSH patches contain only environment-variable references, and the secret is passed to the configured team's DSH process. The default instance also has a marked block in `<DSH_HOME>/.env` so the DSH LaunchAgent can load its Feishu credentials on startup; its launcher must source this file before starting DSH. Headbot preserves other `.env` lines. Removing a team removes its saved Feishu secret. This protects the value from project files and other macOS accounts, but teams run under the same macOS user and are not separate operating-system security boundaries; same-account processes and DSH tools may access account-owned data. Only enable Feishu for trusted teams. Feishu messages run with the selected Bot's DSH permissions; group messages require an @mention.

See the [bundled plugin documentation](plugins/ds-headbot-feishu/README.md) and the [Feishu bot overview](https://open.feishu.cn/document/client-docs/bot-v3/bot-overview) for app setup details. The plugin source is kept in `plugins/ds-headbot-feishu/` and carries the upstream MIT license and attribution. It is maintained by the Headbot project and is not an official DeepSeek Harness plugin.

Use the manager to start, stop, or restart a team. The DS Bot version card checks the registry and offers one **全部更新到 vX.Y.Z** button that updates each instance sequentially, restarting it after the update; the protected default instance is updated last because it restarts the controller. Starting or restarting a team uses its currently installed DS Bot version and never performs an implicit update. DSH version checks use the latest published GitHub release, including alpha, beta, and release-candidate versions. Its manual upgrade button passes that dynamically discovered version to the installation's backup-and-rollback update script. The management page stays open during that restart, retries status checks while DSH reconnects, and shows the confirmed installed version after completion. The update script must honor `HEADBOT_DSH_TARGET_VERSION` and the `HEADBOT_DSH_WEB_UPGRADE=1` marker for user-triggered upgrades while retaining its active-connection guard for background runs; see [DSH runtime upgrade behavior](docs/dsh-runtime-upgrade.md). Teams with auto-start enabled resume when the controller DSH starts; version checks never trigger upgrades.

The **DS Headbot 版本** card checks the latest stable release from GitHub. When a newer version is available, **升级到 vX.Y.Z** becomes active. The updater downloads the tagged repository source, verifies that its package version matches the release tag, packs it locally, updates the controller's `web` profile, and keeps the prior package as a rollback artifact under the DSH user's Headbot data directory. On macOS it restarts the configured LaunchAgent (`com.deepseek.dsh` by default) so the new plugin is loaded. Other service managers can set `restartCommand` and `restartArgs` in the `ds-headbot` plugin config. Team workspaces and audit data remain in place. See [self-update and rollback](docs/self-update.md) for details.

The **LiteLLM** card reports the version installed in the managed virtualenv (under `~/ai/litellm/venv` by default) against the latest upstream LiteLLM release. The upgrade button hands the work to a detached worker so the request path never blocks on pip: a configuration patch gate must read green before anything is installed, the install runs through the managed Python environment with a `uv` fallback, the launchd gateway is restarted and re-probed, and the previous pinned version is restored if verification fails. Gate detail and failure reasons are visible only through the management API and the audit journal.

The **SparkDash** card tracks the local SparkDash checkout against its upstream repository. SparkDash publishes no GitHub releases, so the installed version is the tag that names the checked-out commit (for example `v2.90.0`), with the current commit shown as the honest fallback when the checkout sits on an untagged commit. An upgrade follows the repository runbook (fetch, check out the target commit, reinstall, restart), re-checks the dirty-worktree gate immediately before touching anything, and rolls the checkout back to the previous commit when any step fails; every outcome is audited.

Deleting an instance stops its process, cancels automatic restarts, revokes its communication credential, removes its active definition, and moves its files to `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/archives/<team-id>-<instance-id>-<time>/`. The archive includes an owner-only `instance.json` definition for recovery. Runtime logs are retained under `logs/<team-id>-<instance-id>.log`. The UI requests confirmation and preserves the data. Recreating the same team ID creates a new identity and an empty inbox. Historical communication and attachment copies remain available to the controller's audit reviewer. For recovery, stop the controller, back up its data, restore the archived directory to `teams/<id>`, and restore its `instance.json` team entry to schema 2 `teams.json`, checking ID and port conflicts before restarting.

### Team model settings inheritance

Teams do not keep a frozen copy of the model configuration. On provisioning and before every start the manager links `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/teams/<id>/home/cordis.patch.yml` onto the controller's Web profile patch, so the team resolves model definitions live through DSH's home-level user-patch layer: parent edits — new providers, `input` modalities, context windows — are visible on the next team start with no re-provisioning, and drift is physically impossible. A full copy found under the team's `profiles/web` layer (the pre-0.4.25 shape) is retired to `cordis.patch.yml.model-inherited-<timestamp>.bak` rather than silently deleted. The team's own model choice, set with **编辑**, is written to `teams/<id>/model-selection.patch.yml` — only an `agent-default-model` entry — and passed as an added `--patch` after the communications patch, so it outranks the selection carried by the parent. A hand-written `teams/<id>/model-override.patch.yml` is passed after it and outranks everything; Headbot never generates or reclaims that file. A hand-written regular `home/cordis.patch.yml` is honoured as an explicit local override and never replaced by the inherited link.

### Observability lines reach server.log

Every `[ds-headbot] …` line the manager and its updaters emit is passed through to the host logger and also printed to stdout/stderr, which the service manager captures (on macOS the LaunchAgent redirects both streams into the DeepSeekHarness log directory, `server.log`). The Cordis logger inside the DSH host has no on-disk exporter of its own — its built-in sink is an in-memory diagnostic ring — so printing is what makes lifecycle events visible on disk, including `adopted the still-serving <team> runtime (pid …)` after a controller restart and the best-effort failure clues from every module.

## Team communication and audit

Every managed instance loads the `ds-headbot-communications` DSH tool plugin through a generated patch. The patch references the controller's installed package, so no extra DSH installation or nested Headbot controller is needed. Restart instances after upgrading Headbot to load the new plugin code. DSH launches from `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/teams/<id>/workspace`, while DS Bot uses `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/teams/<id>/home/bot/workspace`. File-send paths resolve relative to the DS Bot workspace first, then the earlier Headbot workspace; absolute paths are accepted only inside one of those two directories. Downloads go to the DS Bot workspace's `inbox`. DSH settings and credentials remain in the sibling `home` directory.

| Bot tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `headbot_list_teams` | Discover recipient IDs and their current status |
| `headbot_send_message` | Send text and files from the DS Bot workspace, with compatibility for the earlier Headbot workspace |
| `headbot_receive_messages` | Read the durable inbox using a replay cursor |
| `headbot_download_attachment` | Verify and save a received file under the DS Bot workspace's `inbox` |

Messages are available immediately after durable audit storage, including when the receiving team is stopped. The receiving bot reads them with its inbox tool. When the recipient is online, an inbox push additionally wakes its lead Bot session at once — the session defaults to the first main bot recorded in the instance, or the team's explicit `pushSessionId` when set — using a single 3-second request against the instance's launch URL; a failed push is only an audit event, because the journal remains the single source of truth and the recipient's own polling still collects the message. Each instance gets a random credential; the broker derives the sender from it, and team credentials cannot access instance management or the controller's audit API.

The manager page includes **团队通信审计**. Reviewers can filter by team, read full message text, download the exact archived attachment bytes, inspect SHA-256 values, and export the complete audit archive. Send, inbox read, attachment receipt, and reviewer download events are retained. An audit write failure blocks the corresponding transfer. The journal uses a hash chain and a checkpoint, and every read or write verifies them; attachment bytes are also verified before delivery.

The protocol and HTTP contract are documented in [Team communication protocol](docs/communication-protocol.md). Defaults: 64 KiB of text, 8 attachments, 10 MiB per file, and 20 MiB of files per transfer. `communicationLimits` may lower these bounds.

Audit files live under `<DSH_HOME>/headbot/communications/`, outside the plugin package and project checkouts. The journal is segmented so it can run for years without becoming one unbounded file: the active segment is `communications/audit.jsonl`, and once it reaches `journalRotateBytes` (default 8 MiB, ceiling 512 MiB, settable in `communicationLimits`) it is **sealed** and later appends move to `communications/audit.000001.jsonl`, `audit.000002.jsonl`, and so on. A sealed segment is never rewritten or deleted, and `communications/checkpoint.json` records the tip `seq`, `hash`, and `segment`, so every read verifies the whole chain across segments. While a message is still undelivered its segment stays active — rotation defers until delivery drains, which keeps replay offsets valid.

Back up **by segment**, not by wiping the directory: copy `teams.json`, `feishu-secrets.json` (if present), every `communications/audit*.jsonl`, `communications/checkpoint.json`, and `communications/objects/` together into one consistent snapshot. Because sealed segments are immutable, an incremental backup only needs the new segments plus the current checkpoint. Treat the Feishu credential file like a password vault. The API has no audit deletion operation. If integrity verification fails, preserve the files and investigate or restore a consistent backup before resuming transfers; deleting the journal to clear the error destroys the audit history.

## Configuration

The bundle defaults to controller path `dsh`, team path `teams`, ingress port `3180`, and package `ds-bot`. The public hostname/IP comes from `publicHost` or `HEADBOT_PUBLIC_HOST`; set `dshCommand` or `HEADBOT_DSH_COMMAND` if the controller service's `PATH` does not include DSH.

If changing the bundle's `config` in a Cordis patch, restate every field because a matching patch replaces the whole config object:

```yaml
- id: ds-headbot
  config:
    publicHost: agent.lan
    publicHosts:
      - agent.example.net
    ingressPort: 3180
    controllerPath: dsh
    teamsPath: teams
    dshCommand: dsh
    botPackage: ds-bot
    inheritModelSettings: true
    teamPlugins: []
    githubToken: <token>
    communicationLimits:
      journalRotateBytes: 8388608
```

An optional `dshHome` setting can point Headbot at a non-default controller DSH home. Team data remains under `<dshHome>/headbot/`.

`githubToken` authenticates the GitHub latest-version checks of the DS Headbot, DeepSeek Harness, and LiteLLM cards (SparkDash tracks its repository over `git`, which needs no token), so they no longer share the anonymous rate limit that can otherwise make checks fail and hide the upgrade button. Equivalent environment fallbacks, read in this order and honoured only when `githubToken` is unset: `HEADBOT_UPGRADE_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` (DS Headbot card), `DSH_UPGRADE_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` (DeepSeek Harness card), `LITELLM_UPGRADE_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` (LiteLLM card). The token value belongs in the patch config or the controller service environment only — never in code, logs, or the audit journal.

`communicationLimits` tunes the communication broker: `textBytes`, `attachments`, `attachmentBytes`, `transferBytes`, and `journalRotateBytes` (audit segment size, default 8 MiB, ceiling 512 MiB; see [Team communication and audit](#team-communication-and-audit)).

Keep team ports distinct from the controller port, ingress port, 80, and 443. Headbot validates team IDs and ports, stores definitions in `teams.json` with owner-only permissions, and refuses duplicate or reserved ports.

## Rollback

To roll back the bundle, stop the controller DSH and remove or disable `ds-headbot` from the Web profile. Restore the previous Headbot package, DSH launch arguments, PF rules, and saved system configuration from the maintenance backup. Team state lives under `$DSH_HOME/headbot/`; removing the bundle does not delete it. Reinstalling the bundle restores the manager definitions and can restart enabled teams.

Version 0.2 upgrades `teams.json` to schema 2 and saves the original schema 1 file as `teams.v1.backup.json`. Version 0.1 refuses schema 2 instead of silently discarding communication identities. Before reverting to 0.1, stop the controller and preserve a complete schema 2 data snapshot; restore the pre-upgrade snapshot for the old version. Keep the schema 2 snapshot for upgrading again, because it contains the identities associated with subsequent audit history. Do not mix `teams.json` from one snapshot with another snapshot's communication archive.

## Scope and deployment status

- DS Headbot is a DSH Web profile plugin and the management layer for multiple DSH + ds-bot instances.
- Team DSH homes are separate directories but run as the same macOS user; they are not an OS-level security boundary.
- All exchanges made through the communication plugin pass through the audit module. A same-user process with unrestricted filesystem or network tools can still use other channels; enforcing auditing against those channels requires additional OS/container isolation. The local hash chain detects corruption and changes against its checkpoint, but an administrator who can rewrite both files is outside this trust boundary.
- The public manager uses HTTP on port 80; session traffic is unencrypted.
- This release targets the DSH `web` profile and its `--public-url` prefix-stripping deployment contract.
- Two real DSH + ds-bot instances were verified in an isolated Agent-Mac home, including path login, client assets, lifecycle, communication tools and audit exports. Production HTTP acceptance is recorded separately on the host.

In a source checkout, run `npm install --ignore-scripts` and `npm test` for the lifecycle, HTTP admission, tool communication, attachment, migration, and audit fault checks. These checks use a simulated DSH process and do not call a model.

To check a future DSH upgrade, run `node scripts/verify-installed-dsh.mjs /path/to/dsh-installation`. This loads the installed Cordis and DSH tool registry in an isolated process and verifies registration of all four communication tools, without modifying an existing profile or calling a model. See [verification record](docs/verification-2026-10-17.md) for the current results.

For an authorized live lifecycle check, run `node scripts/verify-live-headbot.mjs /path/to/config.json` on the controller host. The configuration names `home`, `log` (controller startup log), `installation`, `ingressPort`, `controllerPort`, `publicHost` and optional `output`/`expectedTeamPlugins`. It authenticates with the current launch URL internally, creates two uniquely named temporary teams, checks their pages and tools, then deletes only those definitions. Their archived files and audit records remain for inspection. It never prints credentials or calls a model. Verify the public HTTP entry and browser separately.
