# @kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Cursor SDK agent adapter for the DeepSeek Harness LLM seam: one Cursor agent run per harness model call, backed by [`@cursor/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cursor/sdk) (pinned to `1.0.23`, the version the reference Pi extension was built against). The Cursor agent loop executes its own tools inside the SDK, so the harness sees reasoning, text, and usage only — the turn ends when the agent finishes. Session continuity rides the seam's replayState: a successful finish stores the Cursor agent id, and the next ordinary conversation request resumes that agent with only the new user message, so the Cursor agent's own conversation survives across harness turns and process restarts (the local store persists under `stateRoot`).

The package root exposes the Cordis plugin contract and `CursorAdapter`; prompt flattening, SDK message translation, and error mapping are separate modules.

## Install

From the harness checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/plugins/dsh-llm-cursor
```

The bundle's patch layer inserts the `llm-cursor` row, which registers the `cursor` provider route on the harness LLM seam. Restart the harness, store a Cursor SDK API key through the credentials service (the web Models page writes it) or export `CURSOR_API_KEY`, and select a `cursor/*` model.

## Config

```yaml
- id: llm-cursor
  name: '@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor'
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: CURSOR_API_KEY  # default; resolved per request via ctx.credentials, then the environment
    runtime: local            # optional; local (default) or cloud
    cwd: /path/to/workspace   # optional; local agents run their tools here (default: process.cwd())
    stateRoot: ~/.dsh/cursor  # optional; local agent store root (default: $DSH_HOME/cursor)
    mode: agent               # optional; agent (default) or plan
    models:                   # optional; advisory catalog, defaults to `default` and `composer-2.5`
      - id: default
        name: Default
        contextWindow: 128000
    defaultContextWindow: 128000 # optional positive-integer fallback; this is the default
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000  # optional; positive finite Node timer delay; five-minute default
    retryPolicy:             # optional; omission uses bounded normal defaults
      mode: normal
      maxRetries: 3
    params:                  # optional; extra model parameters merged into every ModelSelection
      - id: thinking
        value: 'true'
```

The plugin registers the single provider route `cursor`. A request selects it with `provider: cursor`; its `model` is passed through as the Cursor model id, so changing Cursor models does not require lifecycle-time registration. Omitting `models` advertises `default` and `composer-2.5`, each with the route's `defaultContextWindow`; an explicit list replaces those defaults, while `models: []` advertises none. Catalog entries are exposed through `ctx.llm.listModels('cursor')` for clients such as ACP editors and the Web selector, but remain advisory: unlisted model ids still pass through unchanged.

Models whose Cursor SDK catalog exposes a `fast` parameter (Grok, Composer, Opus 5/4.8/4.7, and the GPT-5.x family) are additionally advertised as `:fast` and `:slow` id variants — e.g. `grok-4.6`, `grok-4.6:fast`, `grok-4.6:slow` — so the model selector can pick the fast path per model. The adapter strips the suffix before calling the SDK and injects the `fast` parameter (`true` for `:fast`, `false` for `:slow`), which wins over a configured `params` entry with the same id; a suffix on a model without the `fast` parameter is ignored. The plain id keeps the SDK's default variant.

`runtime: cloud` runs the Cursor Cloud agent instead of the local SDK loop; the local store and `cwd` are then unused. `params` entries are merged into every `ModelSelection` (the SDK's model-parameter vocabulary, e.g. `thinking: true`). Reasoning efforts are exposed through the harness reasoning-effort seam; the adapter offers the SDK catalog's effort vocabulary (`effort` for Grok/Claude models, `reasoning` for GLM/GPT models) so the model selector can pick an effort per model.

`streamIdleTimeoutMs` bounds each outstanding provider read without counting time the consumer spends between chunks. The adapter makes exactly one Cursor agent run per `stream()` call; it registers the configured policy as provider metadata, and `dsh-llm-retry` separately executes it at durable agent-step boundaries.

## Dynamic configuration (settings + credentials)

Connection facts are not frozen at load. `resolveAdapterOptions` is the one explicit resolve step from raw config to validated facts, and the adapter re-reads them through a thunk **once per operation**: runtime, cwd, state root, catalog, and idle budget all take effect on the next request, while an in-flight stream keeps the facts it started with. Two optional seams feed that thunk:

- **`ctx.settings`** — the plugin registers the `llm-cursor` namespace with this same `Config` schema and its `cordis.yml` entry as the composition `base`, so a `llm-cursor:` section in the user settings document overrides any field without a restart. Without a mounted settings service the entry config alone drives the adapter, unchanged. A live settings snapshot that passes the schema but fails a beyond-schema bound (an empty state root, a duplicate catalog id) keeps the last good facts and logs the failure; the entry config itself still fails plugin load.
- **`ctx.credentials`** — the API key resolves per stream call, from the *same* resolved snapshot that supplies the connection facts. Configuration carries only `apiKeyEnv`, never a literal key: the reference resolves through the credential seam, and without a mounted seam through the trusted environment layers. Every resolved key is format-checked before use, so a value no HTTP header can carry is refused with `LlmError('INVALID_CREDENTIAL')` naming the failing entry point — never any part of the key. A request with no key anywhere fails with `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` naming every configuration entry point, while the route stays registered and the catalog stays browsable.

The one registration-captured fact is the retry policy: when its resolved value changes, the plugin re-registers the route in place (same adapter instance, one synchronous section), so `ctx.llm.providerRetryPolicy('cursor')` always reports the current policy.

The plugin also declares its route in the configurable-provider directory (`ctx.llm.listConfigurableProviders()`): provider `cursor`, settings namespace `llm-cursor`, empty settings path — the whole section is the profile.

## Model discovery

The plugin offers `ctx.llm.registerModelDiscovery('llm-cursor', …)`, which answers "which models can this provider serve?" for a route a configuration surface is editing or drafting. A draft naming the `cursor` route is answered from the **live Cursor SDK catalog** (`Cursor.models.list()`, the pi-cursor-sdk `/cursor-refresh-models` equivalent) whenever a credential is available — the key typed in the draft, else the route's stored key. The reply is candidates the surface offers for adoption, never a stored catalog. Without any credential the draft is answered from the configured catalog, with no network call. Every other draft — a base URL, a foreign route — is refused with `DISCOVERY_UNSUPPORTED`, because Cursor models come from the Cursor SDK, never from an endpoint this adapter can interrogate.

## Provider/model routing and replay

Each resolution produces one **immutable** snapshot of the connection facts, captured before the first `await` of the operation. A configuration change therefore reaches the next request, never the one in flight.

A successful finish emits `finish.replayState` carrying the Cursor agent id inside the seam's `ReplayEnvelope` (`{ response: { kind: 'cursor', version: 1, agentId } }`; no per-block metadata, so `blocks` is omitted and the envelope passes through assembly unchanged). On the next request, the adapter reads the replay state of the latest model-produced assistant message, validates it, and — for ordinary conversation requests only — resumes that agent (`Agent.resume`) and sends only the latest user message, because the agent already holds the conversation. Auxiliary calls (`purpose: compaction` or `session-title`) always run on a fresh agent with the flattened history, so a summarization or title call can never pollute the conversation of a resumed agent. Malformed replay state fails with `LlmError('INVALID_REPLAY_STATE')` before any SDK interaction; a resumed agent that no longer exists (a cleared store) fails loud as `INVALID_REQUEST` rather than silently starting over.

## Vocabulary differences

- The Cursor agent loop executes its own tools inside the SDK, so `tool_call` messages and assistant `tool_use` blocks are **not** replayed as harness tool-call blocks: the harness would execute them a second time. The harness sees reasoning, text, and usage; the agent's internal tool activity is opaque, exactly like a subagent's.
- A fresh agent receives the flattened harness conversation as one prompt: the system prompt, then each message rendered as `User:`/`Assistant:` text with tool calls and results as a transcript. Reasoning blocks are model-internal and never rendered.
- `GenerateOptions.stop`, `temperature`, and `maxTokens` are rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_OPTION`: the Cursor SDK `send` takes a prompt, a model selection, and a mode, and has no wire equivalent for sampling knobs or stop sequences. The agent loop sends none of these by default, so the rejection only fires for explicit configuration.
- `reasoningEffort` maps to the model's effort parameter: the adapter exposes the SDK catalog's effort vocabulary (`effort` for Grok/Claude models, `reasoning` for GLM/GPT models) as harness reasoning efforts, so the model selector offers effort levels per model. The selected effort becomes the model parameter (e.g. `effort: high`), replacing a configured `params` entry with the same id; models without a vocabulary keep the SDK's default variant.
- The `fast`/`slow` choice is a model id suffix, not a mode: the SDK's `mode` is only `agent`/`plan`, and `fast` is a model parameter (`true`/`false`). Select `grok-4.6:fast` or `grok-4.6:slow` to pin it per model; the suffix is stripped before the SDK call and the `fast` param is injected into the `ModelSelection`.
- SDK error classes map to stable harness codes: `AuthenticationError` → `AUTH`, `RateLimitError` → `RATE_LIMIT`, `NetworkError` → `SERVER`, `AgentBusyError`/`UnknownAgentError`/`ConfigurationError` → `INVALID_REQUEST`, generic retryable SDK errors → `SERVER`, everything else → `TRANSPORT`. A failed run ends the stream with an error finish carrying the run's own error code and message.
- Caller cancellation cancels the SDK run and throws `ABORTED`; the configured stream-idle budget cancels the run and throws `TIMEOUT`.

## App attribution

Every provider HTTP request must carry the shared attribution header from dsh-llm's `attributionHeaders()`. `@cursor/sdk` 1.0.23 exposes no header hook (`CursorRequestOptions` carries only the API key), so this adapter cannot inject the harness attribution header into the SDK's transport; the SDK sends its own User-Agent. This is a documented deviation from the adapter contract, tracked under Known Limitations.

## Dependency weight

`@cursor/sdk` is pinned exactly (not ranged) because the SDK ships platform-specific optional binaries; the pin matches the version the reference Pi extension was built and tested against. The SDK is loaded through a dynamic `import()` per stream call, so its dependency weight stays out of plugin startup. The local runtime uses the SDK's `JsonlLocalAgentStore` (JSONL files under `stateRoot`), which needs no native `sqlite3` module.

## Model Experience

### Cursor agent request

#### What the model sees

The Cursor agent receives the flattened harness conversation as one user message (system prompt plus history for a fresh agent, the latest user message for a resumed one). This package adds no prompt prose beyond the `System instructions:` / `User:` / `Assistant:` framing of the flattened history.

#### Token effect

Provider tokenization governs exact input. Flattening adds the role framing lines; reasoning blocks are dropped rather than re-sent. A resumed agent sends only the new user message, so its input is minimal.

#### KV Cache effect

The Cursor agent's own conversation is the cache domain: a resumed agent reuses its stored context, while a fresh agent starts from the flattened history. Changing the agent (a cleared store, a new `stateRoot`) starts a new domain.

### Cursor agent response

#### What the model sees

SDK thinking messages become harness reasoning blocks, assistant text becomes text blocks, and usage messages become usage chunks. Tool activity inside the agent loop is not surfaced.

#### Token effect

Generated content affects later inputs only after the loop records it. The SDK's per-turn usage is reported when available; a run that reports none yields zero usage.

#### KV Cache effect

Recorded response content appends to the next request through the resumed agent's own conversation and does not invalidate its earlier reusable prefix. Unrecorded transport metadata and usage accounting do not affect cache identity.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **Attribution headers are not injectable** — `@cursor/sdk` 1.0.23 exposes no header hook, so the mandatory harness attribution header cannot reach the SDK's transport; the SDK sends its own User-Agent. A future SDK header hook or a transport-level fork would close this.
- **The harness never executes tools during a Cursor turn** — the Cursor agent loop runs its own tools inside the SDK, and the harness's tool schemas are not sent. Bridging harness tools into the Cursor agent (the Pi extension's MCP-bridge pattern) is deferred.
- **A resumed agent's conversation can diverge from the harness history** — compaction and session-title calls run on fresh agents, but a compacted harness history is not replayed into a resumed agent; the agent keeps its own (longer) context.
- **A cleared store breaks session continuity loudly** — a resumed agent that no longer exists fails with `INVALID_REQUEST` instead of silently starting over; there is no fallback to a fresh agent.
- **Effort vocabularies are a static snapshot** — the reasoning efforts the selector offers come from a built-in table mirroring the SDK catalog (`effort` for Grok/Claude models, `reasoning` for GLM/GPT models), not a live fetch; a model the table does not know exposes no efforts and keeps the SDK's default variant.
- **`GenerateOptions.stop`, `temperature`, and `maxTokens` are unsupported** — the Cursor SDK has no wire equivalent; explicit configuration fails with `UNSUPPORTED_OPTION`.
- **Discovery offers, it does not store** — the live catalog is fetched on demand for the Models page, but nothing writes the fetched list into `settings.yaml`; adopting candidates is the configuration surface's job, and the advisory catalog remains whatever the settings document says.
- **Cloud runs are untested against the harness** — the `runtime: cloud` path is implemented against the SDK's option shape but has no real-API coverage in this package's e2e suite.

# deepseek-harness-plugins

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

Unofficial plugins, local forks, presets, skills, and maintenance tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This is a source collection, not a single installable plugin or a distribution of DSH.

## Contents

- [Repository structure](#repository-structure)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Plugins and presets](#plugins-and-presets)
- [Skills](#skills)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Development](#development)
- [Repository scope and ownership](#repository-scope-and-ownership)
- [License](#license)

## Repository structure

Each directory below is a source collection, not a deployment inventory. Cloning the repository installs and enables nothing.

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [plugins/](plugins/) | Plugin sources, local forks, and retained reference implementations, one directory per component. [plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) keeps its nested package layout. |
| [presets/](presets/) | Agent-preset declarations: a manifest and a Cordis patch per preset. Declaring a preset does not install the packages its rows name. |
| [configs/](configs/) | Configuration-only bundles and service configuration, with no runtime code. See [its README](configs/README.md). |
| [skills/](skills/) | Authored skills and upstream-derived copies, one directory per skill. |
| [bin/](bin/) | Maintainer scripts that build, pack, and check packages, the weekly maintenance helpers, and the [runtime placement](bin/runtime-placement.md) notes. Not a public CLI. |
| [scripts/](scripts/) | The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs). |
| [tests/](tests/) | Vitest configuration and upgrade regression specs that are not package-local. |
| [tasks/](tasks/) | Change cards for the kstack card-flow, one file per card, each tied to one issue. See [its README](tasks/README.md). |
| [docs/](docs/) | [Layout migration](docs/layout-migration.md) and [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) notes, and the retained [implement-task flow diagram](docs/implement-task-flow.html). |
| [.agents/](.agents/) | Development notes and the harness-facing skills for working on this repository. |
| [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/) | Project-local skills loaded by Claude Code when working in this repository. Currently contains [verify-dsh-plugins](.claude/skills/verify-dsh-plugins/SKILL.md), which starts a disposable DSH host with a chosen plugin and mock LLM to verify the web UI and headless CLI with screenshots and logs. Machine-specific settings live in `.env` (described by `.env.example`). |

Root documents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the agent entry point ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) links to it); [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the development flow; [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes runtime layering and verification limits; [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) with [core-exceptions.json](core-exceptions.json) defines the Core baseline.

A local working copy also holds ignored directories such as `reports/`, `releases/`, and `local-design/`. They contain private material and are not part of the published tree.

**Layout migration:** Existing installations, profiles, systemd units, and scripts may still refer to old root-level paths. Moving this repository's sources does not update them; inventory and migrate those references before replacing an active checkout. The retained Slack worker configuration contains machine-specific paths that need review before use elsewhere. Do not assume that an isolated checkout or a passing source test has migrated the live runtime. See the [migration checklist](docs/layout-migration.md).

## Compatibility

Choose an individual package and read its README before installing it. Packages target different DSH releases; presence in this repository does not mean a package supports your installed version.

- [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) declares DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` and Node.js `>=24.9.0`.
- [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) targets DSH `0.2.1` and only replaces upstream prompt text whose fingerprint matches its reviewed version.
- The root [pnpm workspace](pnpm-workspace.yaml) retains development dependencies from the DSH `0.1.0-rc.8` line. Its build and test scripts are not a repository-wide compatibility check.
- Older adapters have package-specific requirements. In particular, the Web Search and Cursor invariant companions depend on a registry absent from current DSH master. Do not treat their older installation examples as current-version guidance.

The [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) distinguishes maintained extensions, retained reference implementations, and removed managed providers.

## Plugins and presets

These entry points describe each component's setup, behavior, and limitations; this is not an install-all list.

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) | Observes tool failures and repeated calls. Installation defaults to observation without LLM calls; proposal generation is opt-in, and activation and rollback require human commands. |
| [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) | Opt-in, preset-scoped alternatives for the Workflow and Ralph prompt sections. Tool schemas and execution behavior remain unchanged; it registers no Cordis Skill. |
| [Goal acceptance](plugins/dsh-goal-acceptance/README.md) | Retains the original request and checks evidence records for Goal completion and initial delegation. Unused since the request acceptance pilot was removed, and not updated for DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where some of its tests fail. |
| [Workflow result selection](plugins/dsh-workflow-results/README.md) | Saves a complete workflow result before returning selected fields through `resultKeys`; requires a tool replacement in the chosen preset. |
| [Codex transport recovery](plugins/dsh-codex-transport-recovery/README.md) | Classifies specific premature WebSocket closures as transport errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Sandbox facts](plugins/dsh-sandbox-facts/README.md) | Writes each bash call's sandbox mode, denial, enforcement and runner failure as a `tool_facts` NDJSON line for headless `--json` runs. Meant to be loaded only by worker runs. |
| [pi-ai server error recovery](plugins/dsh-pi-ai-server-recovery/README.md) | Classifies pi-ai failures that report a 5xx status only as text as server errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Workspace attach](plugins/dsh-workspace-attach/README.md) | Lets a headless run join a web workspace group through `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID`. The web host performs the attach. |
| [AI reference-store daily preset](presets/ai-reference-store-daily/README.md) | Declares the preset for a separately configured reference-store application. Selecting the preset does not start a daily batch. |

Older integrations and local forks:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Web Search](plugins/dsh-web-search/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-web-search` | Keyless DuckDuckGo HTML search, ported from [pi-web-access](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access). |
| [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. |
| [Cursor adapter](plugins/dsh-llm-cursor/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor` | Runs a Cursor SDK agent for each harness model call, with replay-state session continuity. |
| [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. |
| [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. |

Deployment-specific bundles and presets:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. |
| [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. |
| [Aistore structured reader](plugins/dsh-aistore-native-preset/README.md) | Declares the `aistore-native` preset for reader and reviewer child Sessions with scoped tool restrictions; missing presets reject creation without falling back. |
| [Slack intake](plugins/dsh-slack-intake/README.md) | Connects a DSH profile to the Go aistore CLI and runs one claimed reader or reviewer task through a fixed native Agent route; requires absolute paths to the executable and store, and never selects another model or provider. |
| [LLM fallback](plugins/llm-fallback/README.md) | Retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list after a configured error before content (such as quota or rate limits); other requested models are not substituted. |
| [Local presets](presets/) | Preserves local behavior on current upstream subagent controls in `ai-reference-store-next`, recording its upstream base in `UPSTREAM.json`. |

[plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task.

## Skills

[skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it.

| Skill | Purpose and prerequisites |
|---|---|
| [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. |
| [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). |
| [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. |
| [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). |
| [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. |
| [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. |
| [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. |
| [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. |
| [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. |
| [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. |

[skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill.

## Installation

1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile.
2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them.
3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles.
4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation.

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions.

## Development

Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository.

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-market English | [中文](README.zh.md) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dshmarket)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dshmarket) [![stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/dsh-market/dsh-market?style=flat)](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) The plugin market inside DeepSeek Harness. Open Settings → **Plugin Market** → browse, search, one-click install. ![dsh-market](assets/demo-en.png) One-click themes — install, switch live, no restart: ![Themes tab](assets/themes-en.png) ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket ``` Restart `dsh web`, then open **Settings → Plugin Market**. ## What you get - **Browse & search** the full community catalog (800+ plugins, growing daily) — category filters, star counts, top/new sorting, bilingual descriptions that follow your UI language - **Screenshots** — AppStore-style screenshots in the install dialog: author-curated via the registry, with automatic README extraction as fallback; images load from GitHub hosting only, and only after you open the dialog - **Themes** — a dedicated tab for community themes and skins: install → active immediately, switch with one click (themes are mutually exclusive, your choice survives restarts), uninstall to revert - **One-click install** — confirm the source, watch live progress; most plugins go live after a page refresh, no restart - **Backup & restore** — export your profile's plugin list and configuration as readable JSON, import it on another machine, or store it on WebDAV with daily auto-backup; restores validate before writing and roll back on failure - **Updates** — per-plugin update checks (npm version or pinned commit vs HEAD), one-click update, or update everything at once; the market updates itself the same way - **Uninstall** — two-step confirm; plugins installed this session are removed live - **Hot disable / enable** — toggles write `- id: …` + `disabled: true|false` into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the official patch layer, mechanism ported from [dsh-plugin-hub](https://github.com/Noob-stupid/dsh-plugin-hub)): DSH's HMR re-composes within ~1s, no restart, and the loader re-applies the choice on every boot; hand-edited patch rows show as badges, host-infrastructure plugins are protected from toggling, and a malformed patch file is never made worse - **Restart when needed** — changes that cannot hot-load show a one-click restart beside the pending-change banner; the action is restricted to same-origin loopback requests - **Zero jargon** — if a component is missing (pnpm), the market detects it and offers a one-click automatic setup - **Log export** — one click produces a sanitized plain-text log for bug reports (home paths and credential shapes are masked; nothing is ever sent anywhere) - **Diagnostics** — the plugin load order and conflict surface, one page: bundle stack with official/community badges, duplicate loader entries, dependency version mismatches, multi-version core packages, overrides and invalid config entries. Plain-language terms, problem blocks highlighted, everything collapsible ## Speed Installs prefer npm tarballs over full-repo GitHub downloads whenever a plugin publishes to npm (registry-verified against the repo to prevent name squatting). Registry installs are typically seconds; GitHub-only plugins depend on your connection to GitHub. ## Security - Installs are restricted to sources listed in the curated [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) registry — anything else is rejected - Build scripts stay blocked by default (pnpm ≥10); allowing one is your explicit per-package choice - Terminal/CLI-surface plugins are flagged before you install them into the web profile - The install endpoint accepts same-origin POST only; the market never phones home - Backups can contain credentials from your profile config — the UI warns before export and upload; WebDAV sync is https-only, refuses private-network targets, and never stores your password in the browser - The restart endpoint additionally requires a direct loopback client (forwarded requests are rejected) and relaunches the exact DSH entry, arguments, environment, and working directory - One-click restart launches a detached replacement. If DSH is managed by systemd, launchd, pm2, or another supervisor, set the plugin option `allowRestart: false` and let the supervisor own restarts instead; the pending-change notice remains visible but the button is hidden - For terminal-attached launches, the detached replacement keeps running after the original terminal closes - Listing ≠ endorsement: plugins are third-party code, install sources you trust ## Submit your plugin **This repo is the market app, not the catalog.** The plugin list comes from the curated [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry — to get your plugin listed in the market, open a PR **there** (one entry in the list; the site and this market pick it up automatically, usually within a day). Please don't PR plugin entries against this repo. ## Roadmap & feedback - Planned features live on the [Roadmap](https://github.com/orgs/dsh-market/projects/1) — every item welcomes community PRs (drop a note in the linked issue before starting) - File bugs and ideas as [issues](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market/issues); attaching the market's "Export log" makes diagnosis 10x faster ## Data source Live from [awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json) — curated entries, npm mapping, and star counts refreshed daily by CI — with a bundled snapshot as offline fallback. ## Friends ### DSH Desktop (dataelement) [dsh-desktop](https://github.com/dataelement/dsh-desktop) — a desktop app for DeepSeek Harness: run and manage a local Harness without installing Node.js yourself. Ships with this plugin market preset as the default. [dshdesktop.com](https://dshdesktop.com) ### DSH Get [DSH Get](https://www.dshget.com/) — a searchable web directory for discovering DeepSeek Harness plugins: category filters, bilingual descriptions, install commands and per-plugin detail pages. Its normalized catalog snapshot is public at [bobby-sheng/dshget-data](https://github.com/bobby-sheng/dshget-data). ### modlens [modlens](https://github.com/liustack/modlens) — the first vision plugin for DeepSeek Harness: bolts visual understanding onto text-only models like DeepSeek and GLM. Paste an image, get structured JSON evidence back — OCR, layout, semantics. Available right in this market: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @liustack/modlens ``` ## License MIT · [dshmarket.com](https://dshmarket.com) # deepseek-harness-plugins English | [日本語](README.ja.md) Unofficial plugins, local forks, presets, skills, and maintenance tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This is a source collection, not a single installable plugin or a distribution of DSH. ## Contents - [Repository structure](#repository-structure) - [Compatibility](#compatibility) - [Plugins and presets](#plugins-and-presets) - [Skills](#skills) - [Installation](#installation) - [Development](#development) - [Repository scope and ownership](#repository-scope-and-ownership) - [License](#license) ## Repository structure Each directory below is a source collection, not a deployment inventory. Cloning the repository installs and enables nothing. | Path | Contents | |---|---| | [plugins/](plugins/) | Plugin sources, local forks, and retained reference implementations, one directory per component. [plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) keeps its nested package layout. | | [presets/](presets/) | Agent-preset declarations: a manifest and a Cordis patch per preset. Declaring a preset does not install the packages its rows name. | | [configs/](configs/) | Configuration-only bundles and service configuration, with no runtime code. See [its README](configs/README.md). | | [skills/](skills/) | Authored skills and upstream-derived copies, one directory per skill. | | [bin/](bin/) | Maintainer scripts that build, pack, and check packages, the weekly maintenance helpers, and the [runtime placement](bin/runtime-placement.md) notes. Not a public CLI. | | [scripts/](scripts/) | The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs). | | [tests/](tests/) | Vitest configuration and upgrade regression specs that are not package-local. | | [tasks/](tasks/) | Change cards for the kstack card-flow, one file per card, each tied to one issue. See [its README](tasks/README.md). | | [docs/](docs/) | [Layout migration](docs/layout-migration.md) and [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) notes, and the retained [implement-task flow diagram](docs/implement-task-flow.html). | | [.agents/](.agents/) | Development notes and the harness-facing skills for working on this repository. | | [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/) | Project-local skills loaded by Claude Code when working in this repository. Currently contains [verify-dsh-plugins](.claude/skills/verify-dsh-plugins/SKILL.md), which starts a disposable DSH host with a chosen plugin and mock LLM to verify the web UI and headless CLI with screenshots and logs. Machine-specific settings live in `.env` (described by `.env.example`). | Root documents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the agent entry point ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) links to it); [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the development flow; [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes runtime layering and verification limits; [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) with [core-exceptions.json](core-exceptions.json) defines the Core baseline. A local working copy also holds ignored directories such as `reports/`, `releases/`, and `local-design/`. They contain private material and are not part of the published tree. **Layout migration:** Existing installations, profiles, systemd units, and scripts may still refer to old root-level paths. Moving this repository's sources does not update them; inventory and migrate those references before replacing an active checkout. The retained Slack worker configuration contains machine-specific paths that need review before use elsewhere. Do not assume that an isolated checkout or a passing source test has migrated the live runtime. See the [migration checklist](docs/layout-migration.md). ## Compatibility Choose an individual package and read its README before installing it. Packages target different DSH releases; presence in this repository does not mean a package supports your installed version. - [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) declares DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` and Node.js `>=24.9.0`. - [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) targets DSH `0.2.1` and only replaces upstream prompt text whose fingerprint matches its reviewed version. - The root [pnpm workspace](pnpm-workspace.yaml) retains development dependencies from the DSH `0.1.0-rc.8` line. Its build and test scripts are not a repository-wide compatibility check. - Older adapters have package-specific requirements. In particular, the Web Search and Cursor invariant companions depend on a registry absent from current DSH master. Do not treat their older installation examples as current-version guidance. The [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) distinguishes maintained extensions, retained reference implementations, and removed managed providers. ## Plugins and presets These entry points describe each component's setup, behavior, and limitations; this is not an install-all list. | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) | Observes tool failures and repeated calls. Installation defaults to observation without LLM calls; proposal generation is opt-in, and activation and rollback require human commands. | | [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) | Opt-in, preset-scoped alternatives for the Workflow and Ralph prompt sections. Tool schemas and execution behavior remain unchanged; it registers no Cordis Skill. | | [Goal acceptance](plugins/dsh-goal-acceptance/README.md) | Retains the original request and checks evidence records for Goal completion and initial delegation. Unused since the request acceptance pilot was removed, and not updated for DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where some of its tests fail. | | [Workflow result selection](plugins/dsh-workflow-results/README.md) | Saves a complete workflow result before returning selected fields through `resultKeys`; requires a tool replacement in the chosen preset. | | [Codex transport recovery](plugins/dsh-codex-transport-recovery/README.md) | Classifies specific premature WebSocket closures as transport errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. | | [Sandbox facts](plugins/dsh-sandbox-facts/README.md) | Writes each bash call's sandbox mode, denial, enforcement and runner failure as a `tool_facts` NDJSON line for headless `--json` runs. Meant to be loaded only by worker runs. | | [pi-ai server error recovery](plugins/dsh-pi-ai-server-recovery/README.md) | Classifies pi-ai failures that report a 5xx status only as text as server errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. | | [Workspace attach](plugins/dsh-workspace-attach/README.md) | Lets a headless run join a web workspace group through `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID`. The web host performs the attach. | | [AI reference-store daily preset](presets/ai-reference-store-daily/README.md) | Declares the preset for a separately configured reference-store application. Selecting the preset does not start a daily batch. | Older integrations and local forks: | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [Web Search](plugins/dsh-web-search/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-web-search` | Keyless DuckDuckGo HTML search, ported from [pi-web-access](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access). | | [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. | | [Cursor adapter](plugins/dsh-llm-cursor/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor` | Runs a Cursor SDK agent for each harness model call, with replay-state session continuity. | | [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. | | [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. | Deployment-specific bundles and presets: | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. | | [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. | | [Aistore structured reader](plugins/dsh-aistore-native-preset/README.md) | Declares the `aistore-native` preset for reader and reviewer child Sessions with scoped tool restrictions; missing presets reject creation without falling back. | | [Slack intake](plugins/dsh-slack-intake/README.md) | Connects a DSH profile to the Go aistore CLI and runs one claimed reader or reviewer task through a fixed native Agent route; requires absolute paths to the executable and store, and never selects another model or provider. | | [LLM fallback](plugins/llm-fallback/README.md) | Retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list after a configured error before content (such as quota or rate limits); other requested models are not substituted. | | [Local presets](presets/) | Preserves local behavior on current upstream subagent controls in `ai-reference-store-next`, recording its upstream base in `UPSTREAM.json`. | [plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task. ## Skills [skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it. | Skill | Purpose and prerequisites | |---|---| | [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. | | [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). | | [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. | | [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). | | [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. | | [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. | | [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. | | [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. | | [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. | | [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. | [skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill. ## Installation 1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile. 2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them. 3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles. 4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation. For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout: ```sh pnpm dsh plugin --help ``` Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions. ## Development Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope. This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)). The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository. | Root command | Scope | |---|---| | `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. | | `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. | | `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. | For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions. The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter). The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer. ## Repository scope and ownership This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner. The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Preserve the upstream license and attribution notices included with imported code, forks, and skills.

---
description: "Supply generic icons for selected local applications without changing DSH Core or its application launcher."
kind: "package-bundle"
---

# @local/dsh-open-in-app-icons

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

## Summary

This bundle supplies cacheable generic images for application icon URLs that have no usable icon on this host. Its default selection covers `filemanager`, `cursor`, and `vscode`. It preserves the existing browser authentication, application catalog, launcher, and other icon URLs. It adds no browser code and changes no Core files.

## Table of Contents

- [Use this package](#use-this-package)
- [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation)
- [Model Experience](#model-experience)
- [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work)

## Use this package

Install the verified release archive into the intended profile through Plugin Manager, using `action: install_bundle` and its absolute archive path as `target`. The layer inserts only `local-open-in-app-icons`; it does not disable or replace the upstream plugins. Disable this bundle through Plugin Manager to remove its routes. A browser may retain already cached images until their cache lifetime expires.

The complete local selection is in [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml). `applicationIds` is a required nonempty list of distinct lowercase application ids. `cacheMaxAgeSeconds` is a required nonnegative integer; the supplied layer uses 3600 seconds. A profile override replaces the complete config, so retain both fields.

Only authenticated GET requests for the selected exact paths receive an SVG with status 200 and a private browser cache lifetime. Authentication and trust failures remain 401 or 403; other methods remain 405. Other paths retain the upstream response, including unknown icon ids and unavailable change summaries.

## Understand the implementation

[The Host plugin](index.mjs) registers exact routes through the public `webServer.register` API. Exact routes take precedence over the existing upstream icon prefix. Every route uses `connection.requestRejection` before returning image bytes. Context effects remove all registrations on unload; activation fails for invalid config, duplicate ids, a missing bundled image, or an exact-route collision.

[The SVG](assets/fallback.svg) reuses DSH's existing `right-up-outline` geometry under the included [MIT license](LICENSE). Its neutral gray works as a standalone image on light and dark backgrounds; it does not claim to be an application logo.

Run the source regressions with `uv run --no-project bin/test.py`. Pass `--package /absolute/path/to/unpacked/package` to run the same tests against an unpacked release. The tests use a real Cordis Loader, WebServer, and upstream open-in-app implementation, with deterministic desktop and authentication fixtures. The running browser is verified separately after deployment.

## Model Experience

None. This bundle adds no model tools, instructions, or Session events.

### Token effect

None.

### KV Cache effect

None.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

Each selected URL intentionally serves the generic image, even if an application icon becomes available later. Remove that application id and reload the configuration to restore upstream icon discovery. The plugin does not discover missing icons automatically, change application availability, create desktop entries, persist change summaries, or filter Console errors. Its manifest restricts activation to the tested DSH version; verify compatibility before widening that requirement.

A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. |---|---|

| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

# pi-ai server error recovery

Corrects only terminal model-request errors with the code `PI_AI_ERROR`, which only the pi-ai adapter emits, whose message carries a 5xx status as text without the numeric code: `Internal Server Error`, `Bad Gateway`, `Service Unavailable`, or `servers are currently overloaded`. `Gateway Timeout` is not on the list: pi-ai already maps it to the retryable `TIMEOUT`. The official `llm/stream` waterfall changes its code to `SERVER`; the original message and every other field remain intact. pi-ai's own classifier (`classifyPiAiError` in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`) recognizes a 5xx failure only by its three-digit code, so these failures otherwise end the turn without a retry ([#53](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues/53)).

The package does not retry, change models, alter requests, suppress errors, or increase budgets. The official `llm-retry` executor keeps ownership: `SERVER` is in the default `retryableCodes`, and the provider's `retryPolicy` bounds the retries. Other codes, other messages, completed responses and streamed content are unchanged. A persistent failure still ends the turn after the retry budget.

Install as a DSH bundle. No build scripts or runtime dependencies are required. Cordis disposes the listener when the bundle is disabled. Remove this package when the official pi-ai adapter classifies these failures as `SERVER` and the regression tests pass without it.

Verification: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` checks each corrected phrase, unchanged cases, streamed content, metadata, and delegation to the downstream stream. Real provider failures are not simulated by those tests.

# dsh-prompt-compact

Opt-in prompt alternatives for DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1. Upstream tool plugins remain installed; this plugin replaces reviewed Workflow and Ralph system-prompt sections in the selected preset.

## Behavior

- Workflow and Ralph retain explicit-request restrictions and alternatives. Ralph retains the warning that worker reports are not independent verification.
- Cordis and Subagent guidance come directly from DSH. The legacy dynamic-plugin Skill is not registered.
- Tool schemas, permissions, runtime context, execution defaults, ordering, and complete-prompt overrides are unchanged.

The plugin uses the public `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall and calls `next()`. Disposal restores upstream behavior on the next assembly without rewriting Session history.

Only the two sections in `index.mjs` are eligible. Each original must match its reviewed SHA-256 fingerprint. Changed or customized instructions remain intact and produce a warning once per text version; empty or missing sections stay absent. Review the upstream contract before changing a fingerprint.

## Install and opt in

Use the built CLI from the upstream version you run:

```sh
node "$DSH_UPSTREAM_ROOT/apps/cli/lib/bin.js" plugin --profile web add /path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/plugins/dsh-prompt-compact
```

The bundle patch is empty: installation makes the package resolvable but does not enable it globally. Add this row to the `config.plugins` list of a locally authored `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` declaration, never a shipped file:

```yaml
- id: prompt-compact
  name: '@kkiyama117/dsh-prompt-compact'
```

Keep the normal tool plugins. This row consumes `systemPrompt`, publishes no service, and needs no isolate realm. Restart DSH after changing package files and verify a new session. Remove the row to opt out; remove the bundle only after no preset references it.

The runtime imports only Node built-ins, avoiding a second copy of Cordis or DSH registries from this repository's older dependencies.

## Verification

```sh
DSH_UPSTREAM_ROOT=/path/to/built/upstream node --test plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/tests/plugin.test.mjs
```

Tests use that checkout's real Cordis, scope, and system-prompt services. They cover sibling-scope isolation, disposal, complete-prompt overrides, waterfall delegation, unchanged schemas/context, reviewed-source matching, and retention of customized instructions. They do not establish improved task quality for a live model. The legacy `tests/preset-probe.mjs` targets the retired directory-preset API and is not the validation entry point for 0.2.1.

## Provenance

`UPSTREAM.json` records the reviewed upstream commit. The retained Skill files document the old runtime and are not registered by this version. `LICENSE` preserves the upstream notice.

# Sandbox facts

Writes one `tool_facts` line to stdout for each `bash` call whose result carries sandbox facts, so a caller of DSH headless `--json` can prove from the tool host (outside the sandbox) how each command was confined. The model-facing text and the headless `tool_result` line stay unchanged ([#76](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues/76)).

## Line format

```json
{"type":"tool_facts","callId":"<callId>","tool":"bash","sandbox":{"mode":"workspace-write","denied":false,"enforcement":"partial","runnerFailed":false}}
```

- `callId` is the call's `callId`, the same value as the `callId` of its headless `tool_result` line. Join the two by `callId`, never by order: the facts line is written when Core emits `tools/result`, which can come before the `tool_result` line.
- Every key is always present. `mode` is the bash value's `sandbox.mode` as given. `denied` is a boolean. `enforcement` is `"full"`, `"partial"`, or `null` when the value has no `enforcement` key (`danger-full-access`, or a command that was never confined). `runnerFailed` is `true` only when the value says so, `false` when the key is missing. In current Core a foreground runner failure is thrown instead (see below), so `runnerFailed` is `false` in practice; the key stays so that the line shape matches the contract kstack reads.
- No line is written for another tool, a failed call (a sandbox runner failure is thrown, so it is a failed call), a value without `sandbox` (such as a background or promoted job handle), or a value whose sandbox fields are malformed: `mode` not a string, `denied` not a boolean, `enforcement` other than `"full"` or `"partial"` (including an explicit `null` or any other string), or `runnerFailed` not a boolean (including an explicit `null`). A reader must treat a `bash` `tool_result` without a facts line as unknown, never as confined.

## Why it cannot be forged

The plugin writes from the DSH process. A bash command's own stdout and stderr are collected through pipes and reach headless output only JSON-escaped inside a `tool_result` line, so a command cannot print a top-level line.

## Loading

Load it only in headless `--json` runs, because it writes to stdout. Until it is loaded, it does nothing. Loading it in worker runs is a separate kstack change: `run-worker.sh` is to add this row to its run patch, and the package must resolve where `dsh` loads plugins:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: sandbox-facts
      name: '@kkiyama117/dsh-sandbox-facts'
```

No build step and no runtime dependencies. Tests: `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` (synthetic values only).

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|

|---|---|

2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them.
3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles.
4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation.

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions.

## Development

Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository.

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. |
| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions.

The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter).

The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer.

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Preserve the upstream license and attribution notices included with imported code, forks, and skills.

# Session connection cleanup

Listens to the official `session/disposed` event and calls pi-ai’s public `cleanupSessionResources(session.id)`. It never clears all Sessions or closes a cache after each turn. Cordis owns listener disposal. Socket closure is requested synchronously; peer closure is not awaited.

The imported pi-ai package is a peer so the Host adapter and this listener use the same module identity. Installation selects the Host row `local-session-cleanup`. No model calls, timers, stored records, or monkey patches are added.

| [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. |

| [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. |
| [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. |

Deployment-specific bundles and presets:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. |
| [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. |

[plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task.

## Skills

[skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it.

| Skill | Purpose and prerequisites |
|---|---|
| [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. |
| [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). |
| [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. |
| [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). |
| [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. |
| [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. |
| [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. |
| [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. |
| [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. |
| [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. |

[skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill.

## Installation

1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile.
2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them.
3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles.
4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation.

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions.

## Development

Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository.

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. |
| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions.

The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter).

The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer.

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Preserve the upstream license and attribution notices included with imported code, forks, and skills.
