## Compatibility

Choose an individual package and read its README before installing it. Packages target different DSH releases; presence in this repository does not mean a package supports your installed version.

- [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) declares DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` and Node.js `>=24.9.0`.
- [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) targets DSH `0.2.1` and only replaces upstream prompt text whose fingerprint matches its reviewed version.
- The root [pnpm workspace](pnpm-workspace.yaml) retains development dependencies from the DSH `0.1.0-rc.8` line. Its build and test scripts are not a repository-wide compatibility check.
- Older adapters have package-specific requirements. In particular, the Web Search and Cursor invariant companions depend on a registry absent from current DSH master. Do not treat their older installation examples as current-version guidance.

The [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) distinguishes maintained extensions, retained reference implementations, and removed managed providers.

## Plugins and presets

These entry points describe each component's setup, behavior, and limitations; this is not an install-all list.

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) | Observes tool failures and repeated calls. Installation defaults to observation without LLM calls; proposal generation is opt-in, and activation and rollback require human commands. |
| [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) | Opt-in, preset-scoped alternatives for the Workflow and Ralph prompt sections. Tool schemas and execution behavior remain unchanged; it registers no Cordis Skill. |
| [Goal acceptance](plugins/dsh-goal-acceptance/README.md) | Retains the original request and checks evidence records for Goal completion and initial delegation. Unused since the request acceptance pilot was removed, and not updated for DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where some of its tests fail. |
| [Workflow result selection](plugins/dsh-workflow-results/README.md) | Saves a complete workflow result before returning selected fields through `resultKeys`; requires a tool replacement in the chosen preset. |
| [Codex transport recovery](plugins/dsh-codex-transport-recovery/README.md) | Classifies specific premature WebSocket closures as transport errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Sandbox facts](plugins/dsh-sandbox-facts/README.md) | Writes each bash call's sandbox mode, denial, enforcement and runner failure as a `tool_facts` NDJSON line for headless `--json` runs. Meant to be loaded only by worker runs. |
| [pi-ai server error recovery](plugins/dsh-pi-ai-server-recovery/README.md) | Classifies pi-ai failures that report a 5xx status only as text as server errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Workspace attach](plugins/dsh-workspace-attach/README.md) | Lets a headless run join a web workspace group through `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID`. The web host performs the attach. |
| [AI reference-store daily preset](presets/ai-reference-store-daily/README.md) | Declares the preset for a separately configured reference-store application. Selecting the preset does not start a daily batch. |

Older integrations and local forks:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Web Search](plugins/dsh-web-search/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-web-search` | Keyless DuckDuckGo HTML search, ported from [pi-web-access](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access). |
| [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. |
| [Cursor adapter](plugins/dsh-llm-cursor/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor` | Runs a Cursor SDK agent for each harness model call, with replay-state session continuity. |
| [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. |
| [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. |

Deployment-specific bundles and presets:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. |
| [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. |
| [Aistore structured reader](plugins/dsh-aistore-native-preset/README.md) | Declares the `aistore-native` preset for reader and reviewer child Sessions with scoped tool restrictions; missing presets reject creation without falling back. |
| [Slack intake](plugins/dsh-slack-intake/README.md) | Connects a DSH profile to the Go aistore CLI and runs one claimed reader or reviewer task through a fixed native Agent route; requires absolute paths to the executable and store, and never selects another model or provider. |
| [LLM fallback](plugins/llm-fallback/README.md) | Retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list after a configured error before content (such as quota or rate limits); other requested models are not substituted. |
| [Local presets](presets/) | Preserves local behavior on current upstream subagent controls in `ai-reference-store-next`, recording its upstream base in `UPSTREAM.json`. |

[plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task.

## Skills

[skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it.

| Skill | Purpose and prerequisites |
|---|---|
| [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. |
| [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). |
| [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. |
| [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). |
| [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. |
| [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. |
| [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. |
| [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. |
| [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. |
| [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. |

[skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill.

## Installation

1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile.
2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them.
3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles.
4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation.

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions.

## Development

Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository.

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. |
| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions.

The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter).

The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer.

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Preserve the upstream license and attribution notices included with imported code, forks, and skills.

# dsh-ssh — Remote SSH operations plugin for DSH

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Built on the capability list of [badseal/ssh-skill](https://github.com/badseal/ssh-skill), a remote SSH plugin tailored for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): a persistent connection pool inside the Host process + a Web GUI host-management panel + a Web terminal + Agent tools, all implemented through the official NPM SDK without modifying DSH source.

## Capabilities

| Capability | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Host management | CRUD, search, connection test; config stored in `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json`; supports key / password auth, passphrase keys, ProxyJump jump hosts (multi-level) |
| Config import | One-click parse of a standard `~/.ssh/config` (Host/HostName/User/Port/IdentityFile/ProxyJump etc.); existing aliases are skipped |
| Persistent connection pool | Reuses a long-lived connection per host (opposite of the ssh-skill daemon), automatically disconnects after 30 minutes idle, auto-reconnects on disconnect (up to 3 times) |
| Command execution | exec with a timeout (default 60s), stdout/stderr separated, output truncation guard (2MB) |
| Web terminal | xterm.js + WebSocket PTY terminal, auto-sizing, real-time output |
| File transfer | SFTP upload (browser file picker, NDJSON progress stream), download (progress bar + browser save); remote directory browsing |
| Port forwarding | Local port-forward tunnel (listens on 127.0.0.1 only) to reach a remote database / intranet service; list / stop supported |
| Cluster execution | One command run concurrently across many hosts (filter by alias / environment / tag, default concurrency 8) |
| Agent tools | `ssh_list` / `ssh_exec` / `ssh_upload` / `ssh_download` / `ssh_tunnel` / `ssh_cluster`; GUI and Agent share the same host config |

## Security model

- All `/api/dsh-ssh/*` routes are trust-fenced (loopback socket + loopback Host, or a Host header matching a web-runtime `trustedHosts` authority, with same-origin checks) — the interfaces that execute commands against remote servers are not exposed to arbitrary LAN devices.
- Passwords / key passphrases are stored in plain text in `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json`, file mode 0600, directory 0700 (the same trust model as ssh-skill writing passwords into ssh-config comments).
- Tunnels only listen on `127.0.0.1`.
- Before the Agent uses a tool, the host must first be configured in the GUI (or imported from ~/.ssh/config).
- `ssh_upload` / `ssh_download` read/write arbitrary local paths on this machine with host-process privileges (not through the bash sandbox) — same host-local-path semantics as ssh-skill, be aware of that permission surface.
- The remote output of exec / cluster is returned verbatim (not sanitized); a command like `env` may bring secrets from the remote environment back into the conversation log.

## Install

Install the family aggregate package `@linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all` (all plugins and skins in one) or this plugin alone:

```sh
### 从 npm 安装（推荐）
dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-ssh

### 从仓库安装（开发调试）
git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web-ui.git
cd dsh-web-ui
pnpm install && pnpm -r build
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-ssh

```

After installing, **restart `dsh web`**: a "SSH" entry appears in the sidebar; the plugin description is injected into the Agent prompt automatically.

## Configuration

The settings panel (plugin config) toggles `announceToAgent` (whether to announce the plugin to the Agent) and `enabled` (master switch).

## Data

- Host config: `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` (versioned JSON, atomic write)
- Transfer staging: `os.tmpdir()/dsh-ssh-uploads/`

## Development

```sh
pnpm install --filter @linxin666/dsh-ssh...
pnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-ssh test    # unit tests: store + engine (embedded ssh2 Server + real sshd)
pnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-ssh build   # tsc types + tsdown dual-half artifacts
```

## Known limitations

- The remote target path of an upload must be an absolute path (relative paths are rejected).
- Download does not support a whole directory yet (download files individually); upload supports recursive directories (walks the local directory and transfers file by file).
- exec auto-reconnect on disconnect (up to 3 times) may re-execute non-idempotent commands — watch out for side effects on long commands.
- Every hop of a ProxyJump jump host must be a host alias already configured in this plugin.
- Resume (broken-transfer continuation) is not implemented yet.
- The transfer of Agent tools is a host-machine local path (same semantics as ssh-skill).

# deepseek-harness-plugins

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

Unofficial plugins, local forks, presets, skills, and maintenance tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This is a source collection, not a single installable plugin or a distribution of DSH.

## Contents

- [Repository structure](#repository-structure)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Plugins and presets](#plugins-and-presets)
- [Skills](#skills)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Development](#development)
- [Repository scope and ownership](#repository-scope-and-ownership)

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. |
| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions.

The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter).

The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer.

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

# @linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The one-click aggregate package for the whole dsh web UI family: installing it brings every functional plugin (task-board / git-graph / pet / remote-web-ui / live-stats / web-ui-settings / skin-center / community-plugins) plus the skin family (`dsh-skins`, skin assets bundled inside). The compat bridge layer is folded into this package (`src/client`), so no separate compat npm package is needed.

## What it is

- **One install, everything on**: its dependencies pull in all sub-plugin packages (dsh-client-ui-aionui-panel / dsh-client-ui-task-board / dsh-client-ui-git-graph / dsh-pet / dsh-remote-web-ui / dsh-live-stats / dsh-ssh / dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings / dsh-client-ui-skin-center / dsh-client-ui-community-plugins / dsh-skins). The local `ui-dsh-aionui-panel` row is **retired** (settings namespace + Side Card card only; no Explorer/Preview, no `/aionui-panel/*` routes).
- **Aggregation carrier**: `cordis.patch.yml` aggregates the `insert` lines of each sub-plugin, mounted through the dsh plugin profile mechanism.

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all
```

### From the repository (development)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web-ui.git
cd dsh-web-ui
pnpm install && pnpm -r build
node scripts/link-profile.mjs
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-web-ui-all
```

Restart `dsh web` for the plugins to take effect.

### Manual upgrade

When you upgrade by bumping the version in the profile `package.json` and running `pnpm install`, the top-level `node_modules/@linxin666/*` entries are not always refreshed: they can stay linked to the previous version's store directory until recreated. After upgrading, verify the links resolve to the new version (on Windows: `cmd /c rmdir <link>` then `cmd /c mklink /J <link> <target>`), then restart `dsh web`.

## Known limitations

- Every sub-plugin activates together. For only a subset, install that sub-plugin package directly.
- Do not install the aggregate package alongside the standalone package of the same plugin (e.g. @linxin666/dsh-liangshen); run `dsh plugin remove` on the old package before switching.
- Dependencies on the `@deepseek-ai/*` SDK are pinned; compatibility follows the repository's release cadence.

| [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. |

| Component | Purpose |

Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. # @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The dsh web UI plugin group for the DSH settings page: it adds a first-level settings section (a sibling nav item of General / Models / Plugins / Agent presets) that hosts the enable switches and configuration forms of the family plugins.

## What it is

- **One section for the family**: on the DSH settings page it registers a first-level section that renders directly expanded (a static heading followed by the cards, no disclosure fold) and hosts the enable switches and configuration forms of the remaining dsh web UI family plugins (task-board, live-stats, remote-web-ui, describe-image).
- **Sibling sections**: Skin Center, Community Plugins and Desktop Pet ship as their own packages and register their own first-level sections that open directly expanded.

## Install

### From npm (recommended)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-web-ui-settings
```

### From the repository (development)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web-ui.git
cd dsh-web-ui
pnpm install && pnpm -r build
dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-web-ui-settings
```

Restart `dsh web` for the section to appear in the settings page.

## Known limitations

- The section shows on the dsh settings page only when its prerequisite (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings`) is present.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
ModLens

Give a text-only model sight, and just paste the image.

🥇 The FIRST vision plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 🥇

简体中文 · Troubleshooting · Configuration · Output contract · Security · ModSearch (web)

The flagship DeepSeek and GLM chat models are text-only and cannot read images. ModLens is a plug-in vision engine that gives a text-only model sight. **ModLens reads images pasted straight into the chat**, no saving to a file and passing a path first. ## Talk to us Issues are welcome any time: [open one](https://github.com/liustack/modlens/issues/new/choose). And come find me on X: **[@liustack](https://x.com/liustack)**. What you built with it, which harness you are on, what should come next. New releases land there first, and a proper community space is on the way. ## Highlights **🥇 The first vision plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh):** one command, `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @liustack/modlens@3.17.3`, and the text-only DeepSeek model behind dsh reads images through a native `modlens_read_image` tool. Updating is the same command again. The version is named rather than `@latest` on purpose: pnpm 11 holds back releases published in the last 24 hours and resolves the tag against what survives, so `@latest` would install whatever shipped a day ago ([details](docs/harness-setup.md#keeping-it-up-to-date)). Pasting an image works two ways. **① Just paste.** On a text-only model the pasted image lands as a private temp file and its path enters the composer — the same interaction OpenCode and Pi ship — and the `modlens_read_image` tool takes it from there. **② Pick a `(modlens vision)` entry** in the model selector (it remembers your choice, so once is enough), then paste: the thumbnail stays visible in your message, closer to the Codex app feel, and the image is converted to structured evidence at request time, answered by the same underlying route. The plugin auto-discovers every provider route carrying text-only DeepSeek or GLM models and adds a wrapped entry per route (a stock install gets **`DeepSeek-V4-Flash (modlens vision)`** and **`DeepSeek-V4-Pro (modlens vision)`**; extra routes like opencode-go or zai get their own); the two families' own vision models are excluded automatically. Which paste route applies is the host's per-model call: only a model its metadata positively confirms text-only is taken over, anything unconfirmed is left alone, so vision models keep their native paste ([details](docs/harness-setup.md)). **Paste an image and it reads it.** No saving to a file and passing a path first. - **The lightest touch on the market.** No hooks, no wrappers, no local proxy daemon, not a single line changed in any harness config: on the skill harnesses it is exactly one skill folder, on dsh exactly one plugin. Uninstalling is deleting a folder, and your agents are back to stock. - **Zero-config start.** Reuses what Claude Code, OpenCode, or Pi already have set up: the multimodal models on your machine go straight to work. Nothing at all? Antigravity CLI is a free no-key channel, and a free Gemini key brings a read down to 5-10 seconds. - **Evidence, not imagination.** Full transcription, reading-order layout regions, entity and relation lists. The model quotes specifics. - **Install once, use everywhere.** Verified on real machines in Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode. ## Installation **Step 1, hand it to your AI.** Send it this line: > Install and configure the modlens skill following https://github.com/liustack/modlens/blob/main/INSTALL.md, then run the health check and tell me the result. The install starts by checking what your machine already has. An existing login in Claude Code, OpenCode, or Pi can be enough: modlens asks before reusing any of them, and the health check tells you where things stand. **Step 2, only if the health check comes back empty, set up a free engine.** The recommended choice is a free Gemini API key (about three minutes at [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com), no credit card), which also makes every read 5-10 seconds. A free OpenAI-compatible key from another platform works too. To avoid any sign-up, install Antigravity CLI instead, then sign in: ```bash curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash agy # sign in, then exit ``` The install also inventories vision reachable through your other local harness CLIs (OpenCode, Pi) and asks, per harness, whether modlens may reuse it. Granted logins join the engine pool as equals, and every reused read is labeled with whose quota it spent. ## Usage Once installed, just chat. Paste an image or drop a path, ask anything, and the skill triggers on its own: the image goes to a vision engine and the answer comes back grounded in what it read. ## Vision engines: six built-in providers, four reusable CLIs, one failover chain ModLens does not depend on any single vision service. Ten sources of vision in total: six built-in providers, any one of which is enough, plus four local agent CLIs whose logins can be reused. The built-ins: | Provider | What it needs | Speed per read | Good for | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | `gemini-api` | a free Gemini API key ([3 minutes, no card](https://aistudio.google.com)) | 5-10s | the recommended default | | `openai` | any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (key + baseUrl + model) | 5-10s | qwen-vl, GLM, self-hosted gateways | | `anthropic` | an Anthropic API key | 5-10s | machines already holding one | | `antigravity-cli` | the free `agy` CLI, one browser sign-in, no key | 15-45s | zero-signup starts | | `claude-cli` | a signed-in Claude Code | 20-45s | riding your existing Claude subscription | | `kimi-cli` | a signed-in Kimi Code | 20-45s | riding your existing Kimi subscription, named explicitly | Without a pinned provider, every configured engine forms one failover chain: the fast API providers try first, the agent CLIs back them up, the first good result wins, and `meta.attempts` records every attempt so a fallback is never silent. ### `openai` is a universal socket, not just OpenAI Any endpoint speaking the OpenAI chat-completions protocol with image input plugs straight in — that covers most of the vision-model world: ```bash modlens config set openai.baseUrl https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 # qwen-vl modlens config set openai.apiKey modlens config set openai.model qwen3-vl-plus ``` The same three keys work for GLM's open platform, SiliconFlow, OpenRouter, a self-hosted vLLM/Ollama, or any gateway of your own. If your favorite vision model has an OpenAI-compatible API, ModLens can drive it. ### Reusing what your machine already has Two more sources of vision need zero new keys, each behind one explicit consent recorded in config: - **The harness you are talking in right now.** Running inside Claude Code with a subscription signed in? `claude-cli` reads images through it out of the box. The install flow asks the same question for whichever harness you install into. - **Every other agent CLI on the machine.** `modlens doctor` discovers them, you grant per harness, and they join the same failover chain with no priority over your own keys. Every reused read is labeled in `meta.warnings` with whose quota it spent, so nothing is ever silently billed: | Reused CLI | What it needs | Grant with | Rides as | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | OpenCode | a vision model configured in OpenCode | `config set reuse.opencode true` | agent lane, 15-45s | | Pi | model credentials held by Pi | `config set reuse.pi true` | an API key upgrades to the 5-10s inline lane, OAuth drives Pi itself | | Grok | a signed-in Grok CLI (SuperGrok) | `config set reuse.grok true` | agent lane, 15-45s | ### Picking and routing Two knobs: `modlens config set provider ` states a preference (the chain still backs it up), `-p ` pins exactly one with no fallback. Machines behind a proxy set `HTTPS_PROXY` or `modlens config set proxy ` and the API providers route through it. Details: the [CLI manual](docs/cli.md) for defaults and flags, [Configuration](skills/modlens/references/configure.md) for every key, and [Security](docs/security.md) for who fetches what on remote URLs. ## See it work Unedited runs, all driving a text-only DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The newest one first: pasting a screenshot straight into DeepSeek Harness on the `DeepSeek-V4-Flash (modlens vision)` variant. The paste keeps its native thumbnail, the trajectory shows the image arriving "already transcribed by the modlens vision bridge", and the answer walks the UI element by element. ![Pasting an image straight into DeepSeek Harness, read through the modlens vision plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liustack/modlens/main/assets/demo-dsh-paste.jpg) A tweet screenshot in the Codex desktop app. It reads the author, the caption, the photo itself (down to what both people are wearing), the timestamp, and every engagement number: 5.4M views, 1.6K replies, 5.7K reposts, 116K likes. ![Text-only DeepSeek reading a tweet screenshot in full detail via ModLens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liustack/modlens/main/assets/demo-codex-app.jpg) Three images pasted at once. The model reads them one by one, spots that they belong to one visual family, and describes each illustration's content and style. ![Three images dropped together, read one by one](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liustack/modlens/main/assets/demo-codex-batch.jpg) The stress test: a scatter plot comparing 128 AI models. It reads both axes, the log scale, the per-provider color coding, the highlighted region, and every DeepSeek model called out with dashed markers. Dense charts are where vision bridges most often fail. ![The 128-model scatter plot read in full: axes, log scale, and highlighted region](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liustack/modlens/main/assets/demo-codex-chart.jpg) And the paste path, end to end, in a Claude Code terminal on DeepSeek. The pasted image arrives as a path rather than pixels, the skill triggers on its own, the guard confirms the model truly has no vision, and the slide's full content comes back: titles, layout, background, plus an honestly stated uncertainty about the truncated filename. ![The skill triggering on its own in a DeepSeek Claude Code session and reading a pasted slide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liustack/modlens/main/assets/demo-claude-paste-recovery.jpg) ## Documentation | Doc | Read it when | | :-- | :-- | | [Install guide](INSTALL.md) | Installing the skill step by step (written for an agent) | | [CLI manual](docs/cli.md) | The CLI the skill drives: flags, config, doctor | | [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) | A command failed and the message needs decoding | | [Configuration](skills/modlens/references/configure.md) | Setting a key, switching providers, fixing config | | [Output contract](docs/output-schema.md) | Parsing the JSON or building on it | | [Harness setup](docs/harness-setup.md) | Wiring it into Codex, Claude Code, Pi, or OpenCode | | [Security](docs/security.md) | File permissions, image content as untrusted input | | [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) | Finding what changed in a version | ## Contributing ModLens does not accept pull requests. The project is maintained by a single author who reviews every line, which is a deliberate choice for reliability. Two effective ways to contribute: - **[Open an issue](https://github.com/liustack/modlens/issues).** Bugs, suggestions, confusing errors, unclear docs. Issues are read and shape what gets built next. - **Fork it.** Under MIT your copy is fully yours to modify and publish. ## Shameless plug This project runs on LIUSTACK Skills: `shaping` before you build, `coding` while you build, `dig` when it breaks, `snapshot` when you hand off. Lighter than Superpowers, and stronger. ```bash npx -y skills add liustack/vibemaster -g ``` ⭐ If it helps, star [ModLens](https://github.com/liustack/modlens) and [VibeMaster](https://github.com/liustack/vibemaster). Stars are how the next developer finds them. ## Key ecosystem partners The projects worth recommending in the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem. - 🛒 **[dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market)** — The plugin market inside DeepSeek Harness. Browse 800+ community plugins with category filters and screenshot previews, one-click install and update, and live theme switching. Most need no restart. DeepSeek Harness 的可视化插件市场。设置页里直接逛社区全部 800+ 插件：分类筛选、截图预览、一键安装与更新、主题即点即换，装完多数免重启。 ## Star History ## Disclaimer Provided as-is under the MIT License below. The author makes no warranty and gives no endorsement for any particular use, commercial use included. Your use of upstream engines (Antigravity CLI, the Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic APIs, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) is governed by their own terms and quotas, which you are responsible for. ## License MIT # deepseek-harness-plugins English | [日本語](README.ja.md) Unofficial plugins, local forks, presets, skills, and maintenance tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This is a source collection, not a single installable plugin or a distribution of DSH. ## Contents - [Repository structure](#repository-structure) - [Compatibility](#compatibility) - [Plugins and presets](#plugins-and-presets) - [Skills](#skills) - [Installation](#installation) - [Development](#development) - [Repository scope and ownership](#repository-scope-and-ownership) - [License](#license) ## Repository structure Each directory below is a source collection, not a deployment inventory. Cloning the repository installs and enables nothing. | Path | Contents | |---|---| | [plugins/](plugins/) | Plugin sources, local forks, and retained reference implementations, one directory per component. [plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) keeps its nested package layout. | | [presets/](presets/) | Agent-preset declarations: a manifest and a Cordis patch per preset. Declaring a preset does not install the packages its rows name. | | [configs/](configs/) | Configuration-only bundles and service configuration, with no runtime code. See [its README](configs/README.md). | | [skills/](skills/) | Authored skills and upstream-derived copies, one directory per skill. | | [bin/](bin/) | Maintainer scripts that build, pack, and check packages, the weekly maintenance helpers, and the [runtime placement](bin/runtime-placement.md) notes. Not a public CLI. | | [scripts/](scripts/) | The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs). | | [tests/](tests/) | Vitest configuration and upgrade regression specs that are not package-local. | | [tasks/](tasks/) | Change cards for the kstack card-flow, one file per card, each tied to one issue. See [its README](tasks/README.md). | | [docs/](docs/) | [Layout migration](docs/layout-migration.md) and [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) notes, and the retained [implement-task flow diagram](docs/implement-task-flow.html). | | [.agents/](.agents/) | Development notes and the harness-facing skills for working on this repository. | | [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/) | Project-local skills loaded by Claude Code when working in this repository. Currently contains [verify-dsh-plugins](.claude/skills/verify-dsh-plugins/SKILL.md), which starts a disposable DSH host with a chosen plugin and mock LLM to verify the web UI and headless CLI with screenshots and logs. Machine-specific settings live in `.env` (described by `.env.example`). | Root documents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the agent entry point ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) links to it); [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the development flow; [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes runtime layering and verification limits; [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) with [core-exceptions.json](core-exceptions.json) defines the Core baseline. A local working copy also holds ignored directories such as `reports/`, `releases/`, and `local-design/`. They contain private material and are not part of the published tree. **Layout migration:** Existing installations, profiles, systemd units, and scripts may still refer to old root-level paths. Moving this repository's sources does not update them; inventory and migrate those references before replacing an active checkout. The retained Slack worker configuration contains machine-specific paths that need review before use elsewhere. Do not assume that an isolated checkout or a passing source test has migrated the live runtime. See the [migration checklist](docs/layout-migration.md). ## Compatibility Choose an individual package and read its README before installing it. Packages target different DSH releases; presence in this repository does not mean a package supports your installed version. - [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) declares DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` and Node.js `>=24.9.0`. - [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) targets DSH `0.2.1` and only replaces upstream prompt text whose fingerprint matches its reviewed version. - The root [pnpm workspace](pnpm-workspace.yaml) retains development dependencies from the DSH `0.1.0-rc.8` line. Its build and test scripts are not a repository-wide compatibility check. - Older adapters have package-specific requirements. In particular, the Web Search and Cursor invariant companions depend on a registry absent from current DSH master. Do not treat their older installation examples as current-version guidance. The [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) distinguishes maintained extensions, retained reference implementations, and removed managed providers. ## Plugins and presets These entry points describe each component's setup, behavior, and limitations; this is not an install-all list. | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) | Observes tool failures and repeated calls. Installation defaults to observation without LLM calls; proposal generation is opt-in, and activation and rollback require human commands. | | [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) | Opt-in, preset-scoped alternatives for the Workflow and Ralph prompt sections. Tool schemas and execution behavior remain unchanged; it registers no Cordis Skill. | | [Goal acceptance](plugins/dsh-goal-acceptance/README.md) | Retains the original request and checks evidence records for Goal completion and initial delegation. Unused since the request acceptance pilot was removed, and not updated for DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where some of its tests fail. | | [Workflow result selection](plugins/dsh-workflow-results/README.md) | Saves a complete workflow result before returning selected fields through `resultKeys`; requires a tool replacement in the chosen preset. | | [Codex transport recovery](plugins/dsh-codex-transport-recovery/README.md) | Classifies specific premature WebSocket closures as transport errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. | | [Sandbox facts](plugins/dsh-sandbox-facts/README.md) | Writes each bash call's sandbox mode, denial, enforcement and runner failure as a `tool_facts` NDJSON line for headless `--json` runs. Meant to be loaded only by worker runs. | | [pi-ai server error recovery](plugins/dsh-pi-ai-server-recovery/README.md) | Classifies pi-ai failures that report a 5xx status only as text as server errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. | | [Workspace attach](plugins/dsh-workspace-attach/README.md) | Lets a headless run join a web workspace group through `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID`. The web host performs the attach. | | [AI reference-store daily preset](presets/ai-reference-store-daily/README.md) | Declares the preset for a separately configured reference-store application. Selecting the preset does not start a daily batch. | Older integrations and local forks: | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [Web Search](plugins/dsh-web-search/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-web-search` | Keyless DuckDuckGo HTML search, ported from [pi-web-access](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access). | | [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. | | [Cursor adapter](plugins/dsh-llm-cursor/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor` | Runs a Cursor SDK agent for each harness model call, with replay-state session continuity. | | [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. | | [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. | Deployment-specific bundles and presets: | Component | Purpose | |---|---| | [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. | | [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. | | [Aistore structured reader](plugins/dsh-aistore-native-preset/README.md) | Declares the `aistore-native` preset for reader and reviewer child Sessions with scoped tool restrictions; missing presets reject creation without falling back. | | [Slack intake](plugins/dsh-slack-intake/README.md) | Connects a DSH profile to the Go aistore CLI and runs one claimed reader or reviewer task through a fixed native Agent route; requires absolute paths to the executable and store, and never selects another model or provider. | | [LLM fallback](plugins/llm-fallback/README.md) | Retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list after a configured error before content (such as quota or rate limits); other requested models are not substituted. | | [Local presets](presets/) | Preserves local behavior on current upstream subagent controls in `ai-reference-store-next`, recording its upstream base in `UPSTREAM.json`. | [plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task. ## Skills [skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it. | Skill | Purpose and prerequisites | |---|---| | [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. | | [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). | | [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. | | [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). | | [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. | | [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. | | [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. | | [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. | | [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. | | [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. | [skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill. ## Installation 1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile. 2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them. 3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles. 4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation. For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout: ```sh pnpm dsh plugin --help ``` Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions. ## Development Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope. This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)). The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository. | Root command | Scope | |---|---| | `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. | | `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. | | `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. | For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions. # Workflow result selection

This independent tool package retains the deployed `resultKeys` extension without patching DSH. It uses the official workflow engine and preserves native/background recording and cancellation. The complete JSON result is saved before selected fields are delivered; invalid keys or storage failure fail delivery.

Install this package, then replace the `tool-workflow` plugin in the selected preset with `@kkiyama117/dsh-workflow-results`; preserve its config and its isolated workflow engine. The package alone installs no Host tool. Source and upstream revision are recorded in `UPSTREAM.json`. `lib` is generated from `src` using the selected DSH checkout’s TypeScript compiler. The copied DSH code is MIT licensed; see LICENSE.

# deepseek-harness-plugins

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

Unofficial plugins, local forks, presets, skills, and maintenance tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This is a source collection, not a single installable plugin or a distribution of DSH.

## Contents

- [Repository structure](#repository-structure)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Plugins and presets](#plugins-and-presets)
- [Skills](#skills)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Development](#development)
- [Repository scope and ownership](#repository-scope-and-ownership)
- [License](#license)

## Repository structure

Each directory below is a source collection, not a deployment inventory. Cloning the repository installs and enables nothing.

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [plugins/](plugins/) | Plugin sources, local forks, and retained reference implementations, one directory per component. [plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) keeps its nested package layout. |
| [presets/](presets/) | Agent-preset declarations: a manifest and a Cordis patch per preset. Declaring a preset does not install the packages its rows name. |
| [configs/](configs/) | Configuration-only bundles and service configuration, with no runtime code. See [its README](configs/README.md). |
| [skills/](skills/) | Authored skills and upstream-derived copies, one directory per skill. |
| [bin/](bin/) | Maintainer scripts that build, pack, and check packages, the weekly maintenance helpers, and the [runtime placement](bin/runtime-placement.md) notes. Not a public CLI. |
| [scripts/](scripts/) | The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs). |
| [tests/](tests/) | Vitest configuration and upgrade regression specs that are not package-local. |
| [tasks/](tasks/) | Change cards for the kstack card-flow, one file per card, each tied to one issue. See [its README](tasks/README.md). |
| [docs/](docs/) | [Layout migration](docs/layout-migration.md) and [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) notes, and the retained [implement-task flow diagram](docs/implement-task-flow.html). |
| [.agents/](.agents/) | Development notes and the harness-facing skills for working on this repository. |
| [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/) | Project-local skills loaded by Claude Code when working in this repository. Currently contains [verify-dsh-plugins](.claude/skills/verify-dsh-plugins/SKILL.md), which starts a disposable DSH host with a chosen plugin and mock LLM to verify the web UI and headless CLI with screenshots and logs. Machine-specific settings live in `.env` (described by `.env.example`). |

Root documents: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the agent entry point ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) links to it); [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the development flow; [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes runtime layering and verification limits; [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) with [core-exceptions.json](core-exceptions.json) defines the Core baseline.

A local working copy also holds ignored directories such as `reports/`, `releases/`, and `local-design/`. They contain private material and are not part of the published tree.

**Layout migration:** Existing installations, profiles, systemd units, and scripts may still refer to old root-level paths. Moving this repository's sources does not update them; inventory and migrate those references before replacing an active checkout. The retained Slack worker configuration contains machine-specific paths that need review before use elsewhere. Do not assume that an isolated checkout or a passing source test has migrated the live runtime. See the [migration checklist](docs/layout-migration.md).

## Compatibility

Choose an individual package and read its README before installing it. Packages target different DSH releases; presence in this repository does not mean a package supports your installed version.

- [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) declares DSH `0.2.1-rc.3` and Node.js `>=24.9.0`.
- [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) targets DSH `0.2.1` and only replaces upstream prompt text whose fingerprint matches its reviewed version.
- The root [pnpm workspace](pnpm-workspace.yaml) retains development dependencies from the DSH `0.1.0-rc.8` line. Its build and test scripts are not a repository-wide compatibility check.
- Older adapters have package-specific requirements. In particular, the Web Search and Cursor invariant companions depend on a registry absent from current DSH master. Do not treat their older installation examples as current-version guidance.

The [maintenance scope](docs/maintenance-scope.md) distinguishes maintained extensions, retained reference implementations, and removed managed providers.

## Plugins and presets

These entry points describe each component's setup, behavior, and limitations; this is not an install-all list.

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [DSH Evolve](plugins/dsh-evolve/README.md) | Observes tool failures and repeated calls. Installation defaults to observation without LLM calls; proposal generation is opt-in, and activation and rollback require human commands. |
| [Prompt Compact](plugins/dsh-prompt-compact/README.md) | Opt-in, preset-scoped alternatives for the Workflow and Ralph prompt sections. Tool schemas and execution behavior remain unchanged; it registers no Cordis Skill. |
| [Goal acceptance](plugins/dsh-goal-acceptance/README.md) | Retains the original request and checks evidence records for Goal completion and initial delegation. Unused since the request acceptance pilot was removed, and not updated for DSH 0.2.2-rc.1, where some of its tests fail. |
| [Workflow result selection](plugins/dsh-workflow-results/README.md) | Saves a complete workflow result before returning selected fields through `resultKeys`; requires a tool replacement in the chosen preset. |
| [Codex transport recovery](plugins/dsh-codex-transport-recovery/README.md) | Classifies specific premature WebSocket closures as transport errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Sandbox facts](plugins/dsh-sandbox-facts/README.md) | Writes each bash call's sandbox mode, denial, enforcement and runner failure as a `tool_facts` NDJSON line for headless `--json` runs. Meant to be loaded only by worker runs. |
| [pi-ai server error recovery](plugins/dsh-pi-ai-server-recovery/README.md) | Classifies pi-ai failures that report a 5xx status only as text as server errors so the official retry policy can handle them. Does not add retries or change models. |
| [Workspace attach](plugins/dsh-workspace-attach/README.md) | Lets a headless run join a web workspace group through `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID`. The web host performs the attach. |
| [AI reference-store daily preset](presets/ai-reference-store-daily/README.md) | Declares the preset for a separately configured reference-store application. Selecting the preset does not start a daily batch. |

Older integrations and local forks:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Web Search](plugins/dsh-web-search/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-web-search` | Keyless DuckDuckGo HTML search, ported from [pi-web-access](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-web-access). |
| [Exa search compatibility](plugins/dsh-web-search-exa-compat/README.md) — `@local/dsh-web-search-exa-compat` | Keeps the Exa search provider of DSH 0.2.2-alpha.2 on 0.2.2-rc.1, which removed it from Core. Copy the old row's configuration to the new row before enabling it. |
| [Cursor adapter](plugins/dsh-llm-cursor/README.md) — `@kkiyama117/dsh-llm-cursor` | Runs a Cursor SDK agent for each harness model call, with replay-state session continuity. |
| [Web UI family](plugins/dsh-web-ui/packages/) | Local copies of UI, SSH, Git graph, settings, and Modlens packages; consult each package's README. |
| [Market](plugins/dsh-market/README.md) | Local plugin-market copy with its own build and compatibility checks. |

Deployment-specific bundles and presets:

| Component | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Session connection cleanup](plugins/dsh-session-cleanup/README.md) | Listens to `session/disposed` and requests synchronous closure of session resources; does not clear all Sessions or await peer socket closure. |
| [Open-in-app icons](plugins/dsh-open-in-app-icons/README.md) | Serves cacheable generic fallback icons for selected local application URLs; does not discover missing icons automatically or alter existing launcher routes. |
| [Aistore structured reader](plugins/dsh-aistore-native-preset/README.md) | Declares the `aistore-native` preset for reader and reviewer child Sessions with scoped tool restrictions; missing presets reject creation without falling back. |
| [Slack intake](plugins/dsh-slack-intake/README.md) | Connects a DSH profile to the Go aistore CLI and runs one claimed reader or reviewer task through a fixed native Agent route; requires absolute paths to the executable and store, and never selects another model or provider. |
| [LLM fallback](plugins/llm-fallback/README.md) | Retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list after a configured error before content (such as quota or rate limits); other requested models are not substituted. |
| [Local presets](presets/) | Preserves local behavior on current upstream subagent controls in `ai-reference-store-next`, recording its upstream base in `UPSTREAM.json`. |

[plugins/subagent-fallback/](plugins/subagent-fallback/) is not a bundle; it remains only as a reference for implement-task.

## Skills

[skills/](skills/) contains authored skills and upstream-derived copies. Cloning this repository does not install or enable them. Local deployments may link individual skill directories into a DSH skill search path; edit the source directory, not a separate copied version. Read each skill's prerequisites before enabling it.

| Skill | Purpose and prerequisites |
|---|---|
| [issue-driven-development](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md) | Shared issue intake, feature and bugfix delivery, verification, and development-process improvement for humans and AI agents. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) for this repository's setup. |
| [orchestrate-agents](skills/orchestrate-agents/SKILL.md) | Task formulation, direct-versus-delegated execution, and bounded orchestration. See its [runtime limits](skills/orchestrate-agents/README.md). |
| [archify](skills/archify/SKILL.md) | Local fork of [archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) for architecture visualization, with screenshot checks at 1920×1080 and 2048×1320. |
| [quint-lang](skills/quint-lang/SKILL.md) | Quint syntax and CLI reference, imported from [quint-llm-kit](https://github.com/quint-co/quint-llm-kit). |
| [quint-modeling](skills/quint-modeling/SKILL.md) | Build or review Quint specifications from requirements or source code. |
| [quint-execute-spec](skills/quint-execute-spec/SKILL.md) | Implement code against an existing Quint specification. |
| [quint-cli](skills/quint-cli/SKILL.md) | Container-based Quint CLI instructions; requires the documented container tool and image. |
| [quint-verify](skills/quint-verify/SKILL.md) | Run invariant and witness checks and produce a structured verification report. Requires the documented Quint container environment. |
| [slack-reference-intake](skills/slack-reference-intake/SKILL.md) | Reference intake for a separately configured private Go aistore, with authorized Slack access and DSH credentials. Not a standalone public demo. |
| [implement-task](skills/implement-task/SKILL.md) | Retained implementation-flow reference with a [Quint specification](skills/implement-task/spec/README.md). It depends on legacy `subagent-fallback` tools; migrate the callers and specification before using it with current DSH. |

[skills/verify-completion-gate/](skills/verify-completion-gate/spec/README.md) holds only a Quint specification, not a loadable skill.

## Installation

1. Install DSH separately and choose the target profile.
2. Check the selected package's README, manifest, and patch for DSH compatibility, prerequisites, and activation scope. Build compiled packages using their own development instructions before loading them.
3. Install only the selected bundle through DSH's Plugin Manager or plugin CLI. A bundle declares `dsh.bundle.patch` in its package manifest; the repository root and plain skill directories are not bundles.
4. Complete any package-specific opt-in steps. For example, Prompt Compact has an empty bundle patch and needs a row in a locally authored preset. DSH Evolve instead mounts in observation mode on installation.

For CLI usage from a DSH source checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --help
```

Use your own package location rather than the maintainer's filesystem paths in older examples. See the upstream [bundle publishing guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md) for profile installation. Do not edit shipped DSH presets to enable these extensions.

## Development

Use [Issues](https://github.com/kkiyama117/deepseek-harness-plugins/issues) to report problems or propose improvements. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the shared human/AI development flow and this repository's verification and publication scope.

This README is the English source; README.ja.md is its line-aligned Japanese pair; change both together. AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, and package READMEs are written in English. A package translation (README.zh.md or README.ja.md) is optional; when one exists it is updated in the same change, including any README.i18n.yaml record. These process/policy documents are maintained in Japanese only: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md), [docs/maintenance-scope.md](docs/maintenance-scope.md), [bin/runtime-placement.md](bin/runtime-placement.md), [bin/live-apply.md](bin/live-apply.md), and the issue-driven-development skill ([skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md](skills/issue-driven-development/SKILL.md)).

The root [package manifest](package.json) pins pnpm to `11.7.0`. The root workspace includes Web Search, Cursor, and five Web UI family packages—not every package in this repository.

| Root command | Scope |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install` | Installs dependencies for the root workspace using its lockfile. |
| `pnpm build` | Runs the build script of each workspace member. Builds are not all plain `tsc`; UI packages also bundle client assets. |
| `pnpm test` | Runs workspace-member test scripts with workspace concurrency set to one. |

For packages outside that workspace, follow their own README and package scripts. Do not use a passing root build or test run as evidence that those packages work with your DSH version. Compiled packages load generated output, not edited source; follow the package's rebuild and reload instructions.

The repository gate, `python3 bin/gate.py`, runs the checks of every package changed since `origin/main` that `bin/gate-checks.json` lists, plus the document checks, and fails for a changed package without an entry. Card-flow work uses it with the card dispatcher, `python3 bin/dispatch.py`; see the [card-flow adapter](AGENTS.md#card-flow-adapter).

The read-only [local setup diagnostic](scripts/local-setup.mjs) inspects a local DSH profile. It imports `plugins/dsh-market/lib/check.js`, so it requires a built Market package, which is outside the root workspace. It is not a fresh-clone setup command or an installer.

## Repository scope and ownership

This repository publishes plugin, preset, skill, test, and maintenance-tool sources. Credentials, private design and review material, execution reports, deployment inventories, local caches, and release archives stay outside Git. Review new files for sensitive data before committing; ignore rules are not a secret scanner.

The public history starts with a source-only snapshot; earlier local history is not available here. See [architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md) for composition and verification limits, and the [source ownership policy](SOURCE-OWNERSHIP.md) for the upstream Core baseline and reviewed exception.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Preserve the upstream license and attribution notices included with imported code, forks, and skills.

# Workspace attach

Sessions created with `dsh --profile headless` appear as "Ungrouped" in the web sidebar. The web host attaches a Session to a workspace only when the web UI creates it. A headless process must not write the workspace store directly, because the running web host keeps that store in memory and rewrites the whole file.

This package provides a hint-file handoff using two rows from one bundle:

- `local-workspace-attach-producer`: runs in the headless process.
- `local-workspace-attach`: runs in the web host. It injects `workspaceRegistry`, so it stays unmounted where that service is absent, such as the headless profile.

Install the bundle in both the web and headless profiles.

In the headless profile, the `local-workspace-attach` row never mounts, because `workspaceRegistry` exists only in the web host. Cordis then prints a warning on every headless run that the row is pending on `workspaceRegistry`. To avoid that warning, disable that row in the headless profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: local-workspace-attach
  disabled: true
```

Disabling it does not affect the producer row, which keeps writing hints.

## Use

Run headless from the workspace directory with `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID` set to an explicit workspace id, or to the literal `cwd` to pick the workspace whose path equals the Session cwd:

```bash
cd /path/to/workspace
DSH_WORKSPACE_ID=cwd dsh --profile headless "Summarize the open issues."
```

If `DSH_WORKSPACE_ID` is unset or empty, the producer does nothing.

To override `hintRoot` across both rows in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`hintRoot` must be an absolute path):

```yaml
- id: local-workspace-attach
  config:
    hintRoot: /srv/dsh/workspace-attach-hints
- id: local-workspace-attach-producer
  config:
    hintRoot: /srv/dsh/workspace-attach-hints
```

Producer and consumer must use the same `hintRoot` path.

Consumer-only options:

- `scanIntervalMs` (number, default `30000`): background scan period in milliseconds.
- `maxPendingMs` (number, default `600000`): maximum time in milliseconds to keep retrying an unreadable Session before rejecting it as expired.

## Behavior

On `session/created` for a top-level Session (Sessions with a parent or `origin: subagent` are skipped), the producer writes `<hintRoot>/<sessionId>.json` atomically through a temporary file and rename. It never overwrites an existing hint or rejected record.

The consumer runs in the web host:

- Scans the hint directory at startup, on directory changes (debounced), and periodically every `scanIntervalMs`.
- Processes hints sequentially one at a time.
- Calls the official `attachSession`, which requires the Session's stored cwd to equal the workspace path.

Hint outcomes:

- Attached: hint file deleted.
- Retry: kept while the Session is not readable yet, until `maxPendingMs` elapses, at which point it is rejected as `expired`.
- Rejected: renamed to `<sessionId>.rejected.json` containing the original hint, reason (`malformed-hint`, `unknown-workspace`, `no-workspace-for-cwd`, `attach-failed`, or `expired`), and timestamp. Rejected records are never retried.

Timers and the directory watcher are unreferenced and do not keep a process alive.

## Limits

- The Session cwd must equal the workspace path exactly. Runs started from a scratch directory or a separate git worktree cannot join. The `cwd` mode compares the stored cwd as written, so a cwd reached through a symlink does not match the workspace's resolved path.
- The web host must be running for the attach to happen. Hints wait until the consumer processes them and expire after `maxPendingMs`.
- A hint naming a workspace that does not exist is rejected immediately and is not retried later.

Run package tests with:

```bash
node --test tests/*.test.mjs
```

# llm-fallback

This Host bundle retries only the configured source provider/model on its explicit route list, and only after a configured error before content. The bundled policy maps `ollama-cloud/glm-5.3-flash` to `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` for QUOTA or RATE_LIMIT. Other requested models are not substituted. Production policy is in `cordis.patch.yml`.

Run pure tests and the real-Cordis waterfall smoke against the exact built deployment:

```sh
DSH_UPSTREAM_ROOT=/path/to/built/dsh node --test plugins/llm-fallback/test.mjs plugins/llm-fallback/mount.test.mjs
```

The mount test requires an explicit checkout so the plugins repository's older Cordis dependency cannot silently stand in for the upgraded runtime. Its provider responses are synthetic; it does not verify live model or credential availability.
