# dsh-combinagents

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

[![dsh-plugin topic](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-blue)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

A user-owned **reporting composition** for DSH (DeepSeek Harness) agents and
subagents.

DSH already gives each subagent a fixed native parent. This plugin adds a
separate, editable layer on top: you decide who reports to whom, independently
of the native subagent tree. The composition is an overlay. The plugin does not
move a session, rewrite its native parent, change its workspace, or change its
sandbox or permission policy.

> **Compatibility:** DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` on the desktop/web profile. This is an
> unpublished local plugin bundle, not an npm package to install from a
> registry. Node.js 22 or newer is required.

Part of the [dsh-plugin](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic.

## What you get

- A right-sidebar **Agent composition** tab.
- A separate count chip in the session header.
- Add local sessions or external agents, rename nodes, and set **Reports to**.
- Per-edge **message** and **interrupt** grants.
- Automatic mirroring when a subagent starts.
- **Sync native agents** to import native descendants.
- Clone a whole team, or bud one node into a new independent root.
- A plugin-owned task board, separate from DSH Team.
- Native-name model tools that use the composition, while keeping the native
  tool schemas.
- Cross-profile convergence: another DSH profile's edit becomes visible without
  restarting the Host.

## What it does not do

- It does **not** re-parent existing DSH sessions natively.
- It does **not** delete or rewrite DSH sessions when you remove nodes.
- It does **not** widen a sandbox, permission preset, or approval policy.
- It does **not** merge sessions or move a session to another workspace.
- It is **not** a cross-host or multi-user service. It is a local-profile
  feature.

Think of it as an editable organization chart beside the native subagent tree,
not a replacement for that tree.

## Requirements

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` with the desktop/web UI.
- Node.js 22 or newer.
- A **standard** DSH profile (or another preset that keeps the native
  delegation plugins mounted):
  - `tool-subagent-control`
  - `tool-subagent`
  - `tool-subagent-fork`
- The profile must expose `sessions`, `storageDomain`, `subagents`, and the
  sidebar-right client UI. Missing optional services degrade individual fields,
  not the whole tab.

The plugin can run beside other tool plugins. It keeps the native tool
definitions; it only intercepts execution for the six names listed below.

## Install

This checkout is a DSH **bundle** (`package.json` has a `dsh.bundle.patch`
entry). It is not published to npm.

1. Put the checkout in a stable local directory.
2. Register it in your DSH profile as a local bundle. Use the DSH Plugin Manager
   bundle installation for your DSH version, or the equivalent local package
   link in the profile.
3. Make sure the profile entry is enabled:

```yaml
- id: dsh-combinagents
  config:
    autoGrantDelegatedEdges: true
    # Optional: only needed when the JSONL session root is not $DSH_HOME/sessions.
    # sessionRoot: /absolute/path/to/sessions
  disabled: false
```

4. Keep the native delegation plugins mounted. Do **not** use the legacy
   `composed` preset that removes them; without the native definitions there is
   nothing for the plugin to intercept.
5. Restart the Host and refresh the GUI.

After a Host restart, open a **standard** session. Existing sessions created
under an older composed preset keep their old preset until you move them; they
receive a compatibility fallback, but a new standard session is recommended.

If the tab or header chip is missing, confirm the plugin is enabled in the
profile and refresh the page after the Host restart.

## Quick start

1. Open a normal standard session.
2. Open **Agent composition** from the right sidebar or the header chip.
3. Click **Create composition** if this session has no composition yet.
4. Click **Add a session** and select another session. Set its **Reports to**
   parent, or leave it as a root.
5. Open **Details** on an edge to allow messages or interrupts across that
   edge. New manual connections allow messages by default; interrupts stay off
   until enabled.
6. Start a subagent normally with `subagent` or `subagent_fork`. It is mirrored
   into the composition automatically, with its native parent and an
   auto-granted delegation edge.
7. Use **Sync native agents** if a native descendant is missing.
8. In **Teams**, choose a lead, check the connected members, and create one or
   more Teams. Overlapping or disconnected selections are rejected.
9. Use **Shared tasks** with the Team selector; tasks created inside a Team stay
   on that Team's board. Team tools resolve the caller's Team automatically.

A session belongs to at most one composition. If you attach a session that is
already in another composition, its subtree moves; a remaining source forest is
re-keyed to another local root. The moved subtree keeps its internal grants, and
a new boundary edge inherits the previous incoming grant, so an explicit deny
stays denied. An ordinary DSH fork is a new root; it does not inherit
composition membership from its `parentSession` header.

## The tab

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| Add a session | Add an existing DSH session as a composition node |
| Add external | Add a placeholder for an external/non-local execution |
| Reports to | Set the node's parent; `No parent` makes it a root |
| Rename | Change the node label (not the DSH session title) |
| Message / Interrupt grants | Allow that action along the composition path |
| Sync native agents | Import native descendants that are not mirrored yet |
| Clone whole tree | Create a new independent tree; source stays unchanged, including copied task/Team scopes when present |
| Bud as new root | Clone one node and its subtree as a new root |
| Show one-shot agents | Show one-shot nodes that are hidden by default |
| Teams | Select a lead and connected member nodes to create a Team; its board and task tools are scoped to that set |
| Shared tasks | Native-shaped task board: create, list, get, claim/release, edit, depend, reassign, complete, reopen, and delete |
| Session cleanup | Preview orphaned clone sessions and one-shot placeholders, open a brief first-user/last-message excerpt, then delete in a separate confirmed step |
| Open conversation | Open a local session; external nodes never offer it |

Nodes show `live`, `saved`, or `archived` state, plus the native parent,
workspace, sandbox, permission preset, agent preset, and lifecycle mode when
available. The tab scrolls vertically. **Add a session** and **Add task** use the
same in-place panel pattern, each with **Cancel**; Escape also closes the session
picker.

The tab filters **one-shot** nodes by default. Enable **Show one-shot agents**
to see them. External nodes remain visible because they are placeholders, not
necessarily one-shot agents.

## Model tools

The plugin does not register shadow copies of the native tools. It registers a
`tools/execute` interceptor. For these six names, the native definition and
therefore the model-facing name, description, parameters, output schema,
presentation, prompt guidance, and restrictions stay unchanged; only the
execution path uses the composition:

| Tool | In this plugin |
|---|---|
| `list_agents` | Lists continuable composition nodes, with `mode=` in the description |
| `send_message` | Follows composition edges and grants; rejects one-shot targets |
| `interrupt_agent` | Follows composition ancestor/grant rules; can interrupt live one-shot agents |
| `subagent` | Starts a native child, mirrors it, and auto-grants the edge |
| `subagent_fork` | Same as `subagent`, using the fork provider |
| `wait_agent` | Native caller-inbox wait behavior |

The plugin also exposes a **Team-shaped task API over the composition-owned
board**. When the native Team service/tools are not mounted, it registers
`team_task_create`, `team_task_list`, `team_task_get`, and `team_task_update`
with the same field names, actions, CAS revisions, dependencies, readiness, and
write-scope warnings as the native Team task tools. A Team is a connected
set of composition nodes; selecting a lead seeds its subtree and individual
members can be unchecked. When the caller belongs to one, these tools scope to
that Team's board and members. They write only the plugin
board, never native Team state; when Agent Teams is mounted, the native tools
win and these aliases are not registered. `team` selects another Team by id or
unique label, and `team_list` discovers Teams. `composition_task` remains a
legacy composition-board aggregate; it does not list Team tasks. Native
`list_subagent_models` and other unique tools are
untouched.

`list_agents` omits **one-shot** and **external** rows, matching the native
continuable listing. One-shot targets cannot receive follow-ups. The lifecycle
mode is shown in the row description because the native output schema does not
have a separate `mode` field.

### Teams and task boards

A Team is a **connected set of continuable local composition nodes**, not a
native Agent Team. In the composition tab choose a lead; its subtree is
preselected, then add or remove member checkboxes. The selected set is stored
explicitly. The server rejects disconnected sets, one-shot/external members,
duplicate labels, and Teams that overlap an existing Team. Team membership is
stored in the plugin domain, so it survives Host restarts without writing
native Team state.

The `Shared tasks` board follows the selected Team:

- **Composition board** shows tasks without a Team (`teamId: null`);
- a Team selection shows only that Team's tasks;
- Team tasks are capped at 256 non-deleted rows; deleting a Team task writes a
  tombstone (hidden from the board, retained for history); Team deletion removes
  its scoped tasks, not composition nodes or Sessions;
- clone/bud copies Team definitions whose member nodes are included and remaps
  their task `teamId`;
- a Team is a fixed membership snapshot: removing or moving a member, or a
  reparent that disconnects or overlaps it, is rejected. Delete the Team first
  if you need to change its structure.

When native Agent Teams is not mounted, the four Team-shaped tools use the
caller's Team automatically. Pass `team` (an id or unique label) to address a
different Team; the composition root may administer every Team, while a
non-root caller is limited to its own Team. `team_list` shows the available
Teams and their members. The selected Team in the tab is a **view scope**; a
model call that needs another Team must pass `team` explicitly.

| Tool | Scope |
|---|---|
| `team_task_create` | Creates on the caller's/explicit Team board, or the composition board outside a Team |
| `team_task_list` | Filters by status/owner/unowned/ready, returns compact native-shaped pages |
| `team_task_get` | Reads one task from the active scope |
| `team_task_update` | CAS actions: claim, release, edit, set_dependencies, complete, reopen, reassign, delete |
| `team_list` | Lists visible Team ids, labels, Leads, and members for explicit `team` selection |

Typical tool flow:

```text
team_list                         -> find the Team id or unique label
team_task_list { "team": "Build" }
team_task_create { "team": "Build", "subject": "...", "description": "..." }
team_task_update { "team": "Build", "task_id": "...",
                   "expected_revision": 1, "action": "claim" }
```

From the composition root, omitting `team` uses the board of the Team that
contains the root; outside any Team it uses the composition board.

Native Team tools win when Agent Teams is mounted; the plugin then does not
register these aliases. This is an overlay-level **Team-shaped task board**, not
a native Agent Team, Team mode, or a shared checkout. See the technical
contract in [`docs/TEAM-API.md`](docs/TEAM-API.md) and the live proofs in
[`docs/TEAM-TEST-2026-11-19.md`](docs/TEAM-TEST-2026-11-19.md) and
[`docs/TEAM-TEST-2026-11-20.md`](docs/TEAM-TEST-2026-11-20.md).

### Lifecycle modes

Composition nodes carry the same native lifecycle distinction:

| Mode | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `continuable` | A long-lived child that can receive follow-up messages |
| `one-shot` | A terminal execution with no follow-up |
| `external` | An external execution with no local session |
| `unknown` | A legacy or not-yet-synced record |

A name is not a lifecycle mode. A child without an explicit name still gets a
generated `agent-N` name and can still be continuable. Use **Sync native agents**
to refresh modes from the native catalogs.

## Cross-profile consistency

The storages live under the DSH home, so two profiles can open the same
composition data. Each Host keeps its own in-memory storage-domain snapshot.
The plugin makes them converge:

- After a durable composition, policy, task, Team, or clone write, a small
  `.revision` marker is updated.
- A reader that sees a newer marker reopens the storage domain and rebuilds
  session membership.
- Composition mutations take a process-shared `.mutation.lock`, so two profiles
  do not overwrite each other's read-modify-write.
- The tab polls `/state` every 3 seconds and the header chip polls `/summary`
  every 5 seconds while visible.

This is **eventual convergence**, not a synchronous distributed database.
Writes from an older plugin version do not publish the marker, and a custom
storage backend outside the default directory needs a `storageDir` override.

## Safety and authority

- The overlay never writes a DSH `SessionHeader`, native `subagent/catalog`,
  cwd, sandbox policy, or permission preset.
- Composition edges are advisory for organization. The plugin's `send_message`
  and `interrupt_agent` execution use composition grants; they do not bypass
  native session policy.
- Messages prefer the native relay inside a native tree. Live cross-tree
  targets use the composition relay.
- Composition **messages** are authorized by an edge grant, the composition
  root, or existing native-tree ancestry; they do not ask a per-message
  workspace approval question. A native-tree cold target is restored by the
  native subagent service. A plain inactive top-level target is resumed through
  `ctx.agents.resume` with a retained handle; an unowned native child returns
  `TARGET_UNOWNED`, and a foreign inactive native child returns
  `TARGET_NOT_RESUMABLE`. An explicit `allowMessage:false` grant overrides the
  root/native default bypass; only an implicit deny may be waived. **Interrupts** still ask the approval service
  when crossing workspaces without full permission; only an accepted one-shot
  approval proceeds.
- Every delivered, denied, or approval-denied action is audited.
- External nodes cannot receive follow-ups.
- Removing a node removes only the overlay. It never deletes a DSH session.
- **Session cleanup** is the only destructive session operation. It never
  touches live sessions or composition members; it deletes only inactive,
  explicitly confirmed orphaned clone sessions and one-shot placeholders from
  the default JSONL session root. Set `sessionRoot` for a custom root. It
  reclaims the session-log directory; shared attachment/cache files are not
  deleted. This cannot be undone.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| The six native-name tools still behave natively | Is the plugin enabled? Does the profile keep the native delegation rows? Restart the Host after installing. |
| `composition_*` tools are missing | They were removed by design; use the native names plus `composition_task` and, outside native Agent Teams, `team_task_*`. |
| `NOT_IN_COMPOSITION` | Create a composition for this session, or use `subagent` from a top-level agent. |
| `AGENT_BUSY` | An affected agent or one of its composition ancestors/descendants is running. Wait for it to finish. |
| `another DSH profile is changing the composition` | Another profile holds the mutation lock. Retry after a moment. |
| `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` | The domain could not be reloaded; reads keep the last in-memory snapshot and writes fail closed. Restart the Host. |
| `storageMemory` warning | The storage domain could not open. Changes last until the Host restarts; check the DSH storage backend. |
| `TEAM_STRUCTURE_CONFLICT` | A graph edit would remove a Team member, disconnect its selected set, or overlap another Team. Delete the Team before changing its structure. |
| `TEAM_MEMBER_MODE` | A Team member/owner is one-shot, or would become one. Teams require continuable local nodes. |
| `TEAM_LABEL_CONFLICT` / `TEAM_AMBIGUOUS` | Team labels must be unique; use the Team id when a legacy duplicate exists. |
| `TEAM_NOT_FOUND` / `TEAM_FORBIDDEN` | The `team` id/label does not exist, or the caller is neither the composition root nor a member. |
| `TEAM_TASK_LIMIT` / `TEAM_TASK_DELETED` | The 256 non-deleted task cap was reached, or a deleted Team tombstone was mutated. (HTTP surfaces the internal `TASK_LIMIT`.) |
| `TARGET_NOT_RESUMABLE` | The native subagent service cannot restore the target (missing/unsupported continuation state). |
| `TARGET_UNOWNED` | The target Agent is live but has no active runtime owner (for example an independently resumed child). Only a Host restart or the original handle owner can clear that state. |
| A one-shot agent is missing | It is hidden by default. Enable **Show one-shot agents**; use **Sync native agents** if its mode is still unknown. |
| The tree looks stale in another profile | Wait for the 3-second poll, refresh the page, or check that both profiles run this version. |
| The tab is absent | Confirm the plugin and client UI are enabled, then refresh after the Host restart. |

## Limitations

- One composition per session, and a strict `reports-to` forest.
- No native re-parenting and no merging of sessions.
- Labels are user-facing and may be duplicated; duplicate labels make
  `send_message` target selection ambiguous.
- The plugin does not change a session's workspace, sandbox, permission preset,
  or approval policy.
- Task-board and Team state is plugin-owned, not DSH Team state. Teams are
  connected overlays, not native Agent Teams and not a shared checkout. Graph
  edits that would invalidate a Team are rejected; delete the Team before
  removing or moving its members.
- Team tools are exposed only when the caller has a composition; outside a Team
  they operate on the composition board.
- A very large archived composition under an enormous transcript can still make
  the surrounding session UI paint slowly; the bridge itself is not the
  bottleneck.
- Legacy composed sessions use fallback tool definitions until they migrate to
  a standard preset.
- The exact native request-prefix fingerprint is not part of the acceptance
  tests yet.

## Development

```bash
npm test
npm run check
```

Tests use only Node's built-in test runner. There is no build step and no
runtime dependency.

```text
index.js                 Host entry and bridge lifecycle
client.js                Right-sidebar tab, header utility, count chip
src/graph.js             Pure composition graph
src/clone.js             Pure clone/bud planner
src/clone-manager.js     Clone/bud host adapter
src/store.js             Storage domain, revision reload, mutation lock
src/discovery.js         Session and native-catalog discovery
src/manager.js           Serialized mutations and grants
src/http.js              Loopback JSON bridge
src/controls.js          Native tool execution interception
```

More detail:

- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Product handoff](docs/HANDOFF.md)
- [DSH feasibility notes](docs/FEASIBILITY.md)
- [Standard-profile setup and migration](docs/COMPOSED-PROFILE.md)
- [Team API and lifecycle](docs/TEAM-API.md)
- [Native Team vs plugin Team comparison](docs/TEAM-NATIVE-COMPARISON-2026-11-20.md)
- [Clone/bud spike](docs/CLONE-SPIKE.md)
- [Working contract for contributors](AGENTS.md)

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# dsh-openloop-mas

OpenLoop MAS 插件（DeepSeek Harness）。

把「会闭合的多智能体循环」带进 DSH 对话：规划 → 执行 → **机检验收** → 复盘 →
闭合 / 升级人工工单，每一轮都写进 **append-only 账本**。

## 它做什么

在 DSH 里直接可用 6 个工具：

| 工具 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `mas_run` | 跑一个闭环任务，返回状态 + 逐条验收判定 + 票数 + 账本路径 |
| `mas_status` | 当前配置、运行数、未结工单 |
| `mas_ledger` | 读闭环账本（可按 run_id 过滤） |
| `mas_tickets` | 列出人工升级工单 |
| `mas_report` | 渲染某次运行的 Markdown 报告 |
| `mas_doctor` | 运行环境自检 |

插件**不重写闭环逻辑**：它通过 MCP（stdio JSON-RPC 2.0）调用本地 OpenLoop MAS
运行时，因此 DSH 对话里的判定与账本记录和 Codex / Claude Code 客户端**完全一致**。

## 前提

- **DSH >= 0.2.2-rc.1**（声明兼容区间 `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`）
- **Node.js >= 22.19**
- 已装好 OpenLoop MAS 运行时（默认在 `~/.mas`）

## 安装

前置：机器上已装好 OpenLoop MAS 运行时（默认在 `~/.mas`）。

```bash
# 从本仓库打包
cd integrations/dsh-openloop-mas
npm pack            # -> dsh-openloop-mas-0.7.13.tgz

# 装进 DSH Desktop profile
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "dsh-openloop-mas@file:<绝对路径>/dsh-openloop-mas-0.7.13.tgz"
dsh plugin --profile desktop list dsh-openloop-mas --depth 0
```

> `desktop` profile 由桌面应用独占管理，命令行会报
> `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`。
> 这种情况下请在 DSH Desktop 的插件面板里安装，或改用 `--profile cli`。

## 配置

```json
{
  "dsh-openloop-mas": {
    "masHome": "C:/Users/<you>/.mas",
    "python": "C:/Python314/python.exe",
    "timeoutMs": 900000
  }
}
```

- `masHome`：OpenLoop MAS 安装根目录（`install.ps1` 写入的位置）。留空则只依赖
  PATH 上的 `mas` 运行时。
- `python`：解释器路径。留空则从 `masHome` 推断，再退回 `python`。
- `timeoutMs`：单次 MCP 调用超时。默认 900000（15 分钟）——闭环可能要跑好几轮。

## 前提与边界

- 本插件**只负责调用**，判定权在 OpenLoop MAS 引擎手里：机检结果永远压过模型
  主观判断；缺席的评审在 `all` 模式下判**不通过**（不闭合）。
- 插件不引入任何第三方 npm 依赖（只用 DSH 自带的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 与
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`）。
- `lib/mcp-client.js` **零依赖**，可以脱离 DSH 单独跑单元测试：
  `node --test integrations/dsh-openloop-mas/tests/`。

## 挂载机制（容易踩的坑）

DSH 认的字段是 **`dsh.bundle.patch`**（指向 `cordis.patch.yml`），
不是 `dsh.profile.bundles`。放错的结果是：插件被当成普通依赖装上、
**根本不挂载**，pnpm 会警告 `declares no dsh.bundle`。

挂载后，DSH 启动时自动应用 patch：

```
- insert:
    - id: openloop-mas
      name: 'dsh-openloop-mas'
      config: ...
```

工具参数 schema 必须满足 DSH 的 JSON Schema 子集：`items.additionalProperties`
要**显式**为 `true` / `false`，否则 `defineTool` 会抛 `JsonSchemaError`，
整个插件 entry 不激活（`1 entry did not activate`）。

## 与 MOKI 的分工

MOKI 资料库（`dsh-moki-library`）管的是**资料与草稿**：本地文件/文件夹/链接管理、
多格式预览、Word/Excel/PPT 隔离草稿编辑、选区协同（`Alt+D` 唤起 DSH 对话），
修改先入草稿、用户确认后才写回原文件。

OpenLoop MAS 管的是**闭环**：验收标准、机检判定、账本、人工升级。

两者可以同时装，各管一段：MOKI 负责把资料整理成一份可交付的产物，
OpenLoop MAS 负责判定这份产物到底过不过。

## License

MIT

# OpenLoop MAS · 会闭合的多智能体系统

> 一个 **零依赖、纯标准库** 的多智能体闭环运行时：把「规划 → 执行 → 验证 → 复盘」写成**有验收标准、有退出条件、有过程账本**的工程循环。
> **下载一个脚本就能装**，初学者也能跑起来。


[![ci](https://github.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
[![deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-orange.svg)]()

**第一次来？** 直接看 [5 分钟上手](#5-分钟上手) —— 一条脚本装好，
不用 API Key 就能跑通一个闭环。

**想知道它凭什么敢叫「会闭合」？** 看 [为什么做这个](#为什么做这个)。

**想看它踩过的坑？** 最后一节 [门禁考古](#门禁考古) 记着每一道门禁的来历。

---

## 5 分钟上手

### 方式一：一条脚本（跨平台，不需要 Python 环境准备）

```bash
# macOS / Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas/main/install.sh | bash

# Windows（PowerShell）
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

脚本会自己建好虚拟环境、装好包、注册 MCP 服务、跑一遍自检。

### 方式二：pip 安装（需要 Python 3.10+）

```bash
pip install openloop-mas     # 见下方说明：这个包名目前还没上 PyPI
mas install        # 装 skills + 注册 MCP 服务器
mas demo           # 不需要任何 API Key，先看它自己跑通闭环
mas doctor         # 自检（包含 skills 漂移、运行时版本落后）
mas sync           # 把已安装的 skills 同步回包内版本
mas runtime        # 看本机装的是哪一版运行时
mas upgrade        # 把落后的旧版运行时换成当前这版
```

> **升级过、想换新版本？** 先 `mas upgrade`（换掉真正在跑的那份运行时），
> 再 `mas install`（让 MCP 注册指向新版本）。
> 只做后者的话，skills 和注册都刷新了，**但真正在跑的还是旧代码**——
> 这正是 `mas doctor` 的 `runtime` 检查现在会指出来的事。

> **关于 `pip install openloop-mas`**：这个包名**目前还没有在 PyPI 上建立**，
> 直接 pip 会得到 `No matching distribution found`。现在请用上面的**安装脚本**，
> 或从 [Releases](https://github.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas/releases/latest) 下载 wheel。
> `mas doctor` 会**实测**这个包名在 PyPI 上的状态并如实告诉你——
> 包名一旦发布，这段说明和 doctor 的检查都会自动对上。

`mas doctor` 说的是人话：每一项都解释「这是什么」，标清楚是**必需 / 建议 / 可选**，
最后给一句**结论**和一条**下一步命令**：

```
[OK  ] python（必需）
       3.14.10
       是什么：Python 版本够不够新（3.10 以上才能跑）
[注意] skill_codex（可选）
       未安装: ...\.codex\skills\mas-loop\SKILL.md（运行 mas install）
       是什么：给 Codex 装的 skill：让 Codex 会用这个闭环工具
...
小结：8 项正常，6 项注意，0 项坏了
结论：闭环能跑，但智能体接不上：skill_codex、skill_claude、skills_sync、mcp_codex、mcp_claude 还没装。
下一步：运行 mas install，一条命令装上 skill 并注册 MCP 服务。
```

三种结论的区别很重要：**闭环跑不起来**（必需项坏了）、**闭环能跑但智能体接不上**
（skill / MCP 没装）、**一切就绪**。退出码只在第一种情况下非零。

`mas install` 做的是**装 agent skills 到 Codex / Claude Code 的 skill 目录**、
**把 MCP 服务器注册进 `~/.codex/config.toml` 和 `~/.claude.json`**，
然后你可以直接开一个新终端，Codex 和 Claude Code 就认识这套闭环工作流了。

- 幂等：重复跑不会重复注册，也不会覆盖你已有的配置。
- 安全：任何被修改的配置文件都会先备份成 `*.bak-<时间戳>`。
- 不含密钥：安装过程不写入任何 API Key。

> 想看它装了什么，加 `--json`。

### 方式三：只下载一个脚本（零依赖，最适合初学者）

不用 clone、不用 pip、不用自己装任何东西——**下载一个脚本文件**，双击/执行它就行：

```powershell
# Windows：下载 install.ps1 到任意目录，然后执行
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux：下载 install.sh 到任意目录，然后执行
bash install.sh
```

脚本会自己从 GitHub Release 拉取已发布的 wheel、用标准库解开、装到
`~/.mas/`，然后注册 MCP 服务器和 skills，最后跑一遍离线自检。
**不需要 git，不需要 pip，不需要编译工具。**

**机器上还没有 Python？脚本会自己装一个。**

- Windows：脚本会下载官方 Python 安装包，**按当前用户静默安装**
  （不需要管理员权限，不改 `PATH`，不装 py 启动器），
  然后在它自己放的位置把解释器找回来继续装。
- macOS / Linux：脚本会调用系统自带的包管理器
  （Homebrew / apt / dnf / yum）装一个 Python 3.12。
  如果装不上（比如没有 `sudo` 权限），脚本会**如实告诉你**
  并给出可以直接复制的那条命令。

> 不想让它动你的机器？加 `-NoBootstrap`（Windows）或
> `MAS_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1`（shell），它就只检查、自己不去装。

想装固定版本（而不是"最新版"）：

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1 -Version 0.7.93
```

```bash
MAS_VERSION=0.7.93 bash install.sh
```

> 脚本默认会往 `PATH` 里加一条 `~/.mas/bin`（Windows 写当前用户的注册表）。
> 不想动 `PATH` 就加 `-SkipPath`（Windows）或 `MAS_SKIP_PATH=1`（shell）。

### 方式四：从源码安装（适合开发）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tffgwy/openloop-mas.git
cd openloop-mas

# Windows
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
# macOS / Linux
bash install.sh

# 不需要任何 API Key，先看它自己跑通闭环
mas demo
```

> `install.ps1` / `install.sh` 与 `mas install` 做的是同一件事，
> 前者适合从源码装（含开发环境）或「只下一个脚本」，
> 后者适合 pip 安装后的机器。

> 配置文件固定在 `~/.mas/config.json`（Windows：`%USERPROFILE%\.mas\config.json`）。
> 运行账本另存在 `state_dir` 下，两者分开——换状态目录不会把配置弄丢。
> CI 里想隔离，用环境变量 `MAS_CONFIG_PATH` 指定配置文件、`MAS_STATE_DIR` 指定状态目录。

`mas demo` 会离线跑三个场景，并把真实结果打出来：

```
[OK ] closure     期望=closed             实际=closed             迭代=2 票=-
[OK ] stagnation  期望=escalated          实际=escalated          迭代=4 票=T-20261111-085346-4396
[OK ] budget      期望=budget_exhausted   实际=budget_exhausted   迭代=1 票=-
```

> 注意：`mock` 模式里，**通过与否由引擎的机检规则判定**，不是模型自己说「我完成了」。
> mock 只是模拟执行者产出草稿，验证权始终在确定性检查器手里。

## 为什么做这个

多智能体协作最常见的失败不是「模型不够聪明」，而是**循环不闭合**：

- 没有可核验的验收标准 → 大家互相说「差不多了」，谁也说服不了谁；
- 没有退出条件 → 一轮轮往下聊，token 烧完还没有结论；
- 没有过程记录 → 出问题无法复盘，无法交接，无法追责；
- 没有止损 → 一个明显走不通的任务会一直重试到超时。

Loop Engineering 要解决的就是这件事：**让「做完没有」变成一个可以被机器判定的事实。**

OpenLoop MAS 的做法是把闭环写成代码约束，而不是寄望于提示词：

| 环节 | 角色 | 产出 | 谁来判定 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 计划 | `planner` | 步骤与风险 | — |
| 执行 | `worker` | **交付物本身** | — |
| 验证 | `verifier` | 逐条验收标准的通过/不通过 + 证据 | 引擎（机检优先） |
| 复盘 | `reflector` | 失败原因与下一轮改法 | — |
| 闭合 | `lead` | **只判没人判的标准**：`close` / `revise` / `escalate` | 引擎（**最终否决权**） |

一个循环只有同时满足 **产物 + 逐条判定 + 决策 + 账本条目** 才算闭合；否则状态只有三种：`escalated`（升级人工）、`budget_exhausted`（预算止损）、`error`。**没有「差不多完成」这个状态。**

`lead` 是**顾问，不是法官**：**机检失败是事实**，这种情况**不咨询 lead**；
咨询了它也**只能填空**（机检已定的标准原样保留）。
**停滞、预算、死线**由引擎**最终否决**，lead 关不掉一个超预算的运行；
**lead 自己判不了**（`met` 读不出布尔值）就**保持未判定、继续追问**。

## 跑一个真实任务

```bash
mas run --goal "写一份 v0.1.0 的发布说明" \
  --criteria '{"id":"c1","desc":"包含版本号","check":{"type":"contains","arg":"v0.1.0"}}' \
  --criteria '{"id":"c2","desc":"不少于 200 字","check":{"type":"min_chars","arg":200}}'
```

输出：

```
状态：closed（迭代 2 次，token 2140）
账本：/home/you/.mas/ledgers/runs.jsonl
  [PASS] c1 (rule) all required strings present
  [PASS] c2 (rule) length 418 >= 200
--- 交付物预览 ---
...
```

### 支持的机检规则（由引擎判定，可复现）

| type | 含义 | 参数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` / `not_contains` | 必须包含 / 禁止包含 | `arg`（字符串或数组） |
| `min_chars` / `max_chars` | 长度上下限 | `arg`（整数） |
| `regex` | 正则命中 | `arg`（模式） |
| `lines_min` | 非空行数下限 | `arg`（整数） |
| `section` | 必须包含某个 `## 标题` | `arg`（标题名） |
| `json_keys` | JSON 对象必须包含的键 | `arg`（键数组） |

判定口径（实测确认，写标准时按这个来）：

| 类型 | 精确判定 | 容易踩的坑 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` | 产物含给定字符串；`arg` 可为数组，**全部命中**才算通过 | 数组漏一项整条失败 |
| `not_contains` | 产物**不含**任何给定字符串 | 数组是「一个都不能出现」 |
| `min_chars` / `max_chars` | 产物的**字符数**（含空白与换行） | 不是字数也不是字节数 |
| `regex` | `re.search` 匹配，**自动带 DOTALL**（`.` 能跨行） | 想跨行不必加 `(?s)`；命中的是子串不是全串 |
| `lines_min` | **非空行**数（空行不计） | 段落间空行不影响计数 |
| `section` | 产物里**整行**恰好是 `## <arg>`（允许行尾空白） | **必须是二级标题 `##`**，`#`/`###` 都不算；正文里提到 `## 结论` 也**不算**；`## 结论分析` **不满足** `## 结论` |
| `json_keys` | 产物须是 JSON **对象**且含全部给定键 | 产物不是合法 JSON 直接判不通过 |

未知类型会被判为 `unjudged`（**不通过**），不会静默放过。

### 文件级机检（v0.7.15 起）：判定跟的是磁盘，不是文案

上面所有规则搜的都是**产物文本**。下面这十个搜的是**真实文件系统**——
「模型说写了」和「文件真的在」从此是两回事：

| type | 含义 | 参数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file_exists` | 文件存在且是普通文件 | `path` |
| `file_missing` | 文件不存在（清理类验收） | `path` |
| `file_contains` | 文件含给定字符串 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_not_contains` | 文件不含给定字符串 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_regex` | 文件内容命中正则 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_lines_min` | 非空行数下限 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_min_bytes` / `file_max_bytes` | 字节数上下限 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_sha256` | sha256 等于给定摘要 | `path` + `value` |
| `file_mtime_newer` | 修改时间晚于给定 ISO 时间戳 | `path` + `value` |

### 内容级机检（v0.7.70 起）：读的是文件**里面**，不是它的字节

上面十个搜的是**字节**。对**正文不是明文的格式**它们是瞎的：
PDF 的文字在**压缩流**里，`.docx` 本身是 **zip 包**，图片里没有文字。
下面六个**先把内容取出来再判**（只用标准库，不执行文件里的任何东西）：

| type | 含义 | 参数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_contains` | 文件**内容**含给定字符串 | `path` + `value` |
| `content_not_contains` | 文件**内容**不含给定字符串 | `path` + `value` |
| `content_regex` | 文件**内容**命中正则 | `path` + `value` |
| `content_lines_min` | 内容**非空行**数下限 | `path` + `value` |
| `content_min_chars` | 内容**字符数**下限 | `path` + `value` |
| `content_format_is` | 文件**格式**等于给定格式 | `path` + `value` |

```bash
mas run --workspace ./my-project --goal "出一份 PDF 报告" \
  --criteria 'content_format_is:out/report.pdf::pdf' \
  --criteria 'content_contains:out/report.pdf::结论'
```

**格式按 magic bytes 判定**，扩展名只做兜底 —— 扩展名会撒谎，
`.txt` 里装的是 PDF，那它就是 PDF。支持的格式：`pdf` / `docx` / `xlsx` /
`pptx` / `zip` / `png` / `jpeg` / `gif` / `bmp` / `tiff` / `webp` /
`wav` / 文本类。

**读不出内容 = 不通过**（不是「无法判定」）。这是这一版最要紧的一条：
判「无法判定」的话，这条标准会**回到模型手里**，而模型说一句
「looks fine」就把它关上了 —— **没人查过的标准被关上，比不闭合更糟**。

### 统一资源索引与多格式预览（v0.7.71 起）：一个文件夹就是一份索引

```bash
mas files                  # 索引这台机器上所有工作区
mas files ./out            # 索引一个文件夹
mas preview ./out/report.pdf   # 预览一个文件
```

```bash
$ mas files ./out

[./out]  5 个文件  263.7 KB
    pdf        1 个
    image      2 个
    model      1 个
      836.0 B  pdf        report.pdf  pages 2、text chars 57
      327.0 B  image      shot.png  width 12、height 7
      117.0 B  image      liar.txt  width 4、height 4
      213.0 B  model      ascii.stl  triangles 2
      251.0 B  zip        bundle.zip  members 2
```

**格式按文件自己的头判定，不看名字** —— 上面的 `liar.txt` 其实是一张 PNG，
所以它报 `image`。**读不开的文件会列出来并写明原因**（那一行 ⚠ 是信息，
不是噪声：交付物中间有一个读不开的文件，恰恰是读者最该看见的东西）。

`mas preview` 把 PDF 的字从**压缩流**里取出来、把 Word 的字从 **zip 成员**里
剥掉标记取出来；图片没有正文时**明确说「没有可预览的正文」**，而不是给你一个空白屏幕。
文件不存在或传了目录 → **退出码 2**。

[MOKI 资料库](https://github.com/JKZeng-cell/moki-library-for-dsh) 的分工对照）。

### 草稿层（v0.7.72 起）：改动先进草稿，人确认后才写回原文件

```bash
mas drafts                              # 看有哪些草稿在等
mas drafts show D-1a2b3c4d              # 看这一份的 diff
mas drafts approve D-1a2b3c4d           # 批准：写回原文件
mas drafts reject  D-1a2b3c4d           # 驳回：原样不动
mas drafts token                        # 拿人类令牌（agent 批不了自己的草稿）
mas drafts ticket D-1a2b3c4d --token <人类令牌>   # 签一张只管这一个草稿、用一次就作废的票据
mas drafts conflict                           # 查哪些草稿的文件在等待期间被改过
mas drafts approve D-1a2b3c4d --force           # 明知文件被改过，仍要写回
```

一次运行想改一个**已经存在**的文件时，它**不再直接覆盖**：
改动先进草稿，**原文件一个字节都不动**，草稿带一份**可读的 diff**，
你说「批准」才写回，你说「驳回」就**一个字都不改**。

```bash
$ mas drafts

工作区 ~/mas/artifacts：1 个草稿
  D-1a2b3c4d  pending  notes.txt  有改动
        理由：the loop proposed a change to an existing file
```

**新建文件照常直接写** —— 一个还不存在的文件，没有东西可以毁掉。
想回到旧行为，把配置里的 `edit_policy` 改成 `"overwrite"`（默认 `"draft"`）。

**机检读的是草稿里的新字节**，不是磁盘上的旧文件 —— 否则循环会陷入
「提改动 → 读旧文件 → 判不通过 → 再提改动」的死结，**永远闭不上**。
草稿和它改的文件**住在同一个工作区**（`.mas-drafts/`），文件夹被复制时
草稿跟着走 —— 丢掉的草稿，是一份**永远没法被人审阅**的改动。

### agent 经 MCP 提草稿（v0.7.73 起）：提议和批准分成两个动作

`mas drafts` 是**人**的那一半。MCP 上还有**一半给 agent**，
但两半**不是同一件事**：

```bash
# 人在自己的机器上拿令牌（一次就够）
mas drafts token
```

agent 侧的 MCP 工具：

| 工具 | 做什么 | 能不能改文件 |
|---|---|---|
| `mas_draft_stage` | **提**一份改动（带 diff 和理由） | **不能** —— 原文件一个字节都不动 |
| `mas_drafts` | 看有哪些草稿、看某一份的 diff | 不能 |
| `mas_draft_resolve` | 批准或驳回 | **要人类令牌** |
| `mas_files` | 索引工作区 | 只读 |
| `mas_preview` | 预览一个文件 | 只读 |

**agent 提的草稿，agent 自己批不了。** 令牌不对、空令牌、没令牌，
一律拒绝，而且**原文件不动**。
令牌的作用**不是保密，是分权** —— 提议的人不确认自己提的东西。

```bash
# agent 提了一个改动（文件没变）
mas_draft_stage {path: "notes.txt", content: "改过的正文", reason: "补一句结论"}

# agent 想自己批 —— 被拒
mas_draft_resolve {action: "approve", draft_id: "D-1a2b3c4d"}
-> {error: "human_token_required"}

# 人批 —— 才写回
mas_draft_resolve {action: "approve", draft_id: "D-1a2b3c4d", token: "<人类令牌>"}
```

详见 **[docs/drafts.md](docs/drafts.md)**（含与
[MOKI 资料库](https://github.com/JKZeng-cell/moki-library-for-dsh) 的分工对照：
MOKI 管**交互层**（`Alt+D`），本项目管**引擎层**（循环跑出来的东西），
**规则是同一条**）。

### 写二进制交付物（v0.7.70 起）：worker 怎么产出那个 PDF

内容级机检要读得进 PDF，**前提是有一个 PDF 存在**。写文件协议
（v0.7.15）原本只能带**文字**，所以交付物是 PDF 的任务**没法产出 PDF**。

现在写块可以带 **`encoding`** 属性：

```
<<<MAS:FILE path="out/report.pdf" encoding="base64">>>
JVBERi0xLjQK...
<<<MAS:END FILE>>>
```

引擎把块里的内容**解码成真正的二进制**再落盘，之后内容级机检就能读它。

| 情况 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `encoding="base64"` | **解码成二进制**再写 |
| 不写 `encoding` | **按 UTF-8 文本写**（旧行为不变） |
| `encoding="rot13"` 等**不认识**的编码 | **拒绝**，并说明原因 |
| base64 **解不出来** | **拒绝**，并说明原因（不留半截文件） |

**base64 严格解码。** 宽松解码会把**不在字母表里的字符全丢掉**，
于是一段纯胡话被解成**一个空文件**、一声不吭 —— worker 要一份 PDF，
工作区里躺着一个**零字节的 PDF**。宁可拒绝。

**模板块不是请求。** 二进制模板里写着 `out/report.pdf`，看着像个真路径；
靠**路径**认不出模板（任务真可能就要写这个文件），所以改用**正文**认。

```bash
mas run --workspace ./my-project --goal "写一份调研报告" \
  --criteria 'file_exists:out/report.md' \
  --criteria 'file_contains:out/report.md::结论'
```

判定口径：**文件缺失 = 不通过**（不是「无法判定」）；路径越界 = 开跑前拒绝；
参数写漏 = 开跑前拒绝；路径合法但读不出结论 = `unjudged`。
单文件读取上限 8 MiB。**内容级机检读不出内容时判「不通过」**，理由同上。worker 用**写文件协议**（`<<<MAS:FILE path="...">>>` 围栏块）
把内容真的写进工作区，写入进账本可查。完整说明见 [`docs/file-checks.md`](docs/file-checks.md)。



**参数写漏了 = 标准作废，不是标准通过。** 规则缺参数时不可能判出任何结论，
所以引擎会在**开跑前**直接报错（退出码 1，不消耗任何 token），而不是让它恒真通过：

| 类型 | 必须提供 | 非法示例 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contains` / `not_contains` | 非空字符串，或非空字符串数组 | `""`、`[]` |
| `min_chars` / `max_chars` / `lines_min` | 非负整数 | 缺失、`-1`、`"很多"` |
| `regex` | 能编译的正则 | `""`、`"([未闭合"` |
| `section` | 标题文本 | `""` |
| `json_keys` | 键名或非空键数组 | `[]`、缺失 |

**简写形式的坏参数同样快速失败。** `--criteria 'regex:'`、`--criteria 'min_chars:many'`
不会退回成纯描述——它们保留机检类型，然后被上面那张表拦下，退出码 1、零 token。
同一份标准，JSON 形式和简写形式待遇一致：写漏了就是写漏了，不会偷偷变成"交给模型判"。

**评审的判定要"读"出来，不是靠真值转换。** 模型如果回 `"pass": "false"`，
`bool("false")` 是 `True`——一条刚被判定为不通过的标准会被当成通过。引擎读的是
这个值的**含义**：`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` 是不通过，`"true"` / `"1"` / `"yes"` 是通过，
读不懂（`"maybe"`、空、缺失）就算**未判定**，绝不猜。

**类型名写错也不放过。** JSON 形式里写了一个不存在的类型（如
`{"check":{"type":"mystery"}}`），引擎同样在开跑前拒绝，并列出所有已知类型——
一个写错的类型名，如果放行，就会退化成"交给模型判"，模型说"看起来没问题"就闭合了。

只有**简写形式**里类型名本身不存在（`--criteria 'unknown_type:abc'`）才退回成纯描述——
那是压根没打算写机检，区别于"想写机检但写错了"。

### 简写写法（v0.4.2 起）

机检规则不必每次都写成 JSON。命令行可以直接用 `<类型>:<参数>`：

```bash
mas run --goal "写一个去重函数" \
  --criteria 'regex:(?s)def dedupe.*set' \
  --criteria 'min_chars:200' \
  --criteria 'contains:关键结论'
```

**一次写多条标准**，直接给 JSON 数组——数组里的每一条都带上自己的机检规则跑，
不会被当成一条纯文本描述（那样机检就一次都没跑过，闭合其实来自模型的"看起来没问题"）：

```bash
mas run --goal "写一份 v0.1.0 的发布说明" \
  --criteria '[{"id":"c1","desc":"包含版本号","check":{"type":"contains","arg":"v0.1.0"}},
               {"id":"c2","desc":"不少于 200 字","check":{"type":"min_chars","arg":200}}]'
```

简写与 JSON 形式完全等价，判定同样来自引擎的确定性检查器（账本里记为 `source: rule`）。
简写解析在引擎层生效，所以从 MCP、HTTP 或账本重放进来的标准也会被同样处理。
未知的类型前缀（例如 `写清楚就好`）仍然按普通描述处理，不会被误当成机检规则。
参数不是整数的数字类前缀（例如 `min_chars:很多`）同样退回普通描述——标准宁可没有机检，也不能声称自己能检查却做不到。

没有机检规则的标准会交给模型验证者判定；但**如果模型没给出判定，默认判不通过**（`unjudged`），不会因为一句「看起来可以」就放行。
`"required": false` 的标准**只记录、不阻塞闭合**：它有机检规则时照常跑机检，结果原样写进报告（过了是 `PASS`，没过是 `FAIL`），但不会让循环一直不闭合；它没有机检规则时由模型判定，判定结果同样只作记录。

**`required` 标志读的是含义，不是真值。** 写 `"required": "false"`（字符串）**确实**表示可选——
`bool("false")` 是 `True`，而这条标准一旦通过 JSON、MCP 或 shell 传进来，很容易就带上引号；
引擎读的是这个值的含义：`"false"` / `"0"` / `"no"` 是可选，`"true"` / `"1"` / `"yes"` 是必选，
读不懂（`"maybe"`、缺失、`null`）一律按**必选**处理——读不懂的标志绝不能悄悄把标准放宽。

> v0.4.2 起，验证者漏判某条标准时，引擎会在**同一轮内**就缺失的标准追问一次，
> 而不是重新生成整份交付物、白白消耗一整轮迭代。追问仍无答案才按 `unjudged` 记为不通过。

## 并行多智能体：让候选互相竞争

一个 worker 只会产出**一种**解法。v0.2 让多个 worker 带着**不同视角**并行产出候选，由引擎按机检结果选优：

```bash
# 单次任务临时加力，不改配置
mas run --goal "..." --criteria-file criteria.json \
  --parallel 3 --perspective thorough \
  --reviewers 3 --review-mode majority

mas init --wizard    # 交互式配置，第 7 题设并行数、第 8 题设评审数、第 11 题设回退链
```

| 旗标 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `--parallel N` | 并行候选数（N>1 时并发产出多个视角，引擎按机检通过数选优） |
| `--perspective` | 候选视角锚点：`direct` / `thorough` / `concise` / `structured` / `example_first` / `risk_first` |
| `--reviewers N` | 独立评审者数量（N>1 时启用对抗评审聚合） |
| `--review-mode` | 多评审聚合规则：`all`（全票通过）/ `majority`（过半）/ `any`（任一） |

或者直接改配置：

```json
{
  "orchestration": {
    "parallel_workers": 3,
    "reviewers": 3,
    "review_mode": "all"
  }
}
```

| 配置 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| `parallel_workers` | 并行产出的候选数。视角依次为 direct / thorough / concise / structured / example_first / risk_first，**不是同一段提示词的 N 次采样**。 |
| `reviewers` | 独立验证者数量。视角依次为 strict / skeptic / completeness / reader。 |
| `review_mode` | `all` 一票否决（全通过才算通过）/ `majority` 多数通过 / `any` 任一通过。 |

**选优规则是确定性的**：先看机检通过项数，再看产物体积，最后按下标定序。同一份配置跑两次，选中的一定是同一个候选 —— 这让回放可信。

**机检永远压过模型判断**：有 `check` 的标准由规则决定，只有没有机检的标准才交给评审共识。评审说「通过」不能覆盖规则说「不通过」。

**默认就是 v0.1 的行为**：`parallel_workers: 1`、`reviewers: 1` 时，路径与 v0.1 完全一致。

## 多后端故障转移

一个端点返回 502 就让整条循环死掉，那不叫闭环，叫宕机。配置多个后备端点，主端点失败自动切换：

```json
{
  "provider": "openai_compat",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "base_url": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
  "fallbacks": [
    { "provider": "anthropic", "model": "claude-sonnet-4-5", "base_url": "https://api.anthropic.com" },
    { "provider": "openai_compat", "model": "kimi-k2", "base_url": "https://api.moonshot.cn/v1" }
  ]
}
```

每个后备端点都会记录自己实际接了哪一次调用（`provider_used` / `model_used`）。全部失败才会报错。

## 远程接入：HTTP + SSE

stdio 传输给本地 Agent 用；HTTP/SSE 传输让运行时能被远程客户端、浏览器面板或 CI 任务访问：

```bash
mas http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765
```

| 路由 | 方法 | 用途 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/health` | GET | 存活检查 + 版本 |
| `/tools` | GET | 工具清单 |
| `/call` | POST | 调用任一工具，JSON 进 JSON 出 |
| `/events` | GET | SSE 事件流，实时推送账本增长 |

```bash
# 免鉴权（仅限本机访问）
curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/health
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/call \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tool":"mas_run","arguments":{"goal":"写一份发布说明","criteria":[]}}'
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8765/events
```

### 鉴权（对外暴露时必做）

`/call` 能执行任务、读账本，`/events` 能持续推送账本内容 —— 所以从 **v0.4.8** 起，HTTP 传输**内置鉴权**：

```bash
export MAS_HTTP_TOKEN=$(python -c "import secrets;print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")
mas http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765
```

设了 `MAS_HTTP_TOKEN` 之后，除 `/health` 外的所有路由都需要令牌：

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAS_HTTP_TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8765/tools
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAS_HTTP_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tool":"mas_status","arguments":{}}'
```

也可以用 `X-MAS-Token: <token>` 请求头代替 `Authorization`。

**fail-closed**：绑定到非本机地址（`0.0.0.0` / 局域网 IP）却**没有**令牌时，服务器**拒绝启动**（退出码 `2`）—— 环境变量写错不应该变成公网裸奔。开启鉴权后 CORS 也不再回 `*`，而是钉到 `http://127.0.0.1`，避免任意网页跨站调用。


### 常驻部署实战（服务 + TLS 反代）

真正要长期给手机 / 其它设备用，推荐这个组合 —— **服务只绑本机，对外只暴露 TLS 入口**：

```bash
# 1. 令牌落在文件里，不进版本库、不进启动脚本
python -c "import secrets,pathlib;pathlib.Path.home().joinpath('.mas/http_token.txt').write_text(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"

# 2. 服务常驻（示例：Linux systemd / Windows 启动文件夹 / macOS launchd 均可）
export MAS_HTTP_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.mas/http_token.txt)
mas http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8768

# 3. 只把 TLS 入口反代出去（tailnet 内；--https 需要 tailscale serve 权限）
tailscale serve --bg --https=8768 http://127.0.0.1:8768
```

手机 / 其它设备访问 `https://<your-host>:<port>/tools`，带上 `Authorization: Bearer <令牌>`。

要点：

- 服务绑 `127.0.0.1` + TLS 反代，比直接 `--host 0.0.0.0` 安全得多（不暴露在局域网，也由反代统一处理 TLS）。
- 令牌与启动脚本**分离**：脚本里不写明文，令牌文件缺失就报错退出，绝不退化成无鉴权启动。
- `tailscale serve` 默认是 **tailnet only**；`funnel` 会暴露到公网，属于扩大暴露范围，请自行评估后再开。
- 停用：`tailscale serve --https=8768 off`。

## 四道止损机制

1. **迭代预算**：`budget.max_iterations`，超出即 `budget_exhausted`。
2. **墙钟预算**：`budget.deadline_sec`。
3. **token 预算**：`budget.max_tokens`。
4. **停滞检测**：连续多轮产出**完全相同**的产物（默认 3 次，`stagnation_limit`）→ 判定卡死，**升级人工工单**，不再空转。

升级出来的工单带齐上下文（目标、验收标准、最后一版产物、失败原因、迭代历史），人工一句话就能接着跑：

```bash
mas tickets
mas resume T-20261111-085346-4396 --note "按用户口径重写结论段"
```

## 接入你自己的模型

运行时只用标准库，HTTP 走 `urllib`，所以任何 OpenAI 兼容端点都能接。

```bash
# Kimi / Moonshot
mas init --provider openai_compat --model kimi-k2 --base-url https://api.moonshot.cn/v1
export MAS_API_KEY=sk-...

# Claude
mas init --provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-5
export MAS_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

# GPT / Grok / DeepSeek / Qwen / 本地 vLLM 等，OpenAI 兼容即可
mas init --provider openai_compat --model gpt-4o-mini --base-url https://api.openai.com/v1
```

适配器自带三种容错，兼容绝大多数「OpenAI 兼容」网关：

- 网关不支持 `response_format` 时自动降级重试一次，并从回答正文里抽取 JSON；
- 网关用 SSE 事件流回答（很多中转站和本地桥接都是这样）时自动折叠成标准 chat 结构；
- 网关用 Responses 事件流回答（Codex 桥接、OpenMausBot 这类运行时）时同样折叠；
- 网关只认 `input` 不认 `messages` 时也能工作 —— 请求同时带两份，二选一被读取；
- 回答是内容块数组而不是字符串时，自动拼成纯文本；
- usage 字段名在 `prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens` 两套之间自动归一，缺 `total_tokens` 时回填；
- 模型在正文前吐 `<think>` 思维链时自动剥离，思维链不会进入交付物、判定和账本。

装完之后跑一次握手，看你的端点到底说哪种方言：

```bash
mas doctor
# [OK  ] endpoint       端点可用，协议方言 = openai-responses-events
```

也可以完全用环境变量，不改配置文件：

```bash
export MAS_PROVIDER=openai_compat MAS_MODEL=your-model MAS_BASE_URL=https://... MAS_API_KEY=...
```

### 让 DSH 真的能说话：`mas relay`

装上插件不等于模型能用。DSH 的 `dsh-llm-pi-ai` 适配器**坚持要一个 API key**，
而私有端点常常**不要 key**（甚至会因为占位 key 直接 `401`）——这是协议契约和
端点契约打架。`mas relay` 插在中间：丢弃客户端的 `Authorization`，按需换成上游真 key。

```powershell
# 一键生成能跑的 DSH profile（写配置 + 装插件 + 打印命令）
python tools/setup_dsh_bridge.py --profile masbridge --relay-port 8766

# 终端 1
mas relay --upstream http://127.0.0.1:16024 --port 8766

# 终端 2：pi-ai 坚持要 key，给个占位值即可（relay 会丢弃它）
$env:MAS_BRIDGE_API_KEY = "placeholder"
dsh --profile masbridge headless "用 mas_run 跑一个闭环：目标是写一份发布说明，验收标准用 file_exists 要求 out/report.md 存在"
```

> **`headless` 是 profile 名，不是子命令。** 正确形态是 `dsh --profile <name> headless "<task>"`。

中继的两种鉴权模式、安全边界、已验证/未验证清单见 **[docs/relay.md](docs/relay.md)**。

### 同宿主并列插件：MOKI 资料库

[MOKI](https://github.com/JKZeng-cell/moki-library-for-dsh)（`dsh-moki-library`）是
**另一个项目**，别和 OpenMausBot 混：它给 DeepSeek Harness 加一个**本地资源管理器**——
文件/网页链接统一整理、多格式预览、选区 `Alt+D` 唤起 AI 对话、**修改先进草稿、
用户确认后才写回原文件**。

分工很清楚：**MOKI 负责把资料整理成可交付的产物，MAS 负责判定这份产物到底过不过。**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add "dsh-moki-library@file:<绝对路径>/dsh-moki-library-0.1.73.tgz" --allow-build=sharp
dsh plugin --profile web add "dsh-openloop-mas@file:<绝对路径>/dsh-openloop-mas-0.7.16.tgz"
```

> MOKI 需要 **DSH >= 0.2.2-rc.1**、**Node >= 22.19**，且是 **web-platform 插件**——
> 在 CLI / headless profile 里会一直 pending（宿主形态不对，不是装坏了）。

```
├─ install.sh           macOS / Linux 一键安装
└─ docs/                架构、方法论、MCP、定位说明
```

## 命令速查

```bash
mas install       # 装 skills + 注册 MCP 服务器
mas sync          # 把已安装的 skills 同步回包内版本（修复漂移）
mas uninstall     # 移除 skills + MCP 注册（保留账本）
mas init          # 生成/更新配置
mas init --wizard # 交互式向导，一步步配好
mas run           # 跑一个闭环任务
mas demo          # 离线演示三个闭环场景
mas verify        # 跑一次真实闭环自检
mas bench         # 离线基准测试
mas status        # 本机状态
mas ledger        # 闭环账本
mas ledger --undone   # 只看被撤销过的那几条批准
mas undos        # 哪些批准被撤回了：配对 + 改了多少行
mas report        # 闭环复盘报告（Markdown）
mas replay        # 回放运行轨迹
mas export        # 导出账本为 Markdown 表格
mas tickets       # 人工工单
mas resume ID     # 带人工意见继续
mas teams         # 团队模板
mas doctor        # 安装自检
mas selftest      # 隔失门禁：重复打磈易偶发的路径（离线）
mas clean --selftest-ledger   # 清理旧版自检留下的账本污染（先 --dry-run 看）
mas files        # 索引工作区：每个文件是什么格式、能读出什么
mas preview FILE # 预览一个文件（PDF / Word / 文本…）
mas drafts       # 待确认的草稿：list / show / approve / reject / undo / token / ticket / conflict
mas drafts token # 拿人类令牌：agent 提的草稿，agent 自己批不了
mas drafts ticket D-ID --token <令牌>  # 签一张只管一个草稿、用一次就作废、15 分钟过期的票据
mas serve         # 以 MCP stdio 服务运行
mas http          # 以 HTTP + SSE 运行（远程接入；对外部署请设 MAS_HTTP_TOKEN）
mas relay         # OpenAI 兼容中继：给「非要 API Key」的客户端用（默认 127.0.0.1:8766）
```

`mas run` 退出码：`0` = 闭合，`2` = 未闭合（升级或预算耗尽）。CI 里可以直接当门禁用。

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # hindsight-coding-agents Long-term project memory for **coding agents**, backed by [Hindsight](https://vectorize.io/hindsight). One package, several agents: a shared reflect-and-inject core with a thin entry point per agent (**Claude Code**, **Codex CLI**, **DeepAgents Dcode**, **opencode**, **opencode 2**, **Kilo CLI**, **Cursor CLI**, **GitHub Copilot CLI**, **Grok Build**, **Qwen Code**, **Kimi Code**, **Factory Droid**, **ZCode**, **TraeCode**, **Antigravity CLI**, **Devin CLI**, **Cline CLI**, **pi**, **Prime Agent**, **DeepSeek Harness**, **WorkBuddy**, **CodeBuddy**). Ingestion is fully automatic — there is no setup command: a repo's git history and conversations flow into its memory bank in the background as you work. The premise: most of a real fix is derivable from the code, but the _last mile_ often hinges on a project-specific decision that isn't in the code at all — a rounding rule, a retry allowlist, a tie-break policy. Those decisions live in git history and past conversations. This package puts them in front of the agent at the moment it starts working, and keeps a curated set of **pages** (architecture, conventions, in-flight initiatives) that future sessions start from. The agent reads those pages through the `hindsight_search_pages`, `hindsight_list_pages` and `hindsight_read_page` tools. Before the rename they were `hindsight_search_knowledge_pages`, `hindsight_list_knowledge_pages` and `hindsight_read_knowledge_page`: a permission rule in your agent's own settings that names an old tool needs the new name. [View Changelog →](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/changelog/integrations/coding-agents) ## Does it work? [AMB's sdebench](https://agentmemorybenchmark.ai/dataset/sdebench) is the measurement: a coding agent over 61 real repository tasks, three runs each, with and without memory. Accuracy is not what moves — every run solves 60–61 of the 61 either way. These are tasks a good agent can already do. What memory changes is how much it costs you to get there: how often you have to stop and correct the agent, and what the tokens cost. | Agent | Corrections / task | Cost / task | | ----------- | ------------------ | ------------------- | | Claude Code | 0.85 → **0.36** | $0.445 → **$0.338** | | Codex CLI | 1.34 → **0.47** | $0.577 → **$0.276** | | opencode | 1.20 → **0.80** | $0.634 → **$0.553** | No memory → with Hindsight, mean of 3 runs. Corrections reproduce the labels AMB prints on its own chart; cost is derived from the same per-run table. Both numbers move together, and that is the mechanism rather than a coincidence. A correction is a round trip: the agent guesses a project-specific decision wrong, you stop it, you explain, it redoes the work. Every one of those costs a turn of tokens and a turn of your attention. Handing the agent the decision _before_ it starts — the rounding rule, the retry allowlist, the tie-break policy that was settled in a commit message or a conversation months ago — removes the guess, and the round trip with it. ## Install ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install all # every detected agent, wired natively npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code # or just one npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents uninstall all # removes exactly what install added npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents update # refresh the runtime only, no rewiring npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents stats # how often each agent uses Hindsight ``` `install` takes an explicit target — `all`, or one or more harness names. A bare `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install` changes nothing and prints the choice, so wiring every agent on the machine is never something that happens by accident. **Updating is the same `install` command again** — it re-copies the runtime in place. Day to day you should not have to: once a day, a session start checks npm and re-stages a newer runtime in the background (`autoUpdate`, on by default — set it to `false` to pin the version you have). It only replaces a runtime that `npx` installed: a copy from `npm i -g`, a project dependency or a local checkout is left alone. Running `update` or `install` yourself is different — it re-stages the published release over whatever is installed, a local build included. `update` refreshes the copy every wired agent already points at and deliberately touches no host config; re-run `install` yourself after a release that adds a new hook, or to wire another agent. On a terminal it also asks **where memory should live** — Hindsight Cloud, a server you run, or a local daemon on this machine (see [Where memory lives](#where-memory-lives)). Scripted installs pass `--server cloud|self-hosted|daemon` instead; it is asked only once, and never again on re-install. ### Per agent Same command, only the harness name changes. Run after installing the package globally. #### Claude Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code ``` 3 hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json`, MCP via `claude mcp add` (user scope), and the companion skill. #### Codex CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install codex ``` 3 hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` plus `[mcp_servers]` in `config.toml` (needs `codex_hooks = true`). #### DeepAgents Dcode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install dcode ``` The installer registers this package as a local marketplace with Dcode, then invokes Dcode's own `plugin install` command. The package is a native Agent Plugin: its root `plugin.json` contributes the shared skill, the Hooks V2 `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, and `Stop` lifecycle, and the namespaced `hindsight_*` MCP server. Enable the plugin through Dcode's normal plugin manager; no Dcode config patcher or compatibility bridge is required. Dcode namespaces a plugin's MCP tools, so they appear as `plugin__hindsight-coding-…__hindsight_…` rather than under their bare names — the agent resolves them from the tool guide either way. In headless runs (`dcode -n`) Dcode allows the read-only Hindsight tools and gates the two that write (`hindsight_ingest_document`, `hindsight_capture_initiative`) behind an approval it has no UI for; use the interactive TUI to capture an initiative or ingest a document. For the same reason Dcode gets no one-time codebase survey: the survey runs only under the current agent's own CLI, and only Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and opencode v1 have a headless, read-only recipe for it. #### opencode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install opencode ``` A plugin entry in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — native tools, no MCP needed. #### opencode 2 ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install opencode2 ``` opencode v2 (`npm @opencode/cli`) exposes an `opencode2` binary alias **alongside** `opencode` and rewrote the plugin API, so it is a harness of its own. It writes the same plugin entry to the same `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — the two CLIs share that file, and v1 rejects the whole config if it sees v2's `plugins` key — and each CLI then loads its own entry point from the one registered path. So installing either harness wires both, and uninstalling either removes the shared entry. Two differences from v1, both because of the host: there is no one-time codebase survey (v2 plugins cannot define the read-only agent the survey needs, and the survey never borrows another agent's CLI), and the seed banner is written to the plugin log instead of a TUI toast (v2 plugins cannot raise one). Recall, injection, the native `hindsight_*` tools and session write-back are identical. The companion skill is identical too, but it is registered in memory through v2's skill API rather than copied into a skills directory — opencode2 has none of its own, and the two it reads belong to other agents. #### Kilo CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install kilo ``` A plugin entry in `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json[c]`. #### Cursor CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install cursor-cli ``` Hooks in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, and the companion skill. #### GitHub Copilot CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install copilot-cli ``` `~/.copilot/hooks/`, `mcp-config.json`, and the companion skill. #### Grok Build ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install grok-build ``` Native hooks in `~/.grok/hooks/hindsight.json`, MCP in `~/.grok/config.toml`, plus the companion skill. Grok also runs Claude Code's hooks from `~/.claude/settings.json`; those stay silent inside Grok, so a machine wired for both hosts records each Grok session once. Grok passes hook context to the model only from tool hooks, so the session and prompt context arrive with the result of the agent's first tool call after each prompt (a `PostToolUse` hook). #### Qwen Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install qwen-code ``` Native hooks in `~/.qwen/settings.json`, plus MCP and the companion skill. > Qwen's hook `timeout` is in **milliseconds** (its own docs: "Timeout in milliseconds, default > 60000"), unlike every other supported agent, so the installed values are `30000/30000/60000`. > Recall fires on genuine submissions only — `UserPromptSubmit` also fires on tool-result > continuations, so interactive sessions recall once per prompt while headless (`qwen -p`), > `serve`, SDK and ACP sessions seed and retain but do not recall. #### Kimi Code ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install kimi-code ``` Native hooks in `~/.kimi-code/config.toml`, plus MCP in `~/.kimi-code/mcp.json` and the companion skill. (Hooks and MCP go under `$KIMI_CODE_HOME` instead when it is set.) > Kimi's SessionStart hook cannot reach the model, so the session briefing is silent there; > recalled memory arrives on the first prompt instead, as a `` block. Sessions are > retained from every agent's `wire.jsonl` under the session directory, subagents included. #### Factory Droid ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install factory-droid ``` 4 hook registrations in `~/.factory/hooks.json` (user scope), including a cancellation-safe `Notification` write-back, plus a stdio MCP registration under `mcpServers.hindsight` in `~/.factory/mcp.json`, and the companion skill in `~/.factory/skills`. The installer touches only JSON files - no Droid CLI round-trip - and refuses to overwrite a user-managed MCP server already named `hindsight`. Droid's hook protocol matches Claude Code's (`session_id`/`transcript_path`/`cwd` in, `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` out). Recall and injection use the same protocol; write-back also handles Droid's cancellation notification because Droid does not emit `Stop` after a cancelled turn. #### ZCode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install zcode ``` Three hook registrations plus a stdio MCP server under `mcp.servers.hindsight`, both in ZCode's own CLI config `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` - never your real Claude Code settings, even though ZCode embeds the Claude Code agent runtime and speaks its hook protocol. The companion skill goes to `~/.zcode/skills`. Config hooks ship **disabled**, so the installer also sets `hooks.enabled` to `true`; `uninstall` removes the whole block again when nothing else is registered there, and refuses to touch an MCP server named `hindsight` that it did not write. > ZCode's hook `timeoutMs` is in **milliseconds** (installed values `30000/30000/60000`), and > `hooks.maxOutputBytes` caps what a hook may print - anything larger is dropped, injection and > all. The installer seeds it at `32768` only when your config does not already set one. > > ZCode keeps no durable session transcript: `Stop` carries the reply plus a temp, assistant-only > file it deletes as soon as the hook returns, and no user prompt at all. So this is the one agent > whose conversation the plugin journals itself - the prompt hook records what you asked, the > `Stop` hook records the reply - and the write-back then behaves like every other agent's, > appending each new turn to the same session document. `--import-conversations` is therefore not > available for ZCode: there is no past history on disk to backfill from. #### TraeCode ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install traecode ``` Three hook registrations in TraeCode's user-level `hooks.json`, the companion skill under the same dot-dir's `skills/`, and two `filesystem.readWrite` rules in `sandbox.json` — one for `~/.hindsight`, without which the hooks fail silently (exit 0, no effect) because the sandbox blocks those writes, and one for Trae's per-window storage DBs (`/User/workspaceStorage`), which the SessionStart hook seeds with the workspace's MCP enable switch. Network is allowed by default. TRAE ships two editions with different brand roots — the CN build uses `~/.trae-cn` and "Trae CN", the international build `~/.trae` and "Trae" — so every path resolves by probing for the edition dir that exists and defaulting to the CN names. Plain JSON files, no CLI round-trip. TraeCode speaks Claude Code's hook protocol, so recall and injection work exactly as they do there; the event map lives under the top-level `hooks` key and the `version` field the host writes is preserved. MCP is registered per repo, never at the user level: Trae launches user-level servers with the Electron process's cwd (your home directory), where a hindsight entry either self-disables under `optInOnly` (zero tools) or resolves the home bank instead of the repo's. So the installer pre-seeds the per-repo registration for every repo opted in via `mapPathToBank` — a `mcpServers.hindsight` stdio server in `/.trae/mcp.json`, pinned to that repo via `HINDSIGHT_MCP_PROJECT_CWD` — migrates any stale user-level entry back out of `/User/mcp.json`, and seeds the per-workspace enable switch directly. The SessionStart hook re-checks both on every session and writes them only when missing or stale (idempotent fallback) — Trae's hook sandbox cannot be relied on to perform those writes itself. The per-repo file is merged not clobbered, and gitignored when the repo has a `.gitignore` (the path is machine-specific). A foreign `hindsight` entry — in either file — is the user's own server and is never touched. Trae only reads that per-repo file once the global `trae.mcp.enableWorkspaceMcp` setting is on (default off), so the installer handles the gate: an interactive run asks, a non-interactive run takes `--enable-workspace-mcp`, and either way the setting is written and Trae windows must be restarted to pick it up (declining, or a settings file with comments, prints the manual step). Registrations and enable switches take effect on the NEXT window, so the MCP tools appear when you reload after the first session; repos opted into `mapPathToBank` after install need one more `install traecode` run, and if a repo's server still shows disabled in the MCP panel, flip it on once there. > One manual step remains after install (UI state the installer cannot write): enable the hooks > under TraeCode Settings > Hooks. If you declined the workspace-MCP prompt, enable it later in > Trae settings (search "enableWorkspaceMcp"). > TraeCode keeps no readable session transcript - sessions live in an encrypted local DB or the > cloud. Like ZCode, its conversation is journaled by the plugin itself: the prompt hook records > what you asked, and the `Stop` hook closes the turn with the reply it carries in > `last_assistant_message`. `--import-conversations` is therefore not available for TraeCode: > there is no past history on disk to backfill from. #### Antigravity CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install agy ``` Lifecycle hooks, MCP, and the `Hindsight · ` status line. #### Devin CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install devin-cli ``` Hooks in `~/.config/devin/config.json` plus MCP. Needs Node 22.5+ — see below. #### Cline CLI ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install cline-cli ``` A native plugin via `cline plugin install`, plus MCP and the companion skill. #### pi ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install pi ``` An extension entry in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, plus the companion skill in `~/.pi/agent/skills` — native tools, no MCP needed. This command is the only supported route, for pi and for Prime Agent below. Installing us as a pi package (`pi install npm:@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`) is deliberately not wired: both hosts read the same `pi` key of a package's `package.json`, and that key can only name one entry — whichever host it did not name would load the other's bundle and report itself as the wrong agent, taking that harness's config section and stamping every document it retains with it. So the package carries no `pi` key at all, and each host is pointed at its own bundle by the install command above. #### Prime Agent ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install prime-agent ``` Prime Agent is a fork of pi, so it is wired the same way: an extension entry, here in `~/.prime/agent/settings.json`, plus the companion skill in `~/.prime/agent/skills` — native tools, no MCP needed. Installing both is fine and expected: each host loads its own entry from its own settings file, and like every other pair of agents they **share one bank per repo** (the default `coding-agent::{gitProject}`), so what you tell pi is there when you open Prime Agent. Separate entries are what keeps each side attributable — its own `harnesses.` config section, and its own agent stamped on every document it retains. #### DeepSeek Harness ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install dsh ``` A Cordis plugin row in `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh` by default), which every dsh profile composes — native tools, no MCP needed. Two dsh-specific notes: one dsh process serves **several repositories** (its Web UI opens each session in whatever directory you pick), so the bank is resolved per session workspace rather than once per process; and dsh has no plugin-facing notice channel, so the seed line goes to the plugin log rather than the UI. A **forked** session saves only the turns it adds after the fork — the part it inherited is already in the parent's conversation. Everything model-facing — recalled memory, the pages preamble, the `hindsight_*` tools — is unaffected. If you prefer the published-package route, `dsh plugin --profile web add @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` works too: the package ships the profile patch layer, so nothing else needs editing. Either route gets the companion skill — a plugin wired by the host's own plugin manager installs it itself on the first session, since that route never runs our installer. #### WorkBuddy ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install workbuddy ``` 3 hooks in `~/.workbuddy/settings.json`, the stdio MCP server in `~/.workbuddy/mcp.json`, and the companion skill in `~/.workbuddy/skills`. WorkBuddy (Tencent's AI workbench) is built on the shared `@genie/agent-cli` engine, so its hooks follow Claude Code's protocol — the main difference is the transcript schema (`type:"message"` records carrying top-level `role`/`content`), which the package's own reader normalizes. #### CodeBuddy ```bash npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install codebuddy ``` 3 hooks in `~/.codebuddy/settings.json`, the stdio MCP server in `~/.codebuddy/.mcp.json` — the recommended file: the installer follows CodeBuddy's documented fallback chain, merging into an existing deprecated `~/.codebuddy/mcp.json` or legacy `~/.codebuddy.json` rather than shadowing it — and the companion skill in `~/.codebuddy/skills`. CodeBuddy Code runs the same `@genie/agent-cli` engine as WorkBuddy — WorkBuddy merely ships it with a different home folder — so it reuses WorkBuddy's hook runtime, and differs only in the root it writes to. **Both CodeBuddy hosts are covered, and they do not store sessions alike.** CodeBuddy Code (the CLI) writes the WorkBuddy JSONL that the shared reader parses. The IDE hands the Stop hook its own per-conversation directory instead — `CodeBuddyIDE//history///`, whose `index.json` _is_ the `transcript_path` and whose prose sits one level down, in `messages/.json` — so the reader dispatches on the shape it was handed (core/transcript-codebuddy-ide.ts). Uninstall the same way: `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents uninstall claude-code` (or `uninstall all`). **Devin CLI needs Node 22.5 or newer.** Its hooks pass only a session id — the conversation itself lives in `~/.local/share/devin/cli/sessions.db` — so reading it depends on Node's built-in `node:sqlite`. Installing `devin-cli` checks for this first and refuses (with the reason) rather than wiring hooks that could never retain anything. Every other agent works on any supported Node. `install` copies what it needs into `~/.hindsight/coding-agents` and points each agent's wiring there, so nothing depends on where you ran it from. **Updating** is the same command again — it re-copies the runtime in place, leaving the wiring valid and every new session on the new version. `install` merges the native wiring (hooks + MCP registration where the host wants them) into each agent's own config, preserving everything already there; it is idempotent (re-run after moving the package) and backs up any pre-existing file it touches as `.hindsight-backup`. `uninstall` removes only our entries. On Claude Code the install also ships a **companion skill** (`~/.claude/skills/hindsight-coding-agent`) that teaches the agent how this memory works — what "store this in hindsight" should do, the tool surface, per-repo configuration, debugging — so users can ask the agent itself. Manual wiring per harness, if you prefer: **opencode** and **opencode 2** install directly — point `opencode.json` at the package dir: ```json { "plugin": ["/path/to/hindsight-coding-agents"] } ``` One entry, both CLIs: v1 resolves that directory through `package.json` `main`, v2 through its `index.js`, so each loads its own plugin. **Claude Code** and **Codex** get their full three-hook + MCP wiring from this package's own installer — `npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code` / `install codex`. This package's `bin` entries (`hindsight-claude-hook`, `hindsight-codex-hook`, `hindsight-cursor-hook`) are the individual injection-only `UserPromptSubmit` entrypoints for a minimal, hand-wired setup. Adding an agent: hook-based → write a `HookSpec` entry point (see `src/cursor-hook.ts`) and register a `hookAdapter` in `src/harness/registry.ts`; persistent-plugin → implement `HarnessAdapter` (`src/core/types.ts`) fully (see `src/harness/opencode.ts`), or bind the host's own plugin API to `RuntimeCore` directly when it is not an opencode fork (see `src/cline.ts`, `src/dsh.ts`). ## Migrating from the per-agent plugins The older per-agent integrations (`hindsight-claude-code`, `hindsight-cursor-cli`, `hindsight-codex`, …) are superseded by this package. Two things move; nothing else does. **Your server moves automatically.** If `~/.hindsight/claude-code.json` or `~/.hindsight/codex.json` exists, `install` adopts its endpoint — `hindsightApiUrl` → `apiUrl`, `hindsightApiToken` → `apiToken`, and an empty URL means the local daemon, as it did there. The agent you are installing is checked first, so wiring Codex takes Codex's server even if an old `claude-code.json` is still lying around. You already chose where your memory lives; defaulting to Cloud instead would quietly send your prompts somewhere else. Pass `--server` to override. (Those two are the only old plugins that shipped a user config — Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, opencode and Cline have no endpoint to carry.) **Your conversations are re-imported from local disk**, as new documents: ```bash cd /path/to/your/repo npx @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents install claude-code --import-conversations # or: install codex --import-conversations ``` This re-extracts the transcripts the agent already wrote, so it costs tokens roughly in proportion to the history imported, and it is safe to re-run (ingestion dedups by document id). Local transcripts are the source rather than the old bank, because the old bank cannot be split by repo. Its default was a **single static bank** — `dynamicBankId` defaults to false, so everything landed in one bank named `claude_code` — and its documents record only `retained_at`, `message_count` and `session_id`, nothing identifying the project. Working out which documents belong to which repo means joining `session_id` back to the `cwd` in the local transcript, so the transcripts are needed either way; going through them directly is simply the shorter path. **How sessions are matched.** A conversation is imported only when the session itself records the directory it ran in — never inferred from a file or folder name. Claude Code writes that directory on its entries, Codex in its `session_meta` header and DeepSeek Harness in its session-log header, and pi and Prime Agent in their session header, so all five can be attributed exactly, including sessions started in a subdirectory of the repo. Guessing was tempting (Claude names its history folders after the project path) but unsafe: `/` and `.` both encode to `-`, so `repo-sub` is either the subdirectory `repo/sub` or an unrelated sibling repo — and a wrong guess files someone else's conversation into your bank. Sessions that record nothing are skipped and the count is reported. DeepSeek Harness logs are Zstandard-framed JSONL under `$DSH_HOME/sessions`, which needs Node 22.15+ to read; an older Node skips the import with that reason rather than silently importing nothing. Dcode's transcripts record no directory at all — the working directory lives only in its LangGraph checkpoint database — so the repo comes from `dcode threads list --json`, a declared, versioned command contract rather than that internal schema; with the `dcode` CLI unavailable the import is skipped with that reason. The other harnesses (opencode, opencode 2, Kilo, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Devin) keep history in internal SQLite databases with unversioned schemas and are skipped with a reason. **Nothing else is translated.** The old plugin's behavioural settings — 12 `recall*`, 7 `retain*`, `bankMission`/`retainMission`, `dynamicBankGranularity` — describe a pipeline this package replaced, and reinterpreting them would be guesswork. Bank naming changes too: this package uses one bank per **repo** (`coding-agent::{gitProject}`) shared by every agent. To keep the old naming instead: ```jsonc { "bankIdTemplate": "{harness}::{gitProject}" } // reproduces the old per-agent naming ``` ## Where memory lives Three modes, chosen once when you install (`install` asks on a terminal; pass `--server` to script it): | mode | what runs | needs | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | `cloud` | Hindsight Cloud (default) | an API token | | `self-hosted` | a Hindsight server you already run | its URL | | `daemon` | a local `hindsight-embed` on this machine | `uv` on PATH + an LLM key for extraction
