evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Browser recording

`@local/dsh-browser-recording` adds agent tools for user-requested browser interaction recordings in DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`. It does not record your desktop or DSH itself, attach to your personal browser, or install any software. The `personal-web` recipe selects it; applying the recipe or restarting a retained profile requires separate approval.

Ask your agent to record a short browser demo and supply the starting URL. It uses:

- **`browser_recording_start`** — open an isolated browser at an HTTP(S) URL and start a 1280 × 720, 2× recording with a visible pointer.
- **`browser_recording_action`** — hover, click, fill/type, press an allowed key, move to `x,y`, scroll, wait for a selector, or read an accessibility snapshot. Actions include real curved pointer travel and visible typing; neighboring controls can be toured before the target.
- **`browser_recording_stop`** — close the browser, compact idle gaps, and export a silent H.264 MP4. Compacted clips up to 30 seconds also produce an infinitely looping animated WebP. Longer clips return MP4 only, with `loopSkipped: true`.
- **`browser_recording_discard`** — close the browser and delete temporary media without exporting. Previously exported files are not deleted.

## Prerequisites and execution world

On the machine selected by DSH's **subprocess provider**, preinstall Node.js, `agent-browser` (verified with `0.38.1`), Chromium, `ffmpeg` with `libx264` and `libwebp_anim`, and `ffprobe`. A working browser installation is required; the plugin never downloads one. Linux is verified. macOS has path handling but has not been tested; Windows is not supported. Chromium can come from `~/.agent-browser/browsers/chrome-*/chrome` or the execution environment's absolute `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` (including a path containing spaces).

Before creating a recording directory or launching a browser, the runner encodes tiny synthetic frames to check FFmpeg's `-fps_mode vfr` support with `libx264` and its `libwebp_anim` encoder. An executable that only answers `-version` is not sufficient. If this check fails, ask the execution-environment operator to provide compatible FFmpeg on `PATH`; the plugin does not install tools or use a legacy compatibility mode.

The Host sends a self-contained checked runner through DSH's managed subprocess stdin. Browser state, media encoding and file operations happen in that execution world; no same-named Host path is assumed. A remote provider therefore needs its own binaries, browser installation, working-directory mapping and process-lifetime support. This release is verified with DSH's local subprocess provider, not a remote provider.

The recorder uses a unique session and private temporary directory, ignores inherited agent-browser profile/CDP/provider configuration, and enables desktop hover capability through a task-owned Chromium launcher. It does not restore credentials or browser state from another session. It records only one session per DSH Session; overlap and cross-session access are rejected. Plugin/agent disposal, invocation cancellation and a two-minute lifetime deadline attempt to close the browser and discard temporary media. After abrupt Host/machine termination, automatic cleanup cannot be guaranteed; recordings do not resume, and leftover `dsh-browser-recording-*` temporary directories may need manual review/removal.

## Safety and delivery

**Recording captures visible content without automatic redaction.** Do not use it for login, passwords, OTPs, API keys, payment details or personal data. Password and declared OTP/payment autofill fields reject tool-driven typing, but that is not a general secret detector. Arbitrary JavaScript, browser CLI commands, uploads, clipboard reads and credential imports are not exposed. Tool arguments and page snapshots may enter DSH's normal session history. Browser text is untrusted data. Recording authorization does not authorize purchases, posting, sending messages or other external writes; the agent must obtain the normal approvals.

Exports live under the session working directory at `.dsh/artifacts/browser-recordings/<id>/recording.mp4` and `recording.loop.webp`. Treat these as sensitive runtime artifacts and keep `.dsh/` out of Git. Temporary raw media is removed after successful export. An export failure retains the stopped recording for another stop/export attempt or discard. No action is retried automatically; a failed click may already have taken effect.

The agent should inspect the recording, deliver the MP4 with DSH's native `present` tool, and use an ordinary Markdown image pointing to the WebP to show the loop in **Web DSH**. Native image-attachment normalization can turn animation into a still image, so the plugin deliberately returns session-filesystem paths instead. DSH Desktop's `dsh-app:` page does not support the same inline local-image route; deliver/open the file externally there. File delivery is not a durable byte copy: moving a session to another machine requires moving its recordings too.

## Development and validation

The package reuses the existing pinned DSH packages and root compiler; no browser or encoder is bundled. Follow the repository's dependency approval procedure.

- `node packages/dsh-browser-recording/scripts/build-host.mjs` strictly checks TypeScript and regenerates the committed host and self-contained runner.
- `node --test packages/dsh-browser-recording/test/*.test.mjs` checks publication freshness, controlled action inputs, compaction, native Cordis/tool registration, owner isolation, overlap, cancellation and disposal. Native registries are real; subprocess results are controlled fixtures. Included in root `pnpm test`.
- `node packages/dsh-browser-recording/test/recording-journey.mjs` is an explicit opt-in check requiring the preinstalled browser/media tools. It mounts the real plugin and local managed subprocess provider, records a disposable loopback page with no credentials or external calls, checks the changed DOM through a native accessibility snapshot, rejects password-field typing, and verifies animated WebP plus 2560 × 1440 silent MP4 output. Set `DSH_RECORDING_EVIDENCE` to an output directory to retain reviewable media. No paid model, production website, live profile or dependency installation is used.

The pointer/action-interval/compaction workflow follows the recorder used in Amp's `using-agent-browser` skill. This package owns its implementation and does not rely on an Amp installation or a server-synced skill path at runtime.

# DSH customizations

This private repository keeps DSH plugin bundles and reproducible profile recipes for one user across several computers. Clone it on each computer, then apply the profiles you need. DSH keeps credentials, sessions, settings, and other runtime state outside this repository.

The plugins target DSH **`0.2.2-rc.5` only**. Existing consumers can stay on their previous commit until their host operator upgrades the runtime and plugin graph together. **Full validation pending.** The published target still requires the RPC-owner patch; its ownership regression fails without the patch and passes with it. See the [migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md) for scope, evidence gaps, retained-state cautions, and deployment boundaries.

## Prerequisites

Install these tools before you use the repository:

- The checkout-local, patched DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` launcher installed by the frozen dependency command below (a global DSH installation is not upgraded or used by `apply`)
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- pnpm 11.9.0, already available locally (not an unverified downloader shim)

Before dependency work in any checkout or worktree, follow the [repository setup skill](.agents/skills/repository-setup/SKILL.md). It covers dependency ownership, pinned executable availability, offline cache limitations, and approval boundaries. You can read this Markdown directly without a plugin.

Set `DSH_HOME` before applying a profile if your Harness home is not `~/.dsh`.

### Amp orbs

The executable `.agents/setup` prepares fresh Amp orbs with Node.js 24.20.0 (matching CI), the manifest-pinned pnpm, frozen workspace dependencies, and the matching Playwright Chromium and system dependencies. It checks the repository and builds Session Environment. Node downloads are checksum-verified; toolchains stay under `~/.local/share/dsh-customizations-orb`, and a checkout-scoped login-shell hook makes them available to agents and supervised services.

Network provisioning is approved for this orb lifecycle script only. Dependency lifecycle scripts remain disabled; the release-age policy and required DSH patch remain enforced. Normal agent dependency work still follows the offline-first setup procedure above. Setup refuses symlinked dependency directories and never applies a profile, authenticates a user, or starts a persistent DSH host.

Amp snapshots successful setup for reuse by fresh project orbs. Exact snapshots skip setup; stale snapshots retain installed tools and caches while setup reconciles the current lockfile. Warm setup skips existing toolchain/browser downloads and checks system packages before invoking apt. `.agents/resume` only checks readiness and never reinstalls dependencies. These files must reach the project's default branch before future orbs can use them. The browser is suitable for interaction tests; an x64 orb is not the Linux ARM64 container used for visual baselines.

## Apply the starter profile

Before applying to retained state, complete target validation and the [host operator acceptance steps](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md#host-operator-acceptance-sequence), including backups and explicit deployment approval. The commands below are a procedure, not a report of a completed `0.2.2-rc.5` install or deployment.

The `personal-web` recipe selects the standard DSH base and Web bundles plus [Global Guidance](packages/dsh-global-guidance/README.md), [Session Environment](packages/dsh-session-environment/README.md), [OpenRouter](packages/dsh-openrouter/README.md), [Jev](packages/dsh-jev/README.md), [File Intuition](packages/dsh-file-intuition/README.md), [Session Recap](packages/dsh-session-recap/README.md), [Project Steward](packages/dsh-project-steward/README.md), [Product mode](packages/dsh-product-mode/README.md), [Dispatch](packages/dsh-dispatch/README.md), [Firecrawl](packages/dsh-web-firecrawl/README.md), [Google auth](packages/dsh-google-auth/README.md), [Google Drive](packages/dsh-google-drive/README.md), [GitHub](packages/dsh-github/README.md), [Linear](packages/dsh-linear/README.md), [Projects](packages/dsh-projects/README.md), [YouTube](packages/dsh-tool-youtube/README.md), [Image generation](packages/dsh-tool-imagegen/README.md), [Trivy](packages/dsh-tool-trivy/README.md), and [Browser recording](packages/dsh-browser-recording/README.md), targeting DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`. Configure the recap model and Firecrawl key through **Plugins → installed package → Configure** on the corresponding plugin row. Firecrawl replaces the profile's search/fetch providers; it requires a key before either web tool can run. Browser recording requires preinstalled browser/media tools in the subprocess execution environment and never records without an explicit user request.

Existing installations need a coordinated DSH and plugin upgrade, not a plugin-only restart on the old runtime. The host operator owns backups, legacy settings adoption, profile composition, and restart. No intermediate plugin release is required. After the upgrade, key changes take effect on the next request without a restart. Keys stay in DSH's credential store (or the launching environment), never in this repository.

1. After the setup procedure's ownership, executable, cache, and approval checks, install dependencies, validate the repository, and build Session Environment. If the offline install fails, stop; obtain separate approval for cache population rather than retrying online:

   ```sh
   pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
   pnpm run check
   pnpm run build
   ```

2. Preview the commands without changing DSH:

   ```sh
   pnpm run apply -- personal-web --dry-run
   ```

3. Apply and validate the profile:

   ```sh
   pnpm run apply -- personal-web
   ```

4. Start it:

   ```sh
   ./node_modules/.bin/dsh --profile personal-web
   ```

The apply command submits the selected bundles together in recipe order, using `file:` snapshots for local bundles. It does not remove bundles already installed but absent from the recipe. Existing bundle order is retained by DSH; inspect `--dump-config` after updates.

**Required RPC-owner compatibility patch:** the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection@0.2.2-rc.5` still needs [`dsh-client-connection-0.2.2-rc.5-rpc-owner.patch`](patches/dsh-client-connection-0.2.2-rc.5-rpc-owner.patch), which normalizes the consumer context with `getTraceable(this.ctx, this.ctx)`. The ownership regression fails against the unpatched target and passes with the patch; the installed target launcher graph also passes. Keep the target-version patch, pnpm 11 `patchedDependencies` in the [workspace policy](pnpm-workspace.yaml), and [lockfile](pnpm-lock.yaml) synchronized. See the [current migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md#required-rpc-owner-patch) for evidence and limitations.

The apply procedure verifies the checkout-local launcher and the required Connection implementation before writing a profile. The patch must reach each independent profile graph as well as the launcher graph. Preserve workspace YAML settings with a `.bak` backup, use exact target-version pins and narrow release-age exceptions, and resolve the complete profile graph offline with lifecycle scripts disabled. Refuse conflicting overrides and verify the profile's own Web/Connection resolution after the frozen install. Target-version application validation is pending. Missing cache entries remain a hard failure, never an automatic online retry. Review any partial profile changes after an install failure; application is not transactional.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Codex Compatibility

`@local/dsh-codex-compat` is one repository-owned bundle with two Host components: a Codex sign-in helper for Web and the terminal and optional Fast mode. Native DSH/pi-ai still owns OAuth, credentials, token refresh, provider configuration and inference. This package does not install community plugins or replace the native Codex adapter.

The bundle is opt-in and is not included in `personal-web`. Source review, build and merge do not install it. A retained-profile migration requires separate approval, backups and the repository’s [migration checks](../../MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md).

## Components and controls

| Component                       | Cordis row          | Responsibility                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@local/dsh-codex-compat/oauth` | `local-codex-oauth` | Connect Codex from the Models page or a terminal using native authorization. |
| `@local/dsh-codex-compat/fast`  | `local-codex-fast`  | Own the optional request-tier bridge, persisted choices and Fast controls.   |

DSH RC2 discovers a Client half only from a bare package Loader name. The bundle therefore mounts Fast through the package root, which exports the same Host component as `/fast`. This keeps two components and one Client module without a dummy bootstrap plugin.

The components have separate native enable/disable controls. The Fast component also has its own **Fast integration** switch, so you can remove its request modifications without unloading its recovery controls. Neither component depends on the other.

- **Composer → two-bolt Fast button:** Click to cycle **Off → Everything Fast → Main thread only → Off**. The left bolt represents the main thread; the right represents eligible Codex subagents, including nested subagents. Filled bolts indicate Fast. The tooltip names the current and next state and notes higher usage. New sessions start Off; the first click enables everything. There is no subagents-only mode.
- **Plugins → `@local/dsh-codex-compat` → `local-codex-fast` → Configure → Fast integration:** Turn the Fast integration off. Codex login and Standard inference remain available.
- **OAuth component Off:** Close this helper’s interaction, request cancellation of its attempt, and stop future automatic terminal login. An already-queued native credential write can still complete, as explained below. Reconnect Codex requires this component. Native refresh and inference remain available.
- **Fast component Off:** Unloads the request bridge and the shared browser controls, including Reconnect Codex. To turn off Fast and keep Reconnect Codex available, use the **Fast integration** switch.

## Sign-in helper

Open **Settings → Models** and select **Reconnect Codex** on the configured OpenAI Codex card. Open the sign-in link in a new tab and enter the one-time code. If OpenAI blocks device sign-in, check your ChatGPT security settings or workspace permissions. After DSH confirms the connection, retry the failed turn in the same chat. The running DSH instance saves the new grant. If sign-in is already in progress, finish it in the browser tab or terminal that started it.

The Web action uses the authenticated browser connection and starts only when clicked. The originating card can read and cancel its own attempt. Closing the card cancels the attempt when the connection is available. An abandoned attempt also expires when its tab stops checking progress. The code is held in memory until the attempt ends. The browser receives the one-time code and status only. The native flow owns the grant.

The OAuth component adapts the locally authored helper from the adjacent `dsh-sandbox` repository. It does not implement PKCE, callback listeners, device-code exchange, token refresh, credential locking or grant writes. The native authorization service and pi-ai provide those operations.

At activation, the helper checks that the native `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex` flow offers OAuth. It then starts its login task without waiting for human interaction before Web startup finishes:

1. Read credential **metadata**, not the token-bearing record.
2. If the record exists, leave it unchanged and skip login.
3. Otherwise, delegate to native `authorization.begin` for the same credential key.
4. Display native non-secret notices directly in the terminal. Prefer browser login with a TTY, or device-code login without one. Reject unexpected secret prompts.

The optional manual callback text binds both the whole interaction and native prompt signals. This matters because browser login gives manual input a separate signal. Component disposal or native attempt settlement retires the helper’s input; it does not cancel another caller’s attempt by credential key. Error output is generic and does not echo provider error bodies.

If you explicitly start DSH with `DSH_CODEX_REAUTH=1`, the enabled helper requests a replacement login even when a record exists. The helper never deletes the previous grant; the native flow owns its replacement. Ordinary validation never uses this environment variable against a live account.

**Native cancellation is not credential rollback.** In this DSH/pi-ai release, the native pi credential bridge does not forward the login signal into its queued record mutation. A replacement already queued for the native store can complete after the attempt reports `cancelled`. Do not infer that the previous grant is unchanged solely from a cancelled outcome, and do not retry automatically. This bundle neither patches that credential bridge nor handles token payloads.

The terminal action remains available for headless recovery. Both entry points delegate to the same native authorization flow.

## Provider configuration and migration

**The bundle never writes the `llm-pi-ai` provider map.** Native pi-ai registers its authorization flows independently of configured routes. Configure or enable `openai-codex` through the native Models page, and keep model lists, capacities and reasoning preferences in native user configuration.

The old sandbox bundle supplied an entire `llm-pi-ai` Config override containing `openai-codex: {}`. Copying that patch here would replace other provider configuration. This bundle deliberately omits it.

Before replacing selected legacy `@local/dsh-codex-oauth` or `@local/dsh-codex-fast` bundles:

1. Back up the profile and native credential store using the approved migration procedure. Keep backups outside Git.
2. Preserve the effective Codex provider/model configuration in the profile’s native settings. Check other providers and the selected model/reasoning effort too. A saved `models` array replaces the inherited catalog.
3. Remove the legacy bundle selections and install the reviewed compatibility bundle through the approved plugin manager procedure. Do not manually write installed package files or run a package manager in the profile.
4. Confirm both new component paths and the existing configured Codex route. An existing grant must skip login. Standard inference must remain available with Fast integration Off.

Stable component row IDs support Loader replacement, but they are not permission to install two competing implementations or rely on bundle order. Keep one selected implementation after migration. Do not delete, copy or reinterpret the credential record to rename a bundle.

The original Fast storage domain `local_codex_fast` (version 1), RPC channel, browser refresh event and isolated session-cache suffix remain unchanged. Existing integration/session choices survive the package rename. The native credential key also remains `llm-pi-ai/openai-codex`. There is no new token store or data migration.

## Fast usage, scope and recovery

Fast uses subscription limits at a higher rate. OpenAI currently documents 2.5× included subscription usage and 2× purchased-credit/Enterprise pay-as-you-go billing for supported models. These are billing multipliers, not guaranteed speed improvements. Availability depends on the model, account, workspace and rollout. See [OpenAI’s Codex speed documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/speed).

Integration Off stops new Fast requests and immediately revokes pending payload construction, even while settings writes are pending. **Payload completion commits an in-flight request:** a body finalized before Off can still be sent as Fast during later WebSocket connection setup, or continue if already sent. Off does not cancel that request or retract its higher usage. Earlier Enable completions cannot undo a later Off.

If an Off write fails, it still takes effect in this process; the page reports the error. Persist Off before restarting. While a change is unsaved, clicking the two-bolt button retries **Off** for both scopes instead of cycling to a higher-usage state. **Refresh Fast status** appears when a request fails.

The Fast component uses native schema-validated `storageDomain` storage. The main-thread choice binds to the session ID and exact provider/model and survives page reload, resume and Host restart. Selecting another model uses Standard; returning to the previously opted-in model restores its saved choice. **Everything Fast** enables eligible subagents too; **Main thread only** disables their Fast policy; **Off** disables both scopes. Subagent Fast requires the root session’s current supported model to request Fast. New top-level sessions and ordinary conversation forks start Off. Integration Off retains saved choices but makes them inactive; explicitly re-enabling it activates them again. Compaction, title, summary and hand-built model calls are excluded for parents and children.

Subagents Fast applies only to ordinary eligible Codex calls with a complete, consistent live delegation chain to the opted-in root session. Each edge must have native subagent metadata, a consistent delegation depth and a live parent Agent. DSH 0.2.2-rc.5 no longer tracks runtime parent ownership, so a resumed child whose live parent is the opted-in root also qualifies. Spawned and context-forked children, nested subagents and teammates use that boundary. Missing or replaced ancestors and unreachable out-of-process workers remain Standard. Pending payloads recheck the exact Agent identities and root policy. Selecting **Main thread only** revokes pending child Fast payloads; selecting **Off** revokes both scopes. Prepared requests retain the in-flight limitation above.

The existing version-1 storage domain gains an additive `subagents` table. Older records open unchanged and missing child choices mean Off. Previously saved subagents-only choices remain stored but inactive. No bulk rewrite or credential migration runs. Reverting to an older plugin does not preserve the new table on subsequent storage writes; back up runtime state before a retained-profile upgrade or rollback.

Only `openai-codex`, the native `openai-codex-responses` API, the built-in ChatGPT endpoint and a reviewed model allowlist qualify. The model must also exist in the configured native catalog. Gateway endpoints do not qualify merely because they use an OpenAI payload shape.

Fast controls use authenticated DSH Connection RPC. No agent tool can enable this higher-usage mode. Enable rejects stale model/revision data; Off remains available with stale revisions. The component never adds session events or changes model-visible prompts/history.

## Compatibility bridge and diagnostics

**Fast uses a version-specific workaround, not a public DSH adapter extension.** This bundle targets DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`; the bridge verifies pi-ai `1.3.0`. Unreviewed versions disable Fast without modifying Standard requests.

The Fast bridge owns:

1. Read-only discovery through DSH’s private adapter registry.
2. Reversible instance-only wrapping of `streamWithSnapshot`, then the actual captured Models collection’s `streamSimple`. This preserves prepared calls across settings snapshots and adapter replacement observed while the component is loaded.
3. Per-request `AsyncLocalStorage` binding downstream construction and iterator operations. Excluded/nested calls receive an empty scope.
4. A composed `onPayload` callback that requests `service_tier: "priority"`. This SDK’s `streamSimple` drops a direct `serviceTier` option.
5. A separate Fast WebSocket session-cache key.
6. Revocation before restoring only methods still owned by this bridge. Retained callback references become transparent when disabled. Native errors and cancellation remain intact.

The bridge does not replace provider registrations, shared prototypes, global fetch, authentication, transport choice, headers, messages or cancellation signals. A retired adapter never visible to this component cannot be instrumented retroactively. Use Fast for subsequent eligible calls, not to upgrade an already-running request during installation.

A bridge failure produces an explicit request/settings error. Turn **Fast integration Off** to return to Standard. No automatic retry silently changes a requested Fast call to Standard.

Diagnostics report **priority requested**, not server tier confirmed. pi-ai’s `onResponse` provides HTTP status/headers, not the effective tier, and is not called by its WebSocket path. DSH’s current stream drops response-tier data. Accurate account eligibility, billing, speed and server-tier acknowledgment require separately approved live verification. No billing metadata or authentication headers are spoofed.

Status refreshes on page load, window focus, or explicit error recovery. These updates are not a live server-tier feed. Provider failures remain visible through native turn errors.

## Source and development

```text
src/oauth/              terminal interaction and authenticated browser reconnect
src/fast/index.ts        Fast Host entrypoint
src/fast/runtime.ts      persisted policy and authenticated RPC
src/fast/bridge.ts       private adapter compatibility boundary
client/fast/controls.tsx composer and integration controls
client/index.ts         package-wide native slot registration
shared/contracts.ts     typed Fast RPC contracts
```

Use the repository’s pinned tooling and approved setup procedure. From the repository root:

```sh
node packages/dsh-codex-compat/scripts/build-host.mjs
node packages/dsh-codex-compat/scripts/build-client.mjs
node --test packages/dsh-codex-compat/test/*.test.js
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.browser.config.mjs packages/dsh-codex-compat/test/browser
node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test --config packages/dsh-codex-compat/test/playwright.config.mjs
```

`pnpm test` checks this package’s types and committed artifact freshness. Regenerate artifacts after changing source. `pnpm run test:visual` runs shared journeys followed by this bundle’s isolated-profile journey.

OAuth tests use native authorization/credential services with synthetic local flows and temporary records. A separate native pi flow test substitutes only the provider’s login result, holds the real store’s record lock, and proves the documented late-write cancellation limit. It does not execute the OAuth protocol. Fast tests use the installed native adapter/SDK with controlled provider, storage and transport effects. The shell journey uses fixture sign-in replies, disables the OAuth Host component in the fixture profile, and makes no inference calls. It reuses native Host/authentication/navigation helpers with configured Codex discovery/defaults that conflict with the shared unconfigured-provider profile.

Screenshots are diagnostic test-suite captures of the real isolated DSH application with fixture data, not regression baselines or deployment evidence. No ordinary test reads personal credentials, logs in to OpenAI or performs paid inference.

Community integrations informed the Fast design only: [Pi’s payload-hook extension](https://github.com/calesennett/pi-codex-fast), [DSH model modes](https://github.com/DTSFO/dsh-model-modes), and [OpenCode’s Fast aliases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/21706). No community plugin source or dependency is installed or vendored. Runtime dependencies reuse existing DSH packages and Node built-ins.

# DSH customizations

This private repository keeps DSH plugin bundles and reproducible profile recipes for one user across several computers. Clone it on each computer, then apply the profiles you need. DSH keeps credentials, sessions, settings, and other runtime state outside this repository.

The plugins target DSH **`0.2.2-rc.5` only**. Existing consumers can stay on their previous commit until their host operator upgrades the runtime and plugin graph together. **Full validation pending.** The published target still requires the RPC-owner patch; its ownership regression fails without the patch and passes with it. See the [migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md) for scope, evidence gaps, retained-state cautions, and deployment boundaries.

## Prerequisites

Install these tools before you use the repository:

- The checkout-local, patched DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` launcher installed by the frozen dependency command below (a global DSH installation is not upgraded or used by `apply`)
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- pnpm 11.9.0, already available locally (not an unverified downloader shim)

Before dependency work in any checkout or worktree, follow the [repository setup skill](.agents/skills/repository-setup/SKILL.md). It covers dependency ownership, pinned executable availability, offline cache limitations, and approval boundaries. You can read this Markdown directly without a plugin.

Set `DSH_HOME` before applying a profile if your Harness home is not `~/.dsh`.

### Amp orbs

The executable `.agents/setup` prepares fresh Amp orbs with Node.js 24.20.0 (matching CI), the manifest-pinned pnpm, frozen workspace dependencies, and the matching Playwright Chromium and system dependencies. It checks the repository and builds Session Environment. Node downloads are checksum-verified; toolchains stay under `~/.local/share/dsh-customizations-orb`, and a checkout-scoped login-shell hook makes them available to agents and supervised services.

Network provisioning is approved for this orb lifecycle script only. Dependency lifecycle scripts remain disabled; the release-age policy and required DSH patch remain enforced. Normal agent dependency work still follows the offline-first setup procedure above. Setup refuses symlinked dependency directories and never applies a profile, authenticates a user, or starts a persistent DSH host.

Amp snapshots successful setup for reuse by fresh project orbs. Exact snapshots skip setup; stale snapshots retain installed tools and caches while setup reconciles the current lockfile. Warm setup skips existing toolchain/browser downloads and checks system packages before invoking apt. `.agents/resume` only checks readiness and never reinstalls dependencies. These files must reach the project's default branch before future orbs can use them. The browser is suitable for interaction tests; an x64 orb is not the Linux ARM64 container used for visual baselines.

## Apply the starter profile

Before applying to retained state, complete target validation and the [host operator acceptance steps](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md#host-operator-acceptance-sequence), including backups and explicit deployment approval. The commands below are a procedure, not a report of a completed `0.2.2-rc.5` install or deployment.

The `personal-web` recipe selects the standard DSH base and Web bundles plus [Global Guidance](packages/dsh-global-guidance/README.md), [Session Environment](packages/dsh-session-environment/README.md), [OpenRouter](packages/dsh-openrouter/README.md), [Jev](packages/dsh-jev/README.md), [File Intuition](packages/dsh-file-intuition/README.md), [Session Recap](packages/dsh-session-recap/README.md), [Project Steward](packages/dsh-project-steward/README.md), [Product mode](packages/dsh-product-mode/README.md), [Dispatch](packages/dsh-dispatch/README.md), [Firecrawl](packages/dsh-web-firecrawl/README.md), [Google auth](packages/dsh-google-auth/README.md), [Google Drive](packages/dsh-google-drive/README.md), [GitHub](packages/dsh-github/README.md), [Linear](packages/dsh-linear/README.md), [Projects](packages/dsh-projects/README.md), [YouTube](packages/dsh-tool-youtube/README.md), [Image generation](packages/dsh-tool-imagegen/README.md), [Trivy](packages/dsh-tool-trivy/README.md), and [Browser recording](packages/dsh-browser-recording/README.md), targeting DSH `0.2.2-rc.5`. Configure the recap model and Firecrawl key through **Plugins → installed package → Configure** on the corresponding plugin row. Firecrawl replaces the profile's search/fetch providers; it requires a key before either web tool can run. Browser recording requires preinstalled browser/media tools in the subprocess execution environment and never records without an explicit user request.

Existing installations need a coordinated DSH and plugin upgrade, not a plugin-only restart on the old runtime. The host operator owns backups, legacy settings adoption, profile composition, and restart. No intermediate plugin release is required. After the upgrade, key changes take effect on the next request without a restart. Keys stay in DSH's credential store (or the launching environment), never in this repository.

1. After the setup procedure's ownership, executable, cache, and approval checks, install dependencies, validate the repository, and build Session Environment. If the offline install fails, stop; obtain separate approval for cache population rather than retrying online:

   ```sh
   pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
   pnpm run check
   pnpm run build
   ```

2. Preview the commands without changing DSH:

   ```sh
   pnpm run apply -- personal-web --dry-run
   ```

3. Apply and validate the profile:

   ```sh
   pnpm run apply -- personal-web
   ```

4. Start it:

   ```sh
   ./node_modules/.bin/dsh --profile personal-web
   ```

The apply command submits the selected bundles together in recipe order, using `file:` snapshots for local bundles. It does not remove bundles already installed but absent from the recipe. Existing bundle order is retained by DSH; inspect `--dump-config` after updates.

**Required RPC-owner compatibility patch:** the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection@0.2.2-rc.5` still needs [`dsh-client-connection-0.2.2-rc.5-rpc-owner.patch`](patches/dsh-client-connection-0.2.2-rc.5-rpc-owner.patch), which normalizes the consumer context with `getTraceable(this.ctx, this.ctx)`. The ownership regression fails against the unpatched target and passes with the patch; the installed target launcher graph also passes. Keep the target-version patch, pnpm 11 `patchedDependencies` in the [workspace policy](pnpm-workspace.yaml), and [lockfile](pnpm-lock.yaml) synchronized. See the [current migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md#required-rpc-owner-patch) for evidence and limitations.

The apply procedure verifies the checkout-local launcher and the required Connection implementation before writing a profile. The patch must reach each independent profile graph as well as the launcher graph. Preserve workspace YAML settings with a `.bak` backup, use exact target-version pins and narrow release-age exceptions, and resolve the complete profile graph offline with lifecycle scripts disabled. Refuse conflicting overrides and verify the profile's own Web/Connection resolution after the frozen install. Target-version application validation is pending. Missing cache entries remain a hard failure, never an automatic online retry. Review any partial profile changes after an install failure; application is not transactional.

Other launchers, including global `dsh`, are deliberately unsupported by `apply`; `DSH_BIN` may only name this checkout's `node_modules/.bin/dsh`. Keep this checkout at a durable path when using its launcher. No global package, running process, credentials, or history is modified automatically. Restart through your usual service mechanism only after explicitly selecting the verified target launcher. If published-artifact verification confirms the patch is required, carry it in a separately managed launcher's independent dependency graph and validate that graph separately. See the [0.2.2-rc.5 migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md), including existing settings, preset, and history cautions.

The repository-owned `@local/dsh-worktree` bundle and **Worktree coordinator** preset are retired in favor of DSH's native worktree implementation. Session Environment adds an optional, remembered per-session **Worktree** preference that guides agents to use DSH's supplied native tools lazily. The `personal-web` recipe selects DSH's shipped **Git Worktrees** bundle for its native service and `create_worktree` tool. The preference does not enforce isolation, and no old coordinator state is migrated. Updating the recipe does not uninstall the old bundle from existing profiles. Before removing it from a retained profile, review saved sessions and defaults that reference `worktree-coordinator`; those sessions need its declaration to mount. Profile changes require separate approval. Existing Git worktrees and their file changes remain untouched.

Project Steward bundles a separate **Project Steward** preset for repository setup and guidance audits. It retains Standard's tools, proposes changes before writing, and carries optional versioned templates. Each custom preset contributes an additive declaration with a stable ID. The personal-web profile selects Standard as its default; it does not replace a directory roster. Inspect [Project Steward's installation prerequisites](packages/dsh-project-steward/README.md#install-and-select) for duplicate IDs and saved-default handling. Selecting it performs no setup writes or installs.

[Product mode](packages/dsh-product-mode/README.md) adds a planning preset and bundled `product-planning` skill. It clarifies an initiative, inspects the codebase and existing GitHub work, refines project text and agent-ready issues conversationally, and publishes through the shared GitHub tools with individual write approvals. It keeps drafts in the conversation and adds no automatic dispatch, persistent project/session mapping, or custom UI. Select **Product mode** for a new session after an approved profile update and restart; DSH locks preset selection once a session starts. Product mode is separate from the built-in plan-mode switch and respects its restrictions. Standard remains the default. Before installation, check for a duplicate `product-mode` declaration ID. Duplicate IDs fail closed; convert any retained directory-based presets to explicit declarations.

Each coordinator conversation has three occupied worker slots and at most five queued assignments. Ordinary creation and new assignments need no individual Dispatch approval card; adoption of an existing session still requires your consent. This version includes no Gmail/GCP tools, general Drive file mutations, or `gws`

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Dispatch

Dispatch is a Host/Client bundle for DSH `0.2.2-rc.5` with two additive agent presets:

| Preset          | ID                | Role                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dispatch        | `dispatch`        | Coordinates ordinary worker sessions through a restricted toolset. Has no shell or file tools and does no coding itself.                              |
| Dispatch Worker | `dispatch-worker` | Pinned Standard coding composition plus worker guidance and `dispatch_report`, without native delegation. The only preset Dispatch creates or adopts. |

Workers are ordinary workspace sessions, not native subagents. Their relationship to a coordinator is plugin-owned metadata in DSH's plugin storage domain. Selecting a preset starts nothing, and Standard and any saved default preset or model are unchanged.

## Workflow

1. Select **Dispatch** for a new session and describe the work.
2. Dispatch calls `dispatch_refresh_base` to fetch one configured remote branch and pin its commit. Fetching updates only the remote-tracking ref; no checkout is pulled, reset, or changed.
3. `dispatch_create_session` submits the exact prompt, model, branch and pinned base to this conversation's pool. The fixed limits are **3 occupied worker slots and 5 queued assignments**. Ordinary creation and new assignments need no individual Dispatch approval card. This is a bounded admission policy, not semantic authorization for a task or approval of the worker's sensitive operations.
4. A submission returns `executing` or `queued`. Queued entries persist the exact assignment and execution identity, but create no native session, branch or worktree until admission. A full queue returns `queue-full` without accepting more work. Cancellation before durable admission accepts nothing; cancellation after admission does not erase an accepted assignment. Do not retry until capacity changes. Ordinary queued work drains in admission order.
5. An admitted creation makes an ordinary `dispatch-worker` session, sets its native title and session-local model, attaches it to a matching existing workspace when available, and creates its own linked worktree at the pinned commit. Dispatch verifies Git registration and the effective directory before delivering the exact prompt as a coordinator-attributed message.
6. Workers report through `dispatch_report`, naming their current assignment. Follow-ups use `dispatch_send_message` with that assignment ID. For separate work, use `newAssignment: true` and the explicitly targeted owned idle worker. Dispatch does not automatically match new creation requests to old sessions. A successful new assignment replaces the previous one; a failed pre-delivery attempt does not reopen or replace old authority.

Runtime idle is not completion. Unfinished, input-waiting and ready-for-review assignments occupy slots. Automatic capacity retirement requires explicit `done` or `failed`, one-way assignment closure, and a true native idle reservation with no queued input. Sessions and checkouts remain retained after retirement. An explicit quiescent management release preserves the existing cancellation/closure behavior; it never deletes native artifacts.

**Adoption still needs consent.** `dispatch_add_session` prepares an exact adoption card below the completed coordinator response. The owner can approve or reject it once. Approval does not bypass pool capacity: the adoption executes, queues, or remains pending with a full-queue error. Adoption and new assignments retain the exact reviewed checkout/commit and reject drift at execution. Another coordinator's session cannot be adopted.

### Persistent activity

A compact header pill follows the current Dispatch coordinator, even when tool history is collapsed. It shows occupied workers, active runtime work, and queued assignments. Idle unfinished work appears as waiting, not computing. The quiet idle state has no animation; short visual transitions respect reduced motion. Loading, transport errors and disconnects show unknown/unavailable activity instead of false zero or stale live counts.

The pill reads real coordinator-scoped dispatcher state every two seconds, one request at a time, and subscribes to native connection state. Runtime lookup uses the native live-Agent registry; it does not resume dormant workers just to count them. Missing runtime stays unknown while durable occupancy remains visible. It never interprets model text. When native workspace navigation is available, activating it opens the first listed occupied worker; the tooltip identifies that worker. Detailed existing **Dispatch workers** tool cards still offer per-worker navigation and checkout/report details. There is no new dashboard, management menu or queue editor.

New workers join an existing native workspace whose canonical directory matches the repository root. Worktrees change their effective directory, not workspace membership. Without a matching workspace, they remain ungrouped. Dispatch does not create workspaces, rename adopted sessions, or change the saved default model.

### Sidebar roles

Session rows show **D** for the `dispatch` coordinator preset and **W** for `dispatch-worker`. Hover a row to see its full role and preset ID. Native row actions hide the trailing marker while the row is hovered or focused; activity indicators, pin markers, menus, navigation, and titles stay unchanged.

These are display hints from the native session list's last-known preset metadata, not proof of assignment, ownership, or activity. Missing, regular, and unrecognized presets stay unmarked. Reading a role does not bind, retain, or wake the session and makes no Dispatch RPC call.

## Authority and isolation

- **User-only adoption decisions.** The card decides through the `/local-dispatch` Connection RPC channel. Connection authenticates the signed browser credential (or an API credential) and the handler accepts only the `owner` principal. The browser sends only the proposal identity, its digest, and the decision, never a prompt, model, or target. There is no agent-callable consent or ownership tool. Pool admission is a separate, narrow Dispatch policy; ordinary sensitive-operation policies cannot approve adoption.
- **Exact binding.** A decision must match the coordinator session, tool call, proposal ID, SHA-256 digest of the frozen payload (including the reviewed adoption checkout), the current ownership generation, and the current Host lifetime. Changed adoption payloads need new consent. Undecided consent expires on restart. Accepted queued entries retain their exact payload across restarts; interrupted native effects are not replayed.
- **Exclusive ownership.** Claims are serialized across every coordinator in the Host, keyed by worker session and by the checkout's filesystem-provider identity and key. Another coordinator's worker cannot be read, messaged, or adopted. Release (`dispatch_remove_session`) keeps the session, history, branch, and checkout and closes the open assignment.
- **Serialized ownership.** Targeted operations and report delivery check ownership in the same serialized admission as their effect. Claims and release take the same lock. **Interrupt** aborts the active turn and, like DSH's own cancel command, keeps queued and steering input.
- **Native idle reservation.** Creation, adoption, new assignments, and live release use `Agent.runMaintenance()` to reserve native activity across inspection and storage writes. Normal worker turns cannot run during that reservation. Creation keeps its native directory-change notice for the first turn and checks the actual created directory before enqueue; it does not permit human input. UI input can still queue; assignment admission checks both inboxes and cancellation before delivery. If input arrives before delivery, Dispatch restores the previous worker record in one write. If restoration fails, admission remains pending and grants no work.
- **One worker/task record.** The worker record contains its current assignment. A pending assignment reserves ownership but permits no coding tools, follow-ups, or reports. Dispatch confirms admission only after enqueue succeeds. Enqueue and storage are not one atomic operation: an uncertain confirmation remains pending and is never replayed automatically.
- **Assignment closure.** Whether an assignment accepts follow-ups and reports is a one-way closure, separate from the displayed work state. A `done` or `failed` report or administrative status, release, or a successfully admitted new assignment closes it; nothing reopens it, and a closed assignment's state cannot be edited. Reports must name the current assignment, so a late report from an earlier task cannot complete a later one.
- **Linked worktrees only.** Every managed worker must be on its own registered linked worktree. The main checkout never qualifies. Every targeted operation re-inspects Git and the worker's effective directory; a worker that leaves its checkout loses Dispatch admission until it returns.
- **Managed execution world.** Repository inspection and `dispatch_refresh_base` run Git through DSH's `subprocess`, `sandbox`, `sandboxPolicy`, and `fs` services, confined under the calling Session's sandbox policy (the coordinator for fetches and new branches, the worker for its checkout), with paths canonicalized by the mounted filesystem provider. Dispatch uses no Host `child_process` or filesystem calls for repository work.
- **Session-local models.** The exact submitted worker model is selected on the worker's own Agent after the session controller's availability checks. DSH's saved default model is never changed.
- **Coordinator tool restriction.** The coordinator preset registers its tools and a monotonic execution guard that denies every other tool name, including nested calls. On `agent/created`, each coordinator Agent gets a live allowlist in its own scope, so Host-wide tools such as GitHub or File Intuition, and globals registered later, are not visible.
- **Worker restrictions.** Dispatch creates and adopts only `dispatch-worker` sessions. Admission checks the native current-preset projection, not just the creation-time header, before enqueueing the assignment. Dispatch Worker omits Standard's delegation group (subagents, forks, workflows) and plugin-manager tools, and its guard denies Agent Teams tools, Ralph, and coordinator tools. Pending admission denies all tools. Normal admitted work keeps coding, inspection, tests, and background jobs.
- **Reports are data.** A report is bound to the executing worker's own association; there is no caller-supplied recipient or identity. Reports and follow-ups are never treated as user approval, and a draft pull request request does not bypass the worker's normal approvals. Nothing is merged, deleted, or deployed automatically.
- **Shared environment.** Worktrees isolate checkouts only. Databases, ports, credentials, external services, and the execution environment are shared. Guidance and tool guards are not a sandbox against malicious code.

## Tools

Coordinator: `dispatch_list_workspaces`, `dispatch_list_presets`, `dispatch_list_sessions`, `dispatch_find_sessions`, `dispatch_create_session`, `dispatch_send_message`, `dispatch_get_session_status`, `dispatch_read_session`, `dispatch_wait_session`, `dispatch_interrupt_session`, `dispatch_update_session`, `dispatch_add_session`, `dispatch_remove_session`, `dispatch_refresh_base`, plus `ask_user_question`, `todo_write`, and `skill`.

Worker: Standard coding tools plus `dispatch_report`.

## Retained state and recovery

The `local_dispatch` storage domain holds proposals with their checkpoints, workers with their current assignment, and reports. Proposals retain assignment intent and prompts; reports retain their assignment IDs. Dispatch fails to start if the domain cannot be opened; it never falls back to memory. The additive queue, ordering and capacity fields retain schema v3 compatibility with prior v3 records. This prerelease still refuses retained v2 state rather than resetting it. No v2 migration is included. Preserve any earlier draft state before arranging a migration; do not delete or rename the domain to bypass the refusal.

On Host start, undecided adoption proposals expire and interrupted executions become `uncertain`. Queued entries survive and drain only for their retained coordinator identity when dependencies and capacity are available. Executing/uncertain provisioning reserves capacity, including before a worker record exists. A later explicit ownership claim supersedes that old reservation rather than leaving a second permanent slot. A requested native session identity is durable before creation; recovery resolves that identity after a lost response instead of issuing another create. Uncertain effects and pending assignment deliveries are never replayed. Pending reports are retried, but pending assignments are not. A report keeps the same message ID and text across attempts. Each attempt checks the coordinator's live inbox, durable `agent/inbox/spliced` insertions, and committed messages before enqueueing. Identity allocation, ownership validation, deduplication, enqueue, and confirmation share one serialized admission with release and other delivery attempts.

Shutdown refuses new submissions, decisions and reports, preserves queued entries, drains admitted executions and deliveries, and closes storage even if expiring a proposal fails. A native session or worktree identity is retained in the execution diagnostic if its first checkpoint write fails. If the diagnostic write also fails, Dispatch logs the known identities and reports no confirmed success. Native effects and plugin storage are not one transaction; failures retain artifacts for inspection instead of attempting an automatic replay. Dispatch never deletes sessions, branches, or worktrees.

## Installation

Dispatch is in the `personal-web` recipe. Installing it, applying the profile, and restarting DSH require separate explicit approval. Before installation, check for duplicate `dispatch` or `dispatch-worker` preset IDs.

Dispatch admits workers only when the Git Worktrees plugin's `retainOnArchive` is `true`. DSH's default (`false`) reclaims a clean, unreferenced checkout when the session that created it is archived, so until it is set, submitting or executing a create or adoption fails with that instruction.

## Target contracts (DSH 0.2.2-rc.5)

| Contract            | Evidence and adapter                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ordinary sessions   | `ctx.sessionController.create({ sessionId, cwd, agentPreset })` and `resolveAgent()` (`dsh-api-session-controller`). Worker models use `Agent.model.select()` after `ctx.llm` checks; `sessionController.selectModel()` is avoided because it also saves the default.                                                                  |
| Workspace and title | After checkpointing the native session ID, `workspaceRegistry.list()` selects an existing canonical repository match and `Workspace.attachSession()` validates header-based membership. `sessionController.rename()` sanitizes and persists the exact intent as the native title.                                                      |
| Header activity     | Additive session-scoped `conversation.session.header.utilities` list, ascending order, native `useProjection('agentPreset')` hook and `uiWorkspace.openSession()`. Returning null hides only Dispatch; scope disposal removes the registration. Verified against matching installed source and a minimal generated-bundle shell smoke. |
| Connection state    | Native `connection.state.getSnapshot/subscribe` reports connected/connecting/disconnected; React cancels reads on identity changes, disconnect and disposal.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Adoption approvals  | The additive `conversation.chat.turnTail` list is the sole adoption-consent surface. It renders settled proposals from the native per-turn tool source after `turn/end`; native tool output stays read-only.                                                                                                                           |
| Attributed delivery | `agent.followup()` / `agent.steer()` with the `agent-message` source (`kind`, `form: 'relay'`, `senderSessionId`) that `dsh-subagent` registers. The message is built like `createUserMessage` without a runtime dependency.                                                                                                           |
| Tool restriction    | `tools.restrict({ allow })` in each coordinator Agent's scope and `tools.guard()` in the preset scope (`dsh-tools`). A preset-scope restriction would also hide the preset's own tools from its Agents, which `test/preset.test.js` guards against.                                                                                    |
| User-only approval  | Connection RPC handlers receive the authenticated Peer; only `principal.kind === 'owner'` may decide (`dsh-client-connection`). The native `approval/request` waterfall is not used: any composed answerer may grant it and it carries no principal.                                                                                   |
| Native worktrees    | `ctx.worktrees.create(workerAgent, { name, from })` changes only the worker's directory (`dsh-experimental-worktree`); `ctx.workingDirectory.get(session)` reads the effective directory; `worktrees.config.retainOnArchive` is checked before admission.                                                                              |
| Managed Git         | `ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable/spawn`, `ctx.sandbox.confine` under `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve({ session })`, and `ctx.fs.resolve/processPath`, mirroring the Git Worktrees runner (`dsh-subprocess`, `dsh-sandbox`, `dsh-sandbox-policy`, `dsh-fs`).                                                                                |
| Inbox identity      | `Agent.inbox.nextTurn/nextStep` and the `agent/inbox/spliced` event's `inserted` messages (`dsh-agent`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Durable records     | `ctx.storageDomain.open()` with structural `parse`/`safeParse` validators (`dsh-storage-domain`); no custom session event types.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Known limitations

- Tools that another plugin registers directly in a coordinator Agent's own scope (for example, a session toggle) stay visible to the model, because rc.3 exempts an Agent's own registrations from `restrict()`. The execution guard still denies them.
- Any `owner`-principal Connection client can decide, including an API client holding the user's credential. Code in the shared execution environment that obtains that credential is out of scope.
- Creation and adoption are limited to `dispatch-worker` sessions. Other presets cannot carry the worker guard or `dispatch_report`, so they are refused rather than run unrestricted. Do not change a worker's preset while admission is executing. Dispatch checks the recorded native selection; it does not make concurrent native preset recomposition atomic.
- `dispatch_refresh_base` fetches under the coordinator Session's sandbox policy, so a policy that forbids writing the repository's Git directory or network access makes the refresh fail rather than bypassing it.
- Checkout identity uses the filesystem provider's class name and opaque target key. Moving a Host to a different filesystem provider makes existing claims ineligible until released.
- Reports are queued on the coordinator's inbox without extra coalescing. Recovery recognizes an already admitted copy; it is not exactly-once delivery in general.
- The real-shell journey drives real agent loops with a scripted model route. It proves wiring, attribution, and page reload, not how a real model plans or reports. It covers bounded creation, persistent chrome, native navigation, disconnect and reload. Adoption consent and new-assignment safety are owned by `test/service.test.js`; component variations are owned by the browser tests.
- DSH 0.2.2-rc.5 persona templates know only `{{provider}}` and `{{model}}`; any other variable fails the first turn. The personas therefore do not name the working directory, which DSH's runtime context already gives the model.
- Adoption status refreshes poll every 2 seconds while pending, queued or executing. The activity pill polls while mounted and connected. An unavailable worker runtime leaves activity unknown, not zero. Uncertain provisioning may retain a slot until its outcome is investigated; the queue never bypasses it.

## Development

From the repository root, with the verified pnpm 11.9.0 and installed dependencies:

```sh
node packages/dsh-dispatch/scripts/build-host.mjs        # dist/ (checked TypeScript)
node packages/dsh-dispatch/scripts/build-client.mjs      # client.js (type-checked first)
env -u NODE_PATH node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/dsh-dispatch/test/*.test.js
# One command at a time; no downloads or provider calls.
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.browser.config.mjs packages/dsh-dispatch/test/browser --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test --config packages/dsh-dispatch/test/playwright.config.mjs --workers=1 --output=artifacts/dispatch-local
```

`test/service.test.js` owns admission, queue/backpressure, lifecycle, JSON-domain restart, uncertain identity recovery, ownership, adoption consent, exact assignment binding and cancellation. It uses native in-process Agents and temporary Git repositories; simultaneous submissions do not spawn multiple DSH processes or call providers. `test/world.test.js` owns managed Git-world integration. `test/preset.test.js` owns real Loader/tool restrictions and storage schema compatibility. The browser files own React behavior, including unknown/error/disconnect states, navigation, focus, polling cancellation and scope disposal.

The single `test/shell/journey.spec.mjs` uses the existing disposable shell and generated bundle. Its scripted model submits six assignments: three occupied workers report ready-for-review and three remain queued. It checks native registration, persistent counts outside collapsed history, keyboard navigation, reload and connection recovery, then captures light/wide and dark/narrow diagnostic images. These are synthetic fixture data, not deployed changes or visual-regression baselines. Host restart recovery is covered at the real JSON-domain owner boundary, not a full process-restart browser journey.

After the shared 8 GiB/no-swap sandbox OOM incident, validation for this change stays focused and sequential: Node files use `--test-concurrency=1`, affected browser files use `--maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism`, and the Dispatch shell uses `--workers=1` with unique artifacts. Required Environment builds run sequentially before the shell. Observe memory and verify attributed child teardown; do not automatically retry an uncertain or killed run. No broad root suites or baseline updates are required for this task's evidence.

# DSH customizations

This private repository keeps DSH plugin bundles and reproducible profile recipes for one user across several computers. Clone it on each computer, then apply the profiles you need. DSH keeps credentials, sessions, settings, and other runtime state outside this repository.

The plugins target DSH **`0.2.2-rc.5` only**. Existing consumers can stay on their previous commit until their host operator upgrades the runtime and plugin graph together. **Full validation pending.** The published target still requires the RPC-owner patch; its ownership regression fails without the patch and passes with it. See the [migration handoff](MIGRATION-0.2.2-rc.5.md) for scope, evidence gaps, retained-state cautions, and deployment boundaries.

## Prerequisites
